title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference 8.24.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: You you were talking after the game about figuring out your practice schedule and and getting into the right place. Now you come to a week where it's like you have this practice and then you're jumping on a plane and and moving. Does that make it difficult to kind of figure that stuff out? >> Yeah, it is what it is though. I mean it's it's stuff we can't totally control. Shorter week last week. You know, the pro side of it is we got four good days in last week. The downside of it is we're only going to get two days in this week. We got to we'll practice today. You know, we don't go three days in a row until in season, but the in season is so modified. So tomorrow will be you know, more of a jog through meeting type deal and then then obviously a big one versus Green Bay on Wednesday. >> Did you hear what your brother said today? >> I did. I was just made aware. I didn't see it until about two minutes ago. So no comment. >> You're not going to play him on 50? >> We'll see what happens. >> You put yourself in that one if it if it came to that. >> What is that thing I know you've coached against and you've been on opposite sidelines a lot. What is it going to be like being you know, head coaches on opposite sidelines? And like especially a joint practice setting where there's so much communication between bad coaches in terms of how this is going to go. >> In terms of the practice yeah, 100% like you got to be on the same page. So it's easier I would say to be on the the the same page with your brother who you talk to about five times a day anyway. So that's been that's been really good. Being able to you know, have access to you know, his main assistants and stuff like that cuz cuz you know him so well. So the communication there is great. You you do want to you want to send the same message to both teams. I mean let's call it what it is. These joint practices like I mean flip a coin on what can happen sometimes. And we we know and obviously we know the ramifications now from what the league can do as well. So I do think that'll change some people's opinions on on how you know, what the code of conduct should be. So but it's been good on the same page on how we're going to conduct this thing. And and the main thing is you got to go we're just going in to get work. Like and and no no doubt it's a more amped up environment because you're going up against a different opponent. I think it's it's time for our guys to hit somebody else. You know, so it'll be good. >> You said last week that coaches were calling you the day you were hired to set up the joint practices. When did you guys set this up? Was this something like you would always talked about like hey if this ever happens? >> Well, like I think I told you guys when this first came out like I mean if if we could have gone to Seattle to go against them it'd be great. Well, they're in our division so we're not going to Seattle. There's no team in Canada yet and I you know, you'd rather not go all the way out to Buffalo just from a travel standpoint. So you think about kind of that next closest team to to get you out of the heat. It really is Green Bay. You had Minnesota and I'll be honest I mean that was one of the teams I was talking to right away and about 12 hours after I got hired they were already filled up, you know, and so I mean that's like I said I'm not lying in terms of how fast those things go. >> You talked about you know, you guys got to get to work in here. You know, just talk about the value of these joint practices. It's almost like an extra preseason game when you you go out to work. >> It is. I mean there's you know, outside of obviously you know, tackling to the ground because of that amped up level. Again, I people smarter than me but we we all love the joint practices. Maybe some of the players I you know, they got different opinions on it and stuff. For the most part not trying to speak for them. For the most part I think they like it because again they get to go against someone else. Like I think our receivers are getting sick of running the same routes over and over and over versus our corners, you know, and we don't want to just turn into a double move fest every single day and in practice just to try to win practice. We want to get you know, sharpened at the stuff that we're going to do more than we're not. So from that that standpoint ends up being good and again like I was kind of saying with the science aspect of it like there is something to be said about the teams that are in these joint practices and in the lower percentage of injury in those first I think it is four to six games. >> How was the [snorts] Jeremiah >> What's up? >> update on Jeremiah? >> He's doing well, progressing well and uh kind of in the next phase of it. >> How was uh Carson's throwing session and then what's the plan for him? >> Uh, good with the uh throwing session. Um, still TBD in terms of, you know, what this uh I guess we play Friday, this Friday will look like. >> So, is there a chance that um well, I guess he only went through one practice this week, but I guess what do you think that Jeremiah can can get back on the field in this next kind of >> No, he he Yeah, he will not be on the field doing any sort of practice or anything like that right now. >> [snorts] >> When it comes to Carson, you said you said you would tell us his your plan for him this season at some point later on, but with him missing kind of >> In terms of his development, yeah. Yeah. >> So, in terms of that though, in terms missing all the on-field practice time because of his injury and then being having limited reps going forward, how does that affect kind of his development now? >> Uh, that that that's I mean, it's easy to magnify the quarterback position and a rookie and all that kind of stuff, but that Yeah, like you get better at football by practicing and playing football. And so, when you're not out there, it's it's hard to to to get better, right? Um, so, you know, he's missed some days, but that's no different than the the the nose guard. That's no different than the receiver. That's no different than the the left tackle, particularly for the younger guys. So, um it is what it is. Like I mean, injuries are part of this thing and uh you know, he um he's a tough dude. Like I said, I mean, he battled through it for three or four practices before it became so the discomfort became so real that it just wasn't worth it to because it wasn't going to improve until we gave him a little bit of time, so. >> Looking back how quickly he can get on the field during the season if needed. >> Uh, that's that I mean, that's the hypothetical question right now. I couldn't even answer, so. >> You obviously six days from from roster cut down. I'm just curious like how those decisions work between you and then Monty and the rest of the front office. Like what is is that entirely their decision? And I imagine it's not entirely your decision. How how does that kind of balance out? >> Yeah, it's uh it it's what you just said. That's the word I was going to use. It's just collaboration, which is everything I felt since February 1st or whenever I got hired. The communication collaboration has been great and want to make sure that, you know, we're we're building what we believe is the best 53 man roster for September 13th and for the future. Because there's, you know, those are some things that I'll be real. I guess coaches were were so focused on like today. Like I don't even care about the Green Bay practice. Obviously, you got to put, you know, thought into the Chargers and stuff like that. You go to money and me and that side like they're thinking big picture, too. And that's the the smart way of thinking cuz we're so like this and so that that those are all those conversations that are to be had and and are being had right now. >> Is that in your experience kind of where where coaching staffs and front offices often disagrees where coaching staff might be like, well, we need this guy. We want this guy. >> Yeah, I mean and and again disagreed not not in bad terms though, right? Like just hey, this this is what our thought process is, but let me hear yours and yeah, I mean that's that's every single building and those are healthy conversation for sure. >> How is the How's Robin's situation? >> Who's? >> Robin. >> So he will He's got a little bit of a rib issue, too. I mean he he hit him pretty good right there. So just kind of talked about in our team meeting about you know, what's legal, what's not legal, stuff like that and and the targets and all that kind of stuff, but he'll be he'll be I guess you could say more day-to-day and we'll we'll kind of evaluate it every single day. >> Was that was that a defenseless flag? Is that what cuz it didn't look like he got him upstairs. >> It's yeah, I mean it's it it's You got to do whatever you can to to stay away from the head point-blank period. And so even when a you know, a receiver ineligible is bracing and he's lowering his target, you got to lower your target even more. And I don't envy the situation that, you know, the defensive players are put in. I don't envy the situation that the referees are put in right there. So those are going to be bang-bang and I watched about a hundred of them today from ones that were called and ones that weren't and you I mean you're talking millimeters, you're talking inches, you're talking milliseconds in terms of the difference between a call and a non-call. It's It's not easy. >> What's Trey Lance's timeline looking like? >> Um again, we're just taking it one day at a time with with Trey right now. So, that's and truly, that's all I got for you with that. >> What role do you think he can have to start the year on on IR? >> We'll kind of have a probably a better understanding of that, I would say, after we get out of this game. >> Talking about the cuts later on in the week, talked to some of the veteran guys, they've said that they're past that stage where they're counting numbers and things of that nature like they might have been earlier in their careers. Knowing that you do have a lot of young guys still on this roster that are on that bubble spot, do you send the message to anybody to be like, "Hey, like what we're saying like we're focused on this. You can't be counting the numbers at this stage" or >> No, I mean, yeah, there there is the human element, you know, and um I I wouldn't say I mean, I'm not openly talking about it right now because again, we're going to be where our feet are, but ultimately, I mean, that's these guys' jobs, and uh there's 53 that are going to stay. There's, you know, the amount of uh practice squad guys. I'm not going to say the number cuz I don't have it off the top of my head. Whatever it is now, 12, 14, whatever it is. And so, you think now, just do the math in terms of how many guys are not going to be here. And you hope that every single guy that that uh is not an Arizona Cardinal gets picked up somewhere. You just hope. And some will, but some won't. And uh you know, so it's a There is the human element, but again, it's what we all signed up for. Um you know, the the players understand it. We understand, you know, from a coaching perspective, you know, it's it's a it's results-based, uh but we can't live in a results-based world. We got to define success in in terms of, you know, what we believe success is that week. >> Any updates on Blake Gillikin? >> Uh yeah, he's he's good. Um it's We're going to keep him out this week, but we're not worried about anything long-term. I mean, there's there's no point in in, you know, punting him this week for >> Like I was watching Jacoby on the sideline the other night, and the people that he the number of players that he goes around and talks to just during the game, during timeouts is pretty impressive. What do you think makes him such an effective leader? >> Yeah, I think he's uh authentically himself. I think he's just a really cool dude. Um so Jacoby's not trying to be something that he's not in my time with him. I I've I think I've told you guys I've I've never met Jacoby up until obviously I got here, but but I mean he'd been a lot of different places, so I have a lot of different uh you know, coaches, uh front office, players that have been with him and everyone says the same things, you know, uh not to put people's business up, but my brother's uh one of his main assistants is like one of his best friends and like I mean they're like lifelong buddies, you know, and so he was stoked when everything got done here just like I was. Um so it's it's just who he is and um you know, and and the players see that. >> B.J. Hill is obviously less than 12 months removed from coming back from a very serious knee injury. What have you seen from him this camp and preseason? >> Yeah, it's you know, it's it's unfortunate in terms of of what that injury did to him and how much time uh he missed, but uh I know this about B.J. He takes it one day at a time and he's going he's going at it one day at a time. I know he he's he feels better uh every single day that he's out there and it's it's like I say with a lot of these guys that haven't played a lot of football recently, time on task value received. Just keep going. Just keep punching away at it every single day. Keep the right mindset. Uh it's unfortunate, but that's his story right now in terms of the injury and the and the amount of uh missed time, but he's made of the right stuff and he'll figure it out. >> How often do you meet [snorts] with Monty whether informally or formally? Is it daily? Is it every other day to talk about the roster and stuff like >> You know, what's great about Monty amongst a lot of things like it's it can just organically happen whether be a phone call yesterday for however many minutes or or within passing or it's not like it's like hey at 11:00 we have to, you know, it's whenever we can find time to uh to to make sure we're chatting and stuff like that and uh that's kind of like how I like to roll, too, so. >> Is there usually something every day to touch on them? >> Uh sometimes maybe just talking to talk, but but but also just making sure that, you know, from my vantage point, hey, here's some here's some things that came across my desk. Making sure, you know, whether he Sometimes he's probably good, you go deal with it, you know, like I didn't even need to know that. But yeah, it's again, I just think it's just communication. So, and it's it's been great. >> When it comes to these joint practices, do you kind of sometimes have to save your guys from themselves cuz they get so amped up seeing a different color jersey on? >> Uh no, cuz it it's it's still not a game, right? It's so it's uh It's um yeah, it's it's it's it's just that. But but they do get amped up and they're just excited and like I've I've told the coaches I haven't told the players. I mean, it's a I've done a joint practice there before with the Jets and it's a cool place. I mean, they you know, they got the bikes uh with the kids and stuff like that and that's for a cool cause for the for the local and so we'll do that too just like a lot of the other teams do when they joint and then um you know, there's a a ton of fans there. I mean, it's it's Green Bay. What else you going to do? >> [laughter] >> Do you have a certain number of plays you'd like to get in to if you laid out the whole >> I love it there by the way. So. I do. And you know, I'll say this too, it's uh like my family will end up being there, my kids and they just cannot wait to get to Aunt Bree's house for for all the snacks that are there. Go ahead, sorry. But go ahead. >> How many plays do you want to get [snorts] in offensively? Is there >> Um yeah, I mean, we're we're roughly in that kind of 45 to 50 uh with with the ones and then um really we'll take it all the way to the 11th hour in terms of that next group cuz that next group a lot of them are going to be playing 2 days after that. So, and and with us having kind of the short week if you will, um we got to be smart about that. So, we'll take that all the way up to Wednesday. >> Are you used to playing once your ones versus their ones on the same like what's the difference? >> Yeah, yeah. So, you just you just split up the fields, right? And uh you know, so we'll we'll be on uh one field with the one offense versus versus all the offense versus you know, all their defense ones, twos, and threes. And then um you know, obviously they'll be on a different field and then when we get to a two-minute situation, we'll come up. So it kind of has more of a game feel and you know, both sides supporting each other there. So.

text: So, are you actually 10% body fat, Jack? Cuz the broadcast was promoting this. Uh, >> I I don't think I'm that low. Back when we got tested in college, I was like in the mid- teens, I think. Uh, yeah, I don't think I'm quite quite as low as 10%, but that's all right. Got to have a little bit of protection on me to take hits. >> How'd you feel about Friday night? >> I felt good about it. I think it was a good performance by by all three phases of the team, offense, defense, special teams. Everybody was making plays. Um, I think offensively we did a good job. You know, in the run game, we had we had some big runs. had some big passes too and guys were flying around making plays uh uh you know on deep balls and stuff. Uh I think that that gave me a little bit more, you know, made me a little more comfortable in the indie game. But I think just getting more and more reps and especially more more mental reps cuz that's a big thing for me too, like just watching these guys and the way that they operate, the way that they perform out there, picking up as much as I can from them, both out here on the practice field and then watching film too and trying to take as much of that into my own game as I can. Obviously processing information such a pivotal part about playing quarterback and it's something that a lot of people have said you've done really well in your career so far, but how has it changed over the course of training camp? >> Um, I think just just starting to understand the offense more and understanding what we're trying to do on certain plays, why, you know, we might be changing the play against certain looks, things like that, trying to get us into uh like a run play that might be better against a certain front or a certain, you know, safety rotation, something like that, or a pass play that might be better against man versus against zone. So, I think just starting to get more in tune with that as part of the offense and starting to process that more and that that allows me to, you know, hopefully get us in the right play more often than not. >> Taking me back to your college days for a second, you did have an opportunity to leave, right? But you chose to stay. >> Um, I didn't really like have any, you know, phone calls or people trying to tamper with me too much, but it it was never my intention to to leave. Anyways, >> why was it important for you to do that? >> Well, the the culture that we had there was incredible. like the culture of loving your teammates, like being part of something bigger than yourself, wanting to see the team succeed, wanting to see your teammates succeed more than you care about yourself and your own personal success and things like that. And uh you know, we had we had a whole 100 plus players and all the coaches, everybody on the in in the program bought into that. And when you have a culture like that, everybody's bought into it. You can do some special things with it. And I knew that that wasn't something I'd be able to find anywhere else. >> And the culture here has been great when they're really excited to see you get over the goal line yourself with your own legs. What's that like to have your teammates rally around you? >> Oh, that's that's so cool. And I I I you know, I think that's that's you know, football's the ultimate team game and and when you're getting excited for other people to do things like that, you know, you you know, there's times where you're going to be the guy out there scoring scoring the touchdown guys. There's times when you're going to be the guy, you know, pushing another guy into the end zone. There's going to be times when you're the guy on the sideline cheering your teammate on. So, I think uh anytime that you know the whole team can get excited for one guy's success, that's when you really come together as a team. It's cool to see just the support from everybody. And um but, you know, I obviously I try not to to lean into that too much. Yeah. >> Love it. >> What was your NFL team growing up? >> Uh, I was actually a Patriots fan growing up. Patriots. >> Yeah. So, I I I have a story behind it cuz uh I So, my dad had this uh 1996 Green Bay Packers Super Bowl VHS tape and it was the year that the Packers won the Super Bowl cuz he's a Packers fan. They played the Patriots in the Super Bowl and I like the Patriots colors. cuz I like the red, white, and blue. And so that's how I became a Patriots fan. I was really young, don't worry. Was your dad pissed about that? >> No, he he he was okay with it. He was kind of, you know, choose whatever sports you want. I think he's happy that I'm a Brewers fan, though. >> Jack, you were a guy that didn't get a lot of attention coming out of high school and then to become an undrafted rookie free agent and you played with a chip on your shoulder. Like what's your mentality around all of that? >> Um, yeah. I think uh you know especially coming out of high school and only having one scholarship offer I think naturally there's just going to be a chip um because I I want to you know show people I want to prove people wrong obviously but I think uh when you think like having a chip on your shoulder that can kind of put unnecessary pressure on from yourself onto yourself and so I think uh the biggest thing like especially with playing the quarterback position like there's times you just got to play free and you got to make plays like if you're putting so much pressure on yourself it'll be perfect and like I think of myself as a perfectionist like I want to run every play correctly and obviously that's just not something that that can happen. Um but uh I think sometimes like if you do something like that then you can put unnecessary pressure on yourself, chase like goals that really don't matter. So I think you know at times I think there's a chip just because I was like I was an underrecruited guy and coming out of you know college and being an undrafted guy. Uh there's definitely a chip but I think there's times where you know you kind of just got to you know be in the moment and play free. >> Talk about that a little bit more. High school football season is starting. There a lot of kids who are in that position. Yeah. What's your message to it? Uh, I think, you know, if you're if you're not, you know, being recruited a ton like and you feel like you you want to play college football, you feel like you should be, you know, you got to just go to camps in the summer. And then like if you're a quarterback, I mean, I think the biggest thing like you got to obviously you got to be able to make all the throws, but I think a big thing too is you got to just like understand know how to process a defense and know how to run an offense. And there's a lot of um high school offenses that don't really allow quarterbacks to do that. Like espec, you know, me personally coming from a double wing offense, I wasn't really processing a lot of defenses in high school. But you kind of just have to, you know, at times you got to teach yourself like you got to watch NFL games, you got to watch NFL film, you got to watch college games and kind of just understand the way that the game works at those higher levels. I know you said there wasn't one thing that you could say that you've learned, you know, from quarterback learn, but coming to a place with an offensive head coach.
