I think that's a big thing for me too. Uh, when I'm, you know, learning offense or learning a new game plan or something like understand why are we doing certain plays? Why are we, you know, running this motion? what what do we want this play to look like that we want the defense to react differently to that and I think I'm starting to learn that from from you know all the plays in our offense and I think that's starting to help you know the game slow down a little bit for me >> time for one more >> Jack do you have a nickname in high school college because the name Strand is very conducive to plays on words >> yeah um not really honestly a lot of people did just call me Strand either Jack or Strand yeah there's that's kind of that's kind of all it was all right >> leader in the clubhouse of the fan base is uh Strand on business >> strand on stand up. >> The last strand Cory Leven's been saying the last strand. >> The last strand. >> All right. >> How you feeling? >> Feeling pretty good. Um, you know, it's it's good to be back here in Atlanta after it felt like a month in Indianapolis. Um, but it it's good. We got a lot of good work in. Um, obviously getting back to work today feels good being back on the field. >> Does a week like this sort of a game simulation week help you get your juices flowing a little more? Absolutely. Absolutely. Um, you know, getting into the the gameweek schedule, um, Coach Lefansky has been preaching, you know, he wants this to feel like week one, um, as much as possible, getting us ready for when that comes. So, uh, you know, it it does feel it's it's the anticipation of it getting close. Um, it's exciting. Um, and you know, I can't wait. >> Did Mike seem any different to you today being able to do be full be in full go? >> No, he's the he's the same every day. Um, he's he's preparing. um you know and he's he he's the same every day he comes out here um whe no matter how much he's doing whether he's doing just seven on seven um we got to see him in 11 on 111 action today and that was that was a good step in step in the right direction for him um but yeah he he he's the same he approaches every day like a professional um and it was good to see him out here in action >> you don't have a lot of reps with Mike especially in team drills but just in your short time of getting to know him and working with him what do you like about the way he approaches is the quarterback position. >> Um, you know, he he has the the same mentality every play. He doesn't get too down on himself. He doesn't get too high. Um, you know, he comes in the huddle. Um, and you know, he he he demands the huddle uh as a quarterback as a quarterback should. Um, but you know, you guys see it. Uh, he has a a rocket as an arm. Um, can make every throw on the field. So, you know, it's it's cool seeing him in the in the live 11 on 111 action. um and and getting the getting the ground going. >> How'd you feel when you found out he was clear he's going to be able to do that out here this year? >> Yeah, it's exciting for him. Um excited for him. Uh I know it's it's been a tough tough journey going any injury is is a tough journey. Um so it it's good to see him on the opposite side of that. Um and you know he had a little scramble today which was which is cool to see. Um you haven't really got to see that. So, you know, it's it's exciting seeing seeing your teammates um doing what they love to do. Um you know, you can tell he loves the game of football, so it's really cool to to have him back out here. >> How how unique is his arm talent in your opinion? >> Yeah, I mean, it's it's extraordinary. Uh it truly is. Um just the he can he can truly make every single throw on the field. um whether that's a 50 yard bomb um intermediate routes um he he and he trusts in his arm uh to get it there. Um and that's a big thing and you know that I first noticed when I got here um he he trusts that he can make the downfield throws um no matter what the platform is. So it's it's really cool playing with him. >> What were your first conversations with Mike like when you got here? >> Um I don't I honestly don't even remember. uh probably along the lines of ready to do this thing. Um and you know, let's get to it. >> How do you feel like your camp has gone so far? >> Um I feel like I feel like it's been pretty good. Um just you know, for me it's coming out here and and stacking days um and making plays. Uh I know that's kind of cliche, but um you know, when my numbers called, you know, make make a play. Um and that's what I've been trying to do each and every day I come out here. Um go home, reset, and come back and do it again. Um, just trying to make make as many plays as possible to to put myself and this team in in the best situation to be successful. >> So far out of training camp, you know, we're getting into third preseason week. Uh, what's your evaluation of things so far? >> Uh, I think as a team, you know, we're coming along as a as a team. Uh, you know, it's fun being out here, especially being a rookie. So, you know, just, you know, getting in the motion and everything, just like taking everything in day by day. So, right now it's fun for me. It's a grinder at the same time. So, I'm taking the grind like Coach N say, man, you got to chase God through it. So that's what I'm doing right now. Just, you know, chasing God and let him lead me step by step. >> Adjustment wise, what's been the toughest thing? What's been the uh transition that might be uh easier than you thought? >> Probably the speed of the game. Uh it's probably it's a little bit faster than it is in college. So that's probably like, you know, the biggest like thing that I'm like, you know, adjusting to right now. >> What were your expectations for yourself coming into this process? >> My expectation of coming in was, you know, come in make a name for myself. Um you know, I feel like I've been, you know, the underdog, you know, since I came into college. So, man, I just still feel like I'm the same same dude, underdog trying to climb his way to the top again. So, that's, you know, that's my expectation just to make a name and, you know, put put my name out there. >> Do you feel like you've done that? >> Uh, uh, a little bit, but, you know, I got a long way to go. It's, you know, it's a it's a hill. You got to climb it step by step. You know, you can't just skip steps. You know, it don't work like that. So, you know, I'm just taking it step by step, day by day. >> At the same time, is it hard not to start thinking about next week? >> Um, I mean, it's hard, but, you know, you got to focus on, you know, the minor details right now. you know, the things that's in front of you right now. >> You have one thing you'd like to get accomplished Friday night? >> A win. A win as a team. Bring the W back home. >> Who have you uh kind of leaned on, relied on in that, you know, room so >> Um, you know, I talked to Mason Mason Smith. You know, that's a guy I always talk to. Uh, you know, Zack Harrison, Brandon Doris, like, you know, they've been very accepting, you know, just, you know, bringing me in and pulling me closer and closer together, like, you know, this what you do here, this what you do here. you know, it's the right way to do this or, you know, if you thinking too much, hey, this is what I do. So, you know, it's just great being in the room with a a lot of guys that, you know, that want to see me succeed and things like that. So, you know, it's fun just being in the room with those guys. >> What did you think of Douglas beating Harvard Columbus on Friday? >> Oh, man. I remember I think I remember getting back to the dorms Friday night. I looked at my phone cuz I had went to talk to him like last week. I went up there and talked to him just told him like, you know, it's just minor details like, "Yeah, minor details, you know, show effort. A lot of things are changed for you guys." and you know seeing that game right there with them coming back with the dub versus the reigning champs uh defending champs know it's fun you know as alumni to see that. >> Is it fun to to be here as a Cal team you know growing up here and spending year at Kenna State as well >> and it's fun like especially being back home my family is like right down the road like an hour away so you know it's fun being back home playing for the home team like I remember I was telling a couple of guys like I remember being in like 19th grade when the Georgia Dome got you know tore down and things like that. So, you know, just being here, it's it's fun, man. You know, in the city, just to be here to play for the city and, you know, it's just fun. >> Any desire to go back and play in college? >> Nah. Nah, that's class of 2022. I'm old. I'm class of 2020. So, hey, that's out the window for me. >> So, how how was it playing for Nate? And how is he is he different than other coaches you've been around, >> man? Very very energetic. Like, you know, I always like my last coach was coach Oscar J. So, he's an older coach, so know more of a laidback type of coach. like he's aggressive at times and things like that, but you know, playing for coach Na is fun, man. Uh, you know, just getting a young young coach able to run and go and just be so energetic every day to meet it. It's fun for me cuz like I'm a young guy, too, so I be needing the energy sometimes to come up there, you know, just put a smile on my face sometimes, you know, just get me going going someday. So, you know, it's just fun playing with coach Nali. >> Do you have a clear understanding of what they want your role to be here? Kind of a swing tackle role. You feel like you have a grasp on that? >> I mean, I I've always been the type of player. whatever coach asked me to play, whatever he needs me to do, that's what I'm going to do. Uh, I'm not really like set on one position. >> Hey, whatever the team needs me to do, that's what I'm here to do. >> We've we've heard a lot about the attention to detail, the efficiency of this coaching staff. Like, is is that something that has stood out to you throughout this process? Like, is that something that feels everybody's locked in maybe a little bit of a different degree? >> Uh, yeah. Uh, I can only speak from my experience. Uh, do you know Coach Callahan? >> Uh, yeah. very very uh detail oriented and like even it may be a good rep, he may have won a rep, but if something not the way he like it, he he going to get on you about it. Has he almost expanded your awareness of like what constitutes a good rep, like all of the little tiny details that go into doing something at the truly high highest level? >> Most definitely. You definitely look at film differently now. You know, uh when you're going back and watching yourself, you just like, ah, I could have did this better. I could have did that better. And even then, you know, like talking with the people with to with a naked eye, like my mom and stuff like that, but some you played a solid game. I'm like, ah, yeah. I know what I'm about to hear when I go in meetings on Monday. So, no, I wouldn't say that. >> I feel like I've seen you mostly at left tackle. Is that mostly where you've worked so far? >> Yes. Yes. Yes. >> Did you do all right tackle in Kansas City or is did you go back and forth? >> Uh, I went back and forth all the time. >> So, left is not the new thing to you. >> No. Yeah. >> Has pulled any tape from like before you were born yet? Has he done that yet? >> Oh, many times. many times when like especially when it comes to me dropping my post foot, he'll go back to like Washington, Dallas, even Oakland back in the day when he was head coach there and stuff like that and just like put on the tape and just let us watch it. Let's put it on a run like hey look at this, look at this. Like look at the the detail of this guy dropping his post for like how important it is like you know those little things intricate details >> his run game like the way that he orchestrates the run game. What makes it unique? What makes it work in your opinion? Uh, I think it's just mostly just getting off the ball and getting hands on the guy first, you know? Uh, getting movement, but like everything matters cuz you want the run lane to be as perfect as possible for that running back. As you can see, like it came to friction Saturday. Uh, with Tyler making that good run off the sideline and just, hey, showing what we could do. Uh, you know, helping us out. You know, people like Tyler, Bean, Brod, like those guys do a good job for us and help us. you mentioned getting getting hands on them kind of first in the run game, but I I feel like I've noticed that too in pass protection a little bit like the moments where you can find the chance to be aggressive and maybe attack. Is that is that accurate? >> Uh yeah. I mean, I feel like you don't want nobody to just put their hands on you, you know, like especially as a lineman, you'll go straight back into the quarterback. So, just finding any chance to get your hands right and just put them on put them on the defender first. I feel like that helps in any any position you at, whether it's at receiver, running back, quarterback, you know, like put your hands on somebody first so they don't do it to you first, you know, it it makes sense. >> Yeah. Uh, and going back to the to the details, like I know sometimes you can be paralyzed by the amount of details. So, how does coach Callahan strike that balance of here's a lot to to maybe work on or focus on or pay attention to, but also go play fast and and kind of go trust yourself on game day? Uh yeah, I think that's just part of being a pro, you know, just learning those details and learning how to balance that. Uh taking it to the field from the meeting room, you know. Uh I feel like he does make meetings a real a little light, like just laughing and stuff, you know, like and then like giving us a little 5minute break when we he knows he's talking a lot sometimes, but I feel like, you know, just like I said, it's just part of being a pro and just learning how to make that balance in life really. >> Knowing when to improve and then when to kind of like lock in. >> Exactly. Exactly. And like certain details are more important than others, but like all details matter. What's it been like being home? I was uh in Gwynette when coach uh Khan was building that program. >> Ah. >> Oh man, it's cool. You know, just especially being right down the street from home. You got you got all your friends, your family, but not letting it become a distraction is the most important thing. Uh I love my family, but they know like, hey, I'm at work, so like let me do what I got to do, you know. >> What's the energy like with Mike back out there today? 11 on 11. >> Oh man, it's good, man. It's just good to have him back on the field, see him doing good, smiling, making plays, you know, and I feel like all the guys have been supporting him, been around him, especially those guys around him in his room. Like, everybody's doing a good job. >> What do you like most about the way he kind of commands the quarterback position? >> Uh, that's that's that's hard to say cuz I feel like all our quarterbacks do a really good job just coming in there, commanding the huddle, and just like making sure everybody's on the same page, you know? Uh, whether it's somebody line right or or getting the count right. Uh, I feel like all these guys come in and just do a good job demanding it, you know, demanding excellence. >> Is there a degree of excitement in your room when you've got options at that position right now going into the final week of the preseason? We saw what Jack did on Saturday and >> Yeah. Yeah. I mean, yeah, man. Like like you said, like Jack went out there and did a great job Saturday. So, like when you see that and see your quarterbacks banning behind each other and doing stuff like that, man, it just it makes your job a lot easier as O line, you know? It just makes it makes you a little light. It makes you feel a little light.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski AT&T Training Camp Press Conference | August 24, 2026 | Atlanta Falcons
text: All right, excited about the work week. Uh we'll treat this like a regular season schedule and covered that with the players. Is that something Not me, I hope. Um covered that with the players this morning. So, we'll be into our regular season work. So, for instance, today is Wednesday to uh us and our players and I want them to get a feel for what the meetings are like during the regular season, what the practice uh schedule is like. Um we'll give them some game plan stuff on Miami, do some work on Miami. Now, there's a there's a bunch of stuff that you'll install uh on offense, defense, and special teams for this game that you won't show in the game, but I want the guys to get used to hey, here's a game plan, here's a new concept, uh here's a new pressure, here's a new coverage that we're running. Uh we're going to practice it the next few days and and just get the rhythm of that's what happens in the season. Uh so, that's kind of what we'll do. Today, being that we just played 2 days ago with a a bunch of guys, uh amended the practice schedule. So, the starters, the ones, will get all all a lot of the full speed work today, uh while the twos and the threes will be in a jog through a slower tempo. Uh so, you may notice that out there. Um but, great opportunity uh to to put three good days of work in, uh then get on the airplane and head down to Miami for the game Friday night. But, with that, I'll take any questions. >> How much will your ones play in Miami this week? >> I'll I'll talk through the playtime later in the week, Daniel. Um but, we will play our starters in this game. >> Is Mike included in that? >> You know, I I want to get through today, you know, obviously it's Mike's first time back out there, excited for him, obviously, uh to do 11 on 11, um but, we'll we'll we'll work through that. >> How how hard is the curve to be from where he's been all off season to being in 11 on 11 now? Like, what's the hardest part about that? >> I think it's a good question for Mike to probably answer better than I could, uh other than to say, obviously, uh he's had a bunch of reps without the the pass rush in the pocket, that type of thing, but um I I think he's more than eager to get out there and practice and he's done a great job. And I've mentioned this many times to you guys. I think there's ways to get ready to for and to prepare and to improve. You'd love to get every rep as as any player at any position. Often times that's just not possible. So there's so many things you can do to prepare yourself whether it's in a walk through or getting a mental rep or or what have you. So he's he's done a outstanding job in that regard. >> Coach, you always talk about >> In that regard when it comes to Mike, what are the expectations for him this week? Obviously know he's getting the full go today, but what do you need to see from him in the next few days? >> Uh No, really no different than any player. Just executing techniques and fundamentals on a on a given play. Again, the the new part for Mike is just being in there in with a full offensive line and full defensive line, but he's been in walk through huddles. He's been in seven-on-seven. He's obviously gone through individual. So this is a good now that you know Mike is cleared, it's a good that he can start that process of getting back to 11-on-11. >> Given the timeline that we're in now, is it realistic that he could start week one? I'm not saying you made a decision yet, but could that happen? >> Sure. I I can't speculate on those type of things. I'm really I want to to really stay today with Mike and and see how he does in practice. That's where I'll keep my focus. >> Would he have to hit certain are there certain markers or milestones you'd be looking for in three weeks to know that answer? >> Good question. I and I understand. I just I really have to stay in the moment on this one. Stay in the in the process and and worry about you know this is Mike's first 11-on-11 day. So let's see how he feels after today. >> Would you consider this kind of the day where the quarterback competition kind of starts in earnest? >> Yeah, I think it's Listen, competition is is near and dear to all of our hearts and and whether you're uh you know, whatever the depth chart looks like whatever that that Matt puts out. Um you know, you're competing every single day. We do compete periods in practice. You're competing against yourself. That alarm clock goes off and you're you're in a competition, you know, you're everything we do around this building is competing. So, I know it's easy to say uh position battles and those type of things, but uh we're we're constantly competing and and that's not the focus for our guys. Our guys are pushing each other by showing up and putting in the work. >> When we've asked you about you know, the quarterback competition and whatever you want to call it position battle whatever you want to call it, I think for the most part we've asked you about Mike Tua. >> Skylar played real well the other day. I mean, is is that open for him, too? Is that a possibility that he could do enough in the next couple of weeks to earn that? >> Yeah, I I think with all of our guys uh you you're you everyone prepares to be the starter, prepares to be the one. I I don't care where you what position you play on and what part you are on the depth chart. Now, having said that, uh obviously we work with our young guys and and want to make sure that we put all of them, Jack included, um through a process and make sure that that they are uh you know, getting the proper uh things down when it comes to you know, understanding systems, understanding defense or or what what have you. So, uh he's doing everything we're asking him to do, but uh I'm not going to start uh we're not going to put um those type of things out there for our guys to worry about. He he's he's got to keep his focus on on the day-to-day. >> After talking to you about you're always constantly evaluating every single thing with Michael, obviously it wasn't a full go. How much more of a fair evaluation you able to get now that kind of the handcuffs are off and there's no I don't want to say no restrictions or anything, but just that it's equal to what everyone else is. >> Sure. I I think you're right. We are evaluating everything and evaluating every drill and and those type of things, but uh you know, 11 on 11 is is the closest approximation to football and those preseason games are you you know, our our our games and they're keeping score and those type of things. So, certainly 11-on-11 uh is the closest thing to what we do in the fall. So, this is a big step for Mike and and he's excited for it. >> Dealing with different quarterbacks throughout your career, some guys have come back from injuries, a lot of lower body ones. You know, with that, as a coach, there's obviously a mental hurdle at times when you don't want to take that hit or coming back from that. How do you approach that with a guy like Mike who has had this routinely compared to other quarterbacks you've dealt with in the past? >> Yeah. I think there's there's a way to play this game and and you have to play it free and you have to trust in all the work that's been put in prior to stepping on the field and whether that's rehab or whether that's individual drills or what have you. So, I think Mike takes great comfort in knowing he's done everything in his power to get his body ready. And now we'll just continue along on the process. And again, this is you know, day one of of 11-on-11 for him. So, first time being out there in the team drill. So, we'll get through today, but we'll check in, see how he's feeling, and then have a plan for tomorrow. >> After you looked at the tape, how did you think Jack played? I guess. Colts. >> Yeah, I'd say very I kind of put that quarterback position in in one bucket. I thought both Coop and Jack did a nice job of taking what was there. I thought the ball went where the ball was supposed to go most of the time. Are there little things that we have to clean up with young players? Absolutely. Whether it's play calls or or whatever. There's always little things with with young players. So, Jack has room to grow, but when the quarterback position is playing it on time and the ball's going where it's supposed to go, that's what it should look like. Also, I you have to point out that protection was outstanding. And and that's no small part to playing good quarterback play. >> Spent a lot of effort this off season on the floor, the back end of your roster. Do you think that how well you looked against Indianapolis was an indication of what was sort of a testament to that or maybe a validation that you feel like you did it. >> I I think it's you have to be careful just with uh results and certainly results in preseason games. Uh listen, we we're out there, they're keeping score, we want we want to win. You make no mistake about that, but uh you also have to take everything into account um in that regard. >> Was that enough to earn, you know, positional battles aside, maybe more reps at least with the ones or or you know, higher leverage situations down in practice? >> We'll continue to work different guys in there. Uh at this point, Jack's going to work with the twos and threes and and uh but very excited about his development. Um but I I it goes back to the earlier point of like uh all of our young players, we have a plan to bring them along and develop them and that player development is a huge part of what we do. Uh whether you're talking about the quarterback position, the linebacker position, nose tackle, I don't care. Uh player development is important to us and being intentional about how we bring players along is important to us. >> I went through all of this in the I I had two at like 123 attempts from the opening of camp to now and I had Mike at like 112. How how pleased are you overall with the way you guys are kind of, you know, handled that? You know, I'm sure it's hard, but kind of even it it it kind of appears to me anyways. >> Uh well, we're trying. You know, there's you try to be I'll use the word intentional again just and I think credit to Tommy Rees, Alex Van Pelt, and how they've structured this is making sure that everybody's getting what they need to get ready, get what they need to show what they can do all all all the above. So, obviously with the different seven-on-seven drills that we've done uh have been important to make sure that guys are getting enough reps. >> How do you plan to split snaps now with the ones at QB? >> Yeah, you'll see it today. We'll work through different guys. Mike will have some reps in there, too. I will also have some reps in there. >> Going back to what you're saying about development, I know last week you guys kind of said even after the the first preseason game that you wanted to be more efficient in the run game. You just complimented the protection of the the guys up front. When you look at kind of the development within a within a week time frame from the offensive line, how do you feel like that adheres to what you're talking about in this building? >> Specifically the run game, Tori? Yeah, I thought uh you know, run game in the joint practices, in the games, uh it's no secret when any offense blocks the right guys. You you know, you give your runners a chance. I thought that uh we had uh the the players did a nice job. The offensive line, the tight ends did a nice job in the game of uh getting it headed up and and having a guy for a guy. So, like for instance, on TG's touchdown, you know, you can't block everybody, so you're going to have to make a defensive back miss. Um in that case, he did. So, uh the guys did a nice job understanding their roles. Now, you get into the games, the def- the defenses that you see evolve and become more exotic and and you have to work even harder as an offense to make sure that you're getting the proper, you know, blocking schemes you know, versus a given look. Uh so, those type of challenges will grow as you get into the regular season. >> Kendall Daniels seems to have really ascended during the course of this camp. What has he done to impress the coaching staff to get these up downs? >> Very diligent young man uh from the day he stepped on campus learning different positions, but very intelligent. Uh you look at his college career, played different positions. I think that has helped him uh certainly in his pro young pro career, but just doing what he's supposed to do. You know, uh there's there's some parts of this game where you know, you you'll hear coaches say, "Hey, do your job." And and he's done his job. >> I know you'd prefer to not have your quarterbacks get hit either out here or or or Friday night, but uh Mike's been pretty candid about saying when he recovered when in his recoveries from his previous surgeries, he needed to see that he could take that hit and get back up and he'll still feel good. Is that Is that how do you How do you navigate that? And how important is that for for him Friday night? >> Yeah, I I think bigger picture for me at least right this minute is getting in the huddle with all 11, going against a defense with all 11. Obviously, at our practices, we don't touch the quarterback and you know, that's every franchise is is like that when when when you're practicing. So, uh we'll get our work done and then that's just part of the game and that's that's something that obviously as quarterbacks uh you are always aware of on Sundays that uh you know, contact is part of of this game and uh but we'll focus on the practice portion and getting comfortable operating in in an offense when it's 11 on 11. >> Time for one more? >> What about Indy? Is he okay? Is he close to being back? >> He is close to being back. >> What happened? >> Uh not going to get into all the specifics, but he he's getting close. >> With this being the final week of training camp, how are your expectations different from those first couple of weeks for you guys? >> Well, I I think, you know, week three of the preseason has its own uh rhythm, if you will. And like I mentioned before, this is a big week for us to get used to that regular season schedule before we go into week one of the season. Uh so, I think there's the challenge for all of us, players and coaches, this week is is the game plan aspect of this, making sure that the dress rehearsal for an opponent scouting uh procedure is is where we want it. So, uh Coach Olbrich, Coach Reese, Coach Aukerman working very hard to make sure that uh the players are feeling a game plan week this week. And as players, it's all about now your routine. And uh how you take that install this morning from Coach Callan, installing the run game. We'll go out here to the walk-through some of the nuance to the to to the runs that we put in this week. Then you get to run them in practice and just getting the rhythm of their routine I think it is the big part of is a large part of this week. Okay. Thank you guys. Appreciate it.

title: Claudin Cherelus: 'We're all competing for our best' | Carolina Panthers
text: Y'all had Nick back out here today. First time in a while. What was it like just to have him on the sideline during practice? >> Oh, I loved it. I seen him yesterday and off day he came in the locker room um and it pretty much like sparked a smile on everyone face, you know. Um just knowing how much he meant to us and still means to us seeing him around in positive spirits. Um it was just great. >> But how would you assess camp to this point for for yourself? Uh, I kind of like to keep those uh to myself, but um overall it's been pretty good. I like the competitiveness we got. Um, you know, we're playing with like a spark. You know, everyone's getting feisty. You know, you guys have been here for some of them fights. You know, that's going to happen. You know, that just means, you know, we're a collective group. You know, uh, we can fight one day, come back, and next play we're dapping each other up. So, I love it. >> I mean, obviously, you're you're in a competition with Trevan. >> Say that again. You're in a competition right now with Trevan that Canal has told us about. Being that you guys are friends on and off the field, how are you approaching this this uh competition and how are you guys kind of maintaining that through competitive process? >> Yeah. Um you know, we look at everything the same way in that room. You know, we're always competing. It's not just me and Trevor. You know, we're competing with Devin obviously. You know, he's the allp pro in the room. He's the new guy. Um we're all competing on a daily basis. So, I'm not looking at it as, you know, I'm just competing with Trevon. I'm competing for my best. You know, we're all competing for our best. We're trying to be, you know, the be best version of that linebacker room that we can. And, you know, ultimately, you know, whoever is going to go out and help us, you know, that's going to be out there. So, not thinking too much of it. >> Claude, in what ways have you gotten better um since coming to Carolina a couple years ago? Uh that's a tough question, but um you know coming out of uh college I was you know I would say I had to learn some ball. You know there was a lot of scheme and stuff that you know I just didn't see uh down in swack football. It was a lot of you know Zone Reed. I remember um my first meeting in um you know my first meeting in in the league actually I asked a question about you know 10 personnel and everyone laughed because no one really does that in the league. there's always a tight end on the field. Um, unless it's Don, but um, I would say my my knowledge, my understanding of the game and then definitely communication. >> Kind of pick piggybacking off that, you know, you have some young guys in this linebacker room that Jackson watch as well. What's some things that you try to instill in them? Uh, now that you're, you know, you've been around the block a couple times. >> Uh, uh, everything really. You know, if he has questions, I always ask Jack if he's good. Um, but, you know, mainly special teams. You know, I feel like that's just major, especially as a linebacker in this league. you know, we tried out two guys, sometimes one on dime. Everyone else who's up got to be able to play four phases. That's just the nature of the game. Um, so, you know, besides everything else, special teams, just being on that. >> What are the biggest differences of wearing the green dot and not wearing the green dot? How you feel more comfortable? >> Um, having to get back to the huddle so fast, you know, cuz everyone's waiting on you. You got to get that call out of everyone. So, you know, you running down on a deep ball that may or may not get caught. you know, you got to run back and be in front of that ball, give that call out, you know, catch your your breath fast. Um, a lot of the communication, but I think we do a good job in the room of, you know, talking with each other. So, you know, certain stuff, you know, that the Jack linebacker can help you out or whatever, but I would say, yeah, just getting get into the huddle and communicating with everyone. >> Was that in a linebacker room that first meeting you you talked about asking about the 10 personnel? >> Yeah, it was. >> Who was the coach at that time? Uh, I was in New York actually, so I I had um coach Rudy, he's the DC for the Browns now. But I had asked that question and you know like a couple guys laughed and I'm looking around confused like what? Like it's a real question. You know, it definitely humbled me. >> You talked about not just competing against Trevan, but Devin as well. How would you describe Deon as a player? >> I mean, um, just his attention to detail, you know, how fast he picked up everything and obviously you can tell like everything matters to him. It's it's all important. Um just him constantly trying to get better, you know, coming out on a daily. Um just asking like, "What are you looking for? What do you need?" Like, you know, he's pulled me to the side a couple times and like told me like, "Oh, pay attention to this um from today's practice. Like, look at this." Um see if if this will help you on these plays. Just little stuff like that. Um it's definitely raising the standard of the room and he's definitely um great to have just helping everyone get better. Well, guys always say you got to prepare as if you're starting every week, but how different is it when you're when you get that call and you know you're up that week this position you guys both in? >> Uh I mean it's not much different. It's just something like oh someone is the only thing is like someone said it like it's official but like I said I go in every practice like I'm competing to start you know like I I I want to you know that's that's the task I want. I mean, personally, I think if you're not trying to start in this league, then you know, what are you what are you in it for, obviously. So, um, just going in, um, I don't think it's much different. >> What do you think your what what parts of your skill set do you think make you, uh, ready and equipped to to be full-time starter? >> I think, um, communication and mindset is the biggest thing. um just across the league in general. Um I don't think you can get by in this league by just being a freak in nature, like a freak athlete at offball linebacker. Just all the communication, the checks, the front sets, just knowing where you're supposed to be, you know, solving the pieces of the p puzzle. Um you have to be ready to do that inside linebacker in this league. >> Okay, couple more, please. when you're coming from a small school and like you said kind of picking things up with the league, how important is the partnership between you and a team, like having been here for a couple of years and knowing like we're going to work together to kind of get you where we know you can be? >> Uh I I think it was big. um just them trusting me, you know, like just seeing progress little by little from when I first came in to now to this point where um you know, there's a lot of small things that I'm not seeing, not picking up on when I'm watching myself and now to the point where like you know, the pre- snap communication I'm just getting on everything. I'm seeing I'm everything's slowing down pretty much. So, that was the biggest part. >> Do you remember when it kind of slowed down for you? Was there a specific moment? uh kind of my second year when like I damn near got you know like thrown in there. Um you know I was nervous obviously you know going to make my first start but then it was like okay I'm seeing little by little more experience and I feel like that's just what it comes down to like you know getting experience with everything it slows everything down. Okay. >> Thank you. >> Appreciate y'all. Hey,

title: Chuba Hubbard: 'I just want to win' | Carolina Panthers
text: You happy to see us? >> So happy to see y'all. Hope y'all are happy to see me. >> Chuba, how is this hamstring injury maybe different than than others you've dealt with or how are you kind of managing it obviously with the calf history, too? >> Yeah, to be honest, like I feel pretty good. Um uh I think the coaches are just and obviously training staff are just trying to take care of me. Obviously, last year I kind of came back a little early and it kind of lingered on for a little bit. So, I think it's just them kind of uh protecting me from myself a little bit. I would have been out the next day if I could have, but feel good. I feel healthy. Um looking forward to week one, obviously. >> You've been around Brad and Bryce and their dynamic for the last 2 years. How has that relationship evolved now that he's the offensive play caller? >> Yeah, I mean, it's been cool to see Brad obviously transition to that role. He's done a great job. Um he's fun. Obviously, him and Dave pick at each other's brains and stuff like that, but just to see the offense evolve, especially throughout the years, it's it's been fun. >> Chuba, we asked earlier in training camp who who we asked to Jaylen Phillips who he thought a leader on the team was and and the first name he said was you. And um we're kind of noticing that you have been a leader for a long time, but in the locker room now you are among the unquestioned leaders in the in the locker room. When you hear that, how does that make you feel? What are your reactions? >> Yeah, I mean, since I first came to Carolina, that was something that you know, I brought with me um as a rookie, obviously. A guy speaking up and being rah-rah, a lot of guys didn't like that. but a big thing is I've always just wanted to win. I wanted to change the culture in Carolina and I want to you know, bring the best out of not just myself, but other people. So, the fact that my boy Jaylen said that, obviously, I appreciate it a lot. He's a he's a great leader himself and player, but um I'm just trying to like I said, bring the best out of myself and others and help us continue to win here. >> Talking about bringing the best out of others, um you've been here, you've been the pupil, now you're kind of the mentor. Can you talk about how that process has gone and and you know, kind of I guess being sort of a big brother to guys like Ja'Marr Chase? >> Yeah, I mean I'm I'm starting to turn into uncle a little bit. Yeah, I'm I'm I'm def- I'm definitely getting there. But I just like to think of me in that spot when I was a rookie and how much it would have been to like have somebody like me constantly trying to push me, give me tips and things like that. You know, it goes a long way. A lot of these guys are just trying to figure out their process and find their footing in this league. So, any way I can help is is I feel like it's my duty to do that. The better we are as a whole, the more games we're going to win. So, that's my mindset. >> That after practice jugs group is growing each and every practice. >> Yeah, it's it's growing throughout the years. I mean, I remember when we first started it was probably like me, Tommy, Terrace Marshall, and then be like one or two other people at times. But me and Tommy for the most part. And then as time went on, more guys just want to get more work. And now you see all the time, not just us, but defense, offense, everybody's getting work some way, somehow. So, it just show you shows you that our work work ethic and where the team's head is. So, it's good. >> Let's see if Rico can >> wanted to be a part of helping to change the culture. Because you have been part of this for several years, where have you seen the culture evolve? >> I think the biggest thing overall is just the connectiveness of the team. Like I've had I've been a part of great teams since I've been here, a lot of talent, but this is probably the closest team I've been with where everyone's just not just playing for themselves, but for each other. And that goes a long ways. That's what winning takes cuz when the game's on the line, you know your brother's beside you and you don't went through training camp, you don't went through the Hall of Fame training camp with with everyone and and seen the worst days and the best days. It just brings another, I guess, level of play out. So, um I just attribute that to all the guys in the locker room, obviously the coaches. >> You know, last year you had the injury and then Rico came in and had some big games and then they were working you back in and then it was kind of like it seemed like they were in this area they didn't know how to really split up the carries. Um and then you you carried the load sort of down the stretch. Where are you now, you know, with with your NFL experience in terms of how many carries you need? Is it Is it important to get a certain number of carries? Where do Where do you kind of stand on that? >> I mean, to be honest, I don't really stand anywhere. Um I think I've said since day one everybody knows I want to win. I've seen it where I haven't gone the ball, I have gone the ball, and we've won games regardless of both both both things. So, the biggest thing for me is like, let me be healthy, let me be my best, and whatever is required of me, let me do that at a high level. So, that's where I go when I regarding that. >> When you When you think of that going from the guy who has encouraged J.B. for the last couple of years in his comeback, to be in the guy who shares a role with him, what's that been like for you and watching him go through that? >> Yeah, I mean, he's been through a lot of adversity. And the big thing about J.B. is he works really hard. That's something I noticed early on, and that's kind of hence why we work so great together. I've said it a few times, like I see a part of him in myself, especially when I was younger, and I feel like I'd be be doing a disservice disservice not just to him, but to myself and the team if I didn't do my best to try to prepare him to be the best. I think he's in the best shape he's been in. He's looked great, obviously. He's doing really good job. And he takes the coaching. He's in there late with me at times, and it's going to show up this year. So, I'm excited for him. >> I know it was a preseason game, but what was the moment like for you to watch him get in the end zone and tap his forearm and honor his father? >> Yeah, like I said, he's been through so much. I think people don't realize one obviously that side of things, but also the injury side of things and how that can just weigh on you. Not everybody can come back from that. So, I think it's just a testament to who he is not just as a person um or sorry, not just as a football player, but also a person. Like I said, his work ethic his work ethic is is great and to be able to see him obviously battle through everything and then have that moment was good. I told him many more will come though, so don't get too caught up on it. >> You talked about when you were a rookie, you've always had that leadership quality about you, the rah-rah guy, but it rubbed people the wrong way. What do you What do you mean by that? >> Well, it was just I mean, imagine a a rookie coming in and trying to I guess be rah-rah, lead the locker room and kind of saying stuff all the time. I haven't I didn't really earn my respect yet, you know what I mean? You got to got to earn your respect in this league. It was all in the right all in the right uh mind, I guess you could say. I just wanted to win and I felt like I'm passionate about this game. That's one thing I think everyone knows I care a lot about football. I care a lot about this team and I wanted to change change things in Carolina. So, I wouldn't say like guys were just like, "Oh, this kid." But, it was more so like, "Whoa, whoa. Easy now, young buck." But, um I stood my ground. I still do. Um I haven't changed. Obviously, I've evolved in different ways, but that's just always been a part of me. >> Is there a moment where you felt like, "Okay, now I have this respect to go along with my leadership quality?" >> I mean, I think throughout the years uh my first two, three years, I kind of just earned that. I was the same guy consistently over and over. Um win or lose, I still worked the same. Um I tried to bring people along and people started to see that. And as time goes on, you you you earn respect. Like I like I said, and now obviously, I'm I'm fortunate enough to be in a position where obviously, guys can come to me for advice or tips and look at me as a leader and that's a blessing. I'm definitely blessed for that. Yeah, I I do. I keep them to myself though, but my main goal is to win. Winning everything. Win my one-on-ones, win the practice, win the game, win the walk-through, win the recovery. That's that's my main goal always. >> Last one. >> Well, I'll make it two parts then. >> [laughter] >> First first one's easy but if Sunday was week one, would you be ready to play? >> Yeah. >> Okay. And second, I just wonder you've seen Bryce from the beginning so I wonder if Bryce looks any different to you in this camp than before. >> I think he just looks more confident. Each year goes on, the more the more his confidence goes up. Obviously, the the more you're in the offense, that comes with that so I think he's just done a great job not just with obviously the play calling and and leading us in that manner but just also just taking us in and making sure we're going in the right direction. I think it's hard to rally offense at times and you got so many different people. That's just football. So many different personalities. Everyone kind of gets going at different paces and stuff like this but I feel like he's done a great job of just I guess corralling the herd or whatever you want to say and and leading us. I I I'll always say Bryce is a one-on-one player and leader and also friend. He's a special guy so I'm glad he's our quarterback. >> You're coming home. Coming home comes too fast, doesn't >> Shoot. I still got some more years some good years in me though so but I don't think it comes fast. It did. It did. I try. >> [music] [music]

title: Panthers Live Press Conference
text: Heat. Heat. Heat. Heat up here. Heat. Heat. N. Alex. All right. What a day. Uh first of all, Atrium Health had uh Giani Norman out here, 11 years old. uh you know, love to bring him out here and just inspire the crew. You know, we all got stuff we're working on and Giani's got had his own battles to get back to where he's at and um but he was able to share that moment with the team. Um other good stuff, we had uh Nick Scon back um uh really successful surgery uh on the men, you know, right at the beginning of it, but if you know anything about Nick, the way he's going to attack this thing is like he does everything else. And uh you know, so he's uh Chris Brazzle as well. He was here uh inside getting some rehab. So good to have the guys back um around their teammates and uh showing a lot of love through the building. >> When were you to the surgery? >> Yeah, I think Nick was first. Uh that might have been like two weeks ago and then probably about five or six days after Nick. Uh Chris also went down there. They were down in Texas uh together actually uh recovering and we were able to stay in touch with them. Uh Jaquin Jarrett uh did a great job of going down there, hanging out with the guys. cuz I was able to FaceTime them in their recovery. You know, they it was like right after the Bills game, you know, they were they had all their ideas and thoughts about, you know, what went on and so it was good to kind of hear that and uh see that they're following along with us. >> Dave, go ahead. >> Dave, what's the update on uh Devin Lloyd? >> Yeah, Devin was just a vet rest, so he was really sore uh coming out of the practice. Um really had a fantastic day and then, you know, we just kind of we weren't we were going to play him, but coming out of that didn't feel like we wanted to. And then uh today he got some like more intensive treatment um on his knee and he was able to he he's doing great. He's doing great. Uh we don't foresee this being something that's going to hinder him long term, but it was a good moment and opportunity for us to take advantage of this window uh to get him all the way back. >> Chuba's been um Chuba's been um battling that hamstring. You know, >> what is your prognosis for him? Is he expected to be ready for the regular season? >> Absolutely. He he's expected to be ready for week one. Um, I think he hit over 20 miles an hour the other day in RTP, but that's in a controlled setting and right now we didn't want to put him back out there. He's not ready to to for someone to pull on his jersey for him to pull through that, but he's ahead of schedule. He's doing a great job. >> What about Xavier? >> Yeah, Xavier, his foot's still sore. He's in a boot. We're going to have him in a boot till Thursday. Take that off. Then we'll ramp him up over the weekend to get him ready for that practice that we have on the uh bye-week before the Chicago week. Dave, what about Haynesk? Expect him to be ready for this preseason finale. >> He will not be uh ready for the preseason finale. He's trending same direction as Chuba. He's getting his uh long speed and all that stuff up, but he's not in a place where we can cut him loose to play football right now. >> Dave, what's your plan on not you not going to play the starters on Friday, I guess? >> Yeah, that's still up in the air. Um and honestly, you know, we have a really really intense practice planned with the Texans on Wednesday. So, you know, depending on how we come out of that and um if we get the volume that we're looking for, the odds are they won't play. Um you know, if between um Demo and I, if we're not able to get the work that we wanted, there may be some early play for some of the guys, but um we're going to kind of make that decision after the practice. >> The roster is about to go down to 53 in six days. What are the little things you look at? Maybe some of those fringe players that, you know, hopefully they come out on the other side of that. >> Yeah, versatility is huge, right? whether you're a um interior offensive lineman, whether you're a wide receiver or a DB, you know, can those guys play special teams, can the guys inside play multiple spots? Those things are all going to help. Uh we have a really competitive team, really competitive roster. We got some tough decisions to make, Dan and I. And we've been previewing some of those, but we got another great opportunity and we have a practice on Wednesday and we have a game on Friday uh to be able to look at the whole group to to give them one more shot to compete and to show us what they can do. Dave, we saw Darren Waller out there for the first time today. How do you think he looked? >> Yeah. Um, you know, we sprinkled him in, got him a couple of team reps. He looked really good in RVAs. We weren't able to get him a target in the in the course of the team periods, but he looked good running. He's in great shape, and I think it's just a matter of time for him to just hear the words, get where he fits into the concepts for us to be able to continue to evaluate that. >> How involved do you think he'll be Wednesday? >> Uh, same deal on Wednesday. He'll pop into some team uh settings and we'll get him some exposure against the Texans in that practice. >> Dave, when you signed Darren, what was the conversation like? I mean, he's coming in mid camp. He's getting a week of work. >> Yeah. >> Uh how are you able to evaluate him that quickly? How much you have to take in his past and how much you have to take in like the the status of the rest of >> Yeah, we have to lean on his uh his recent history playing. Um last year, you know, for example, just watching the cutups and that's the reason why we brought him in. leaning on that part. Hard to get the evaluation. We spent the first part of last week just running him and pushing him and making sure he was practice ready. We didn't want to rush that part. And then this week, the plan is rolled out today, you know, got him out there, got him some exposure, and he'll get some great reps on Wednesday as well to evaluate it. Um, but again, it's a good room. We love those guys and trust them, you know, and so, uh, he comes into a room to see where if he can help us in some way, but the guys are doing a great job of of showing what they can do as well. >> He play Friday. >> Uh, he probably won't play Friday. Um, you know, if we get enough work on Wednesday, he I don't I wouldn't want to put him out in a game type of setting having only practiced for a week. >> In the uh during the the game Friday, I think the team br excuse me, Saturday team broadcast said Taylor was going to be out at least another month. >> Do you have updates on him and I turn? >> I don't have any specific timelines on Teemo. Um, we are kind of at the mercy of uh the treatment and recovery um for him. So, we just have to kind of make sure that we're following that course. Um, if you ask Teemo, he's running around. He looks great. He's pushing sleds. He's doing everything. Um, but it's just a matter of the medical condition just doesn't allow you to put him into a contact type of situation right away. So, we're going to have to play that by ear. >> Was that Cory that interception? kind of what can a play like that just do for another guy? >> Yeah, it's a confidence thing and and for Cory, you know, he was a guy that just continued to make plays last year and um just looking for those types of plays. You know, he had one he had a play a couple maybe two or three plays before the interception that he was close on um and could have made the op and then he made the one that that counted there at the end as we got closer and need a touchdown situation. So, um, yeah, and Cory, the the thing about Cory is he's really improved on special teams, and we played him at nickel, we played him at safety, we played him at corner last year. So, that versatility definitely sticks with us as we go into the uh into making the 53. >> Um, I know you like what you've seen from Jonathan Brooks so far. If Cuba returns for week one as you expect, do you foresee a running back by committee approach in that game? >> Yeah, we'll definitely uh roll it out just the way we have been. um where you'll have a lead back for the series, the other guy comes in on third down so they can be in there for the protection and also we run the ball on third down. So those are good opportunities to just keep a guy into the game um while the other person whether it's Chuba or JB, we'll make that decision when we get closer. But whoever the the lead guy for the base downs is, you know, they get they'll get the bulk of that rhythm um so that they kind of feel what's happening with with the fronts and how the defense is trying to play as well. After watching tape from the joint practice and then the game, is there anything you learned about this team coming out of Jacksonville that you didn't already know? >> Well, we're fit. We're ready to play a game. Um, you know, starting nine days before everybody else, you know, between us and the Cardinals, we've gotten these guys to a point where we're ready to play football and that showed up in the game. We were able to stay strong throughout uh the rest the third and fourth quarter. And uh so that's just a a great collective team effort of Jeff Brown and I with the calendar, Josh Hinx, Denny Callington working to make sure we're pushing the guys the right way outside of a couple of guys who have missed some practice time. Robin Doo started a little bit later. Derek, we had to rest Derek and kind of get him on and off type of rhythm. Uh Bobby Brown missed some time. Those are four guys that really need this week. They need Wednesday. they need the following week and those couple of practices that will get to get them up to speed from a conditioning standpoint. Um, so that's something I learned about our group and um, and just the fact that like the physical nature of how we play, it isn't always reflected on the scoreboard. I'm glad we've won two out of three, but for me as I'm looking, I just want to see our play style and we're playing a physical style of football that I'm really proud of. looking at linebacker. Obviously, Devin was not out there, so a lot of treb and clad with the ones. Where does that competition stand heading as? >> Yeah, they're headtohead. Um, you know, it's back and forth and it's like it's neck and neck. Again, I've talked about this before, but these are guys who aren't just teammates. These are friends and they understand that. They understand what they're up against. We could use them both and and we we're going to need them. You know, the nature of the position is a violent spot. Um, and both of the guys can help us on special teams as well. So, we'll have to make that decision as we get closer, but uh they're both doing a great job of competing uh to be in that spot next to Deon. >> We've asked you a lot about about that position battle. Is there another one that you're kind of that's kind of flying under the radar that you think is very critical? Also, >> I think we're all aware of the receiver, you know, uh group. It feels like we have about seven guys that I'd love to keep. I don't know if we're going to be able to keep seven. You know, there's been years where we were able to keep seven for a while. Um I don't know if that's possible. So those guys are competing. They're pushing. You know, that's that's Jimmy. That's John Mechy. Just Reed, Casey Washington keeps making plays. Um, so these are guys that are going to be in the conversation as we get down to it. >> This is the last question right here. >> Uh, Ryan Fitzgerald obviously hit the 61 yard in Jacksonville. This training camp, he hasn't been in a competition, but he is still performing. How have you noticed his approach to this offseason in comparison to >> Yeah, it goes back to the spring. Ryan's goals coming out of it. Tracy gave him the challenge. Time to get stronger. Um, he took that challenge. He got stronger. He focused on a lot of plyometric explosive type of movements and put on some good weight, some good muscle. And I mean, you can see the ball jumping off his foot different than last year even. Um, and I'm really proud of the way that Ryan's just he's so steady, you know, and and he handled the competition well. He's handling this part well being our guy. um missed the chip shot right after the the 61 yard, you know, but again, it's just about the reminder of like you just got to stay locked in and go through your your whole routine before it. But um I'm really excited for what he's done. >> Thank you, coach. >> All right. Thank you. >> Thank you. What up with y'all? >> Johnny, what up, man? >> Questions for Y'all had Nick back out here today for the first time in a while. What was it like just to have him on the sideline during practice? >> Oh, I loved it. I seen him yesterday and after he came in the locker room u and it pretty much like sparked a smile on everyone face, you know, um just knowing how much he meant to us and still means to us seeing him around in positive spirits. Um it was just great. >> How would you assess camp to this point for for yourself? Uh, I kind of like to keep those, uh, to myself. But, um, overall it's been pretty good. I like the competitiveness we got. Um, you know, we're playing with like a spark. You know, everyone's getting feisty. You know, you guys have been here for some of them fights. You know, that's going to happen. You know, that just means, you know, we're a collective group. You know, we can fight one day, come back, and next play we're dapping each other up. So, I love it. >> I mean, obviously, you're you're in a competition with Trevan. >> Say that again. You're in a competition right now with Trevan that Canal just told us about. Being that you guys are friends on and off the field, how are you approaching this this uh competition and how are you guys kind of maintaining that through competitive process? >> Yeah. Um, you know, we look at everything the same way in that room. You know, we're always competing. It's not just me and Trevon. You know, we're competing with Devin obviously. You know, he's the allp pro in the room. He's the new guy. Um, we're all competing on a daily basis. So, I'm not looking at it as, you know, I'm just competing with Trevon. I'm competing for my best. You know, we're all competing for our best. We're trying to be, you know, the be best version of that linebacker room that we can. And, you know, ultimately, you know, whoever is going to go out and help us, you know, that's going to be out there. So, not thinking too much of it. >> Claude, in what ways have you gotten better, um, since coming to Carolina a couple years ago? Uh, that's a tough question, but um, you know, coming out of, uh, college, I was, you know, I would say I had to learn some ball. You know, there was a lot of scheme and stuff that, you know, I just didn't see, uh, down in swack football. It was a lot of, you know, Zone Reed. I remember um, my first meeting in um, you know, my first meeting in in the league actually, I asked a question about, you know, 10 personnel and everyone laughed cuz no one really does that in the league. There's always a tight end on the field um, unless it's Dime. Um, I would say my my knowledge, my understanding of the game, and then definitely communication. >> Kind of pick piggybacking off that, you know, you have some young guys in this linebacker room that Jackson could watch as well. What's some things that you try to instill in them? Uh, now that you're, you know, you've been around the block a couple times. >> Uh, uh, everything really. You know, if he has questions, I always ask Jack if he's good. Um, but, you know, mainly special teams. You know, I feel like that's just major, especially as a linebacker in this league. You know, we tried out two guys, sometimes one on dime. everyone else who's up got to be able to play four phases. That's just the nature of the game. Um, so you know, besides everything else, special teams just being on that. >> Father, what are the biggest differences of wearing the green dot and not wearing the green dot? How you feel more comfortable? >> Um, having to get back to the huddle so fast, you know, cuz everyone's waiting on you. You got to get that call out to everyone. So, you know, you running down on a deep ball that may or may not get caught. You know, you got to run back and be in front of that ball, give that call out, you know, catch your your breath fast. Um, a lot of the communication, but I think we do a good job in the room of, you know, talking with each other. So, you know, certain stuff, you know, that the Jack linebacker can help you out or whatever, but I would say, yeah, just getting get into the huddle and communicating with everyone. What do you say about how, you know, maybe how far he's come or his ability to learn and pick all that up and how he's doing in that space? >> Well, that's not true. It's just the understanding of how important it is to the collective group, the other 10. He is the epicenter of our communication than the center is. So, the understanding of they're there listening to you, right? Being crisp, concise, on point, right? Once you get into the huddle, I've got this, I'm in charge. That's us as well as coaches, right? How do we get that out of players? Anything that we do, be it a quarterback, be it another player, it's our job as coaches to get to max- maximize their measurable skill set. That is a we thing, not a me thing, not an individual thing. So, we're all in that together. He is certainly more than capable of that and I saw it today he was even better. >> Now that you've settled on this quarterback decision, how much effort has to go into turning four quarterbacks into three for the roster? >> Well, we're going to get a chance to see it Thursday night. I'm excited for Dylan and see Taylen. You know, we went through the first couple of games the way we went about it. Tylan did a great job over the course of time with limited reps and went and going against the Bills, really executing our offense at a high level. So, I'm excited to get him out there and see him play. >> Neither uh DeShawn or Chig are playing Thursday night? >> They will not play Thursday night, either one of them. >> Did you have a change of heart in if you were going to play the starters? It felt like early in the preseason or training >> I did. And I and and I talked to coach Vrabel. We we had talked about initially like wanting to play our starters. And get him a series or two. They really hadn't played their guys, but we both felt like we were thin. Especially up front on both sides of the ball, and we just felt you know, we'd be better off not playing our starters in the game Thursday night. >> I know you said it was your decision yesterday and you were making the decision, but I'm just curious, did you consult at all with Andrew Berry or anyone in the front office, or did you just morning just inform them that that was the decision? >> Well, I think any major decision, right? Is an organizational decision. Ultimately, I have to make that call, Uh I guess if you said, "Hey, the decision on trades or free agents that we bring in or contracts, ultimately Andrew would have to make that decision, but those are organizational decisions, right? That's that's the way it runs and and that's we we talked about it. We did. We had conversations about it and we landed on this. >> Is there enough time in the preseason for Malik Collins to be ready for game one? >> Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. I saw it when he first showed up. I mean, he was doing box jumps. I was like, is he's ready now, for God's sakes. I was kind of bummed he wasn't out there for 3 weeks. I mean, he looks great. I mean, holy cow. I mean, uh impressive for the injury that he had and his work in the off season at his age as a vet, it says a lot about him. How much he loves football, how much he loves the Browns and his teammates. Awesome. >> Talking about Deshaun, do you expect him back on the field today or tomorrow? >> If not, it'll be shortly. It's It's It's just something that's a little bit nagging. If we do, we'll get him out there. If he doesn't go practice, he'll probably do some individual today. I'm hopeful he'll do some of that. >> What's his injury? >> What's his injury? We're moving forward, I think we'll see some of him today. Uh to what extent I don't know that. We'll see. He was in the walk-through today, which is a good sign. >> Now that this thing is wrapped up, how confident do you feel that Deshaun can get all the reps that he needs to get with this starting 11 to be super ready to go? >> Oh, yeah. I feel very confident. >> Good. >> Thank you.

Um, so I think it's a balance of both ways. We we've, you know, been here a long time and played with a lot of tackles and feel like we we can always manage situations when a backup goes in a game and and I I mean, I can I feel like I can name 15 tackles we've played with at some point, you know, and the different things that we tried to do schematically to help them. I >> mean, last year Dalton came in late, he ended up helping you obviously. [cough and clears throat] How much how much how hard is it to do that if you did end up having to try to add in somebody at this point in the game or seeing that last year make you say if that's a way it ends up going we can >> I think the easiest focus for us is we have guys in house that that we believe in and continue to get reps with them and um like I said still feel like we have several practices left to get all that ironed out and and a lot of times this thing goes into the season sometimes where where you decide who fits you best and and what are the combinations that you'd like to utilize in certain situations. You know, I I don't I don't feel like anybody should feel comfortable going in this last week that that they've made the team. That's a that's a big part of it is we want guys that we can depend on. Yeah. I not set in stone yet on exactly how that'll fall, but but similar. >> You're evaluating the players. You're also evaluating their schemes a little bit. Uh where we're really carting it up and and looks we think we'll see early in the season. So there's a balance there of ironing out schemes, starting to game plans and stuff and and get the work we feel like we need to get. Now that you've seen the film, what did you think of Connor and Brian inside on the offensive line? >> A lot of positives. I think a lot of positives and two guys that I really believe are are improving with every rep. Um there's a lot of intent from them on on making sure they get better. And so that's that's really encouraging to see. They're locked in in all scenarios, whether it's meeting, whether it's walkthrough, whether it's practice. Um encouraged by what I see from them. >> Have you would you say it's fair to say that Connor has made up the time maybe he lost by continuing his re rehab. >> I think it's fair to say that yeah, he you wouldn't have known if if you brought somebody in here that didn't know the situation. They would think um he looks like he's been practicing for a while. >> When you and Darren went over in the film, how did you guys think Dante did in his return options? >> I think Yeah, I think him and all the returners really got what was asked of him there. Um, so I wouldn't say you were discouraged or or overly um raving about any of them. I think they all they all did a nice job handling the things we wanted them to handle and um so that part was encouraging. >> Thank you. Thank you. >> [music]

title: HELP! HELP! Minnesota Vikings Still Don't Have A Center! HELP!
text: Blake Brandle can't snap. Sound the alarms. Oh god. >> You are Locked On Vikings, your daily Minnesota Vikings podcast, part of the Locked On Network, your team every day. >> What's going on everybody? Welcome to the Locked On Vikings podcast, where we're always trying to learn something new. Today's Town Hall Tuesday. That means I am answering your questions as submitted to me via the Google form in the show notes. If you have a question at any time, throw it in that Google form and I will get around to it by the next Tuesday. First question comes from Arturus MK who asks, "Brenle is looking a little cooked. Should we maybe move Walter Rouse to center or maybe Caleb Tierin or Tyrion Ingram Dawkins to center? Obviously, we cannot bring some bring in somebody who's played center. Uh, so should who should we convert to center next? Okay. Uh, I we shouldn't convert any more centers, but I I I want to give this a little more dedicated time because it's something I've mentioned a few times, but like Will Ragus has been on this all over this. Uh, I know Jud Olga's mentioned it too at camp that not only have there been a handful of like disaster broken play missed snaps from Brle and Jurgens, but there's a lot that are outside the frame where guys are chasing them that that don't get necessarily mentioned. And that's to me going to be a bigger problem. If the snap is not accurate, it will throw off the timing of the play. And typically what you really want is you want the snap to go to that dominant side so that the the quarterback doesn't have to wait for it to turn so that he can turn and catch the ball at the same time and get back into his drop back that much faster. Um, if you have it on the wrong side so then he has to take it and then turn, you're going to be behind and now suddenly all of the really precise Kevin Oonnell timing stuff is ruined. Not to mention the potential for a disaster broken play. So, the fact that this has continued and last week, uh, I think it was Rags asked Kevin Oonnell about this and said, "Hey, there's been a lot of bad snaps. What's up?" And he acknowledges, "Yep, that's an issue. We're working on it. It's an issue. We we're, you know, we're not going to we we cannot let that be an issue. We have to fix it." But that seems like lip service. I don't have an encyclopedic knowledge of who the centers are elsewhere around the league. I I typically wait for the Vikings to make a transaction or not. Then I'll decide, you know, what I feel about that guy, then we'll watch tape. We'll all do it together. Um, but something's got to give, right? Somebody's center three is going to be available for trade. There's a Brett Jones out there somewhere for those with eyes to see. So, for me, something out there's got to work. You got to have a better plan. even if it's a better backup plan than Michael Jurgens and you say, "Okay, Blake, you're going to get go out there because you're a pretty good blocker, but short leash these snaps have to be good and you know, if not, we're going to do the quick hook and we're going to put in some other veteran we can get our hands on that can snap reasonably even if they're not as good of a blocker because a a a proper snapper is going to be more important, bar none. And if they just walk in with Blake Brandle backed up by Michael Jurgens, I will call that irresponsible and it will be a problem and I will be right to criticize it. There's just there's no way that this just goes away. So I it's got to get fixed. Brandle had all off season to fix it. It is not fixed. That is what it is. The most convenient point to pick up a center might be on day. So maybe we'll wait till then cuz that's going to be the best time to get one. But if not, yeah, I'm going to be pretty loud about it. The last Dayton Triangles fan asks, "Earlier in the offseason, Arie mentioned that he thought the Vikings would use more cover three. Is that something we can glean from preseason games? And if so, has it borne out over the first two?" It has not. The Vikings averaged 17 cover three snaps a uh cover three reps a game. It was like 34% or something like that or I'm sorry it was uh it was like 28% last year and they are up to 18 snaps a game which because of preseason weirdness reasons that's 34% but that's still very much within a range of like similar uh over the last two games. So I think they're going to use cover three about the same. Now if they were going to make that change they might not want to reveal that in the preseason. But on the other hand the preseason's for your staples. So, I would say cover three remains not necessarily one of those staples. Next question comes from Brian who asks, "Jim McCarthy wasn't this bad in camp, right? He held his own in the competition with Murray for a few weeks. He seemed to do well in joint practices. What explains the discrepancy between that and his preseason game performance?" Um, the the game is different. The preseason game is different. And this kind of leans into what uh or leans against the arguments that I've been making about like joint practices versus the preseason where joint practices are used as kind of the tuneup for the ones. Well, the one thing the ones aren't going to get is that stuff in between the play. That's they they can try to practice it on time the best they can, but it's much more strictly enforced in an actual game. You get a delay of game penalty. There's an actual play clock that's there. It's all exactly the same. And so for McCarthy, not only are these reps more live, you can get tackled, you can get hit, things are going to be faster, the other team doesn't care about your well-being, right? They can they can light you up. But the other part of it is that the operation between the whistles is timed and hurried and there is a rhythm that you cannot stop. You hit that big thing to Ty Felton, you got to get up and in the huddle and go do the thing, right? you have that kind of play in practice. Well, people celebrate a little bit, but you're going to be on to the next play, but you don't have to respot the ball, move that much unless you're doing like a situational drill or whatever.
