title: Special Teams Coordinator Chris Tabor meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Chris, I wanted to know about um Bradley Pinion. He's had a 15 yard punt, a 25 yard punt. How do you handle that during the week or in review? Do you hammer him for that? You tell me. He's a vet. >> No, he's a vet. I think in to the naked eye, everybody would say, "Yeah, you got to be better than that." Uh he knows that that needs to get rectified and uh looking forward to seeing how he handles this next game for, you know, next opportunity. Um, Kyle Lewis, uh, it looked like he should have had a tackle on a punt return, maybe two punt returns. I couldn't tell. Tell me about that. >> No, he's a player that, uh, very instinctual, you know, and can run. So, he's been playing on the inside core and the punt uh, all through spring and and most of training camp and then we just made the transition to move him outside just kind of maybe looking down the road a little bit, see what that would look like. And uh I mean those were he's had three reps, you know, the Giants practice and then the two in the game. Uh obviously did a great job of getting down there which is first and foremost and then we'll work this uh the finish phase. I feel real confident that he can get that done because that's really that's who the player that that's what he is. >> I was going to ask you about that. He's all over the place with him. Why do you why do coaches not worry about throwing too much? >> Uh I think what we're doing with him is in our world, I mean, he's number one, you have to ask, is he a good football player? He's a good football player. He's instinctual. He can run and he's physical. Uh playing Gunner out there, it's really it's it's a very violent deal out there. It's usually twoon-one. Uh he fits that mold that he can and he's shown that he can win on the outside. I I still think there's going to be things that he's going to learn through repetition. Uh but I'm not I'm not worried about it. He's uh he likes to play football, so he he's he's willing. >> Chris, uh DJ Herman looked like he got a couple of good blocks, few good blocks out there, uh as the upman. Can you talk about that and tell me the difference between having him or a big man, a defensive or offensive lineman? >> Yeah. No, I think it's it's something that we're just kind of always working. Uh Herm is getting better and better. I mean, he's he's he's a guy that we're trying to make uh multiaceted. Also, he's worked up on the front line. We've put him back there in the back. He's a guy that can wear a lot of hats, so we're just trying to get him a lot of reps and uh he is he's he's he's getting better. I saw progress from the New York practice uh into the game. So, I was excited about that. >> And and what's the difference in having a I know he's a converted linebacker, I guess, a offensive guy versus a lineman, a defensive or offensive lineman in that role. >> Well, is it's really about it's really about space uh between the the blocker and the returner. And uh so and really can a player play out in open space? Can he change direction and and those type of things? So uh when I see the skill set regardless whether offensive lineman, defensive lineman or offensive player, you know, a fullback type, uh those are the kind of guys we're looking for in the back end. >> Chris, how popular do you get at this point in in the training camp? >> I don't think I'm very popular at all. Uh but now I understand what the question is. I mean, this is, you know, a lot of guys had a lot of opportunities the other night and uh, you know, we got to clean up a lot of things obviously, but it'll it'll be the same there. There's going to be a bunch of opportunities again uh, Friday night for them and and um, as as I stated in the meeting, there's going to be times you're playing so much offense or defense, you're going to be tired on special teams, but you're going to need to win that one play rep. Uh, I I I said go back to when you were 12 years old. would you give anything to playing in the National Football League? And so here it comes. When you say that you're tired, I'm going to say go back to that 12- year old kid. Here's that one shot. Go for it. So, um, like to see some improvement from the guys. Uh, but, uh, everybody's, you know, you got to take advantage of your opportunities, right? >> What do you tell guys about, uh, the importance of using the fair catch signal in terms of self-preservation? Maybe >> I would never use the word self-preservation. And I would use making good football decisions. Uh there's no question down there. I thought that we should, you know, obviously wave fair catch. Uh lesson learned, right? Young player trying to make a play. He got he's getting one opportunity and he's trying to take advantage of that. And I think that anytime you press or you try to make things happen, uh you can get in in into trouble. I always say let things happen for you, not to you. Uh so yeah, we got to be better down there. We got to always make sure that we end up that our offense has the ball at the end of the play. So, I asked you this may, but I'm going to ask you again now that you might have a better idea, and you probably talked a half about it. How much will Malik Washington's expected heavy snap count on offense affect your thinking in terms of how much you use them on returns? >> Guys, I'm going to I'm going to say the same thing that I said back in May. At the at the end of the day, I I understand everyone's workload. I'm I'm very well aware of it because that's how I have to craft our our our depth. Uh but at the same time, if a if a player is dynamic and have the can have the ball in his hands and can change a game, I don't I don't understand why you would want to have wouldn't want to do that. Now, are we trying to develop other guys? No question. And you have to have I always say I I always like to have a lot of horses in the stable. And uh so we're we're we're still trying to to get some more horses ready to go. Uh but he's a he's a dynamic player and uh you know, I'd hate to have a dynamic player sitting on the sidelines. Chris, we saw Harrison Bucker have a 69 yard field goal. Would you attempt Riley? Would you let Riley Patterson attempt that on Friday? How is that affect general strategy? >> I haven't I just I I don't know if it's going to be a trend. I mean, the situation was a trend for not a trend. It was what was it? 3 seconds left in the half. So, uh take a shot on goal, right? I mean, because it's going to be the final play of the half. I don't think you're going to attempt a 69yd field goal, obviously, uh in the in the middle of the game. Harrison Buckner, great leg and those type of things. I really like where Riley's at, you know, I mean, that ball he hit the other night, I mean, jumped off his foot. He's do he's been doing really well. So, uh, really pleased with where he's at. >> At the risk of sounding ridiculous, does Riley have the kicking job? >> I think No, I I will always say this. I think that they're all you're always competing and uh he knows that. Uh but ever since uh you know I I feel terrible for Zayn because Zayn was doing a really really good job. Uh but Riley has stepped up since then and and I really like where he's at. >> Chris, because the long distance accuracy has gotten so good and the kickers have gotten so good. Could you ever envision a a point where they take away the kicker's ability to work with the ball during the week or even narrow the goal post? >> I've thought about it. I would say this, the only position in the National Football League that people uh want to penalize for being really good, you know? I mean, it's almost if a the go, you know, golfers are really good at if they making long putts, you know, should we make a movable hole go around on the green, you know? You know what I mean? So, it's a I understand the question and I get it, but I I also want to defend those guys. They I don't think they should be penalized for getting really good at their craft. Chris, if I ask you which of your rookie draft picks you believe are going to be effective core special teams players in coverage. >> Who are the first couple names that come to mind? >> All of them. >> Oh boy. Okay. >> That's I'm sorry. They all have to be. That's just that's the world we're in, you know. So,

title: DL Jordan Phillips meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: How do you measure progress of the team nowadays? Is it joint practice, preseason games, uh intra squad practices out here? What what do you >> I mean, it's all about the process, you know? So, you know, it's not just about games, uh joint practices every day. You know what I'm saying? It's about, you know, how you retain information meeting rooms, how you're able to take that onto the field and translate it onto the field and how you're able to judge your effort, your physicality, and your fundamentals at the end of the day. And how I know physicality is a big thing with a how are you guys doing in that area do you think? >> Yeah I mean every day you know what I'm saying the goal is to be physical. You know this game is played physically. This game was not made for soft people. So that's always a point of emphasis you know when we take the field and you know we go against each other and try to get each other better. >> How much are you back in? >> Yeah he's great man. You know great leader um great player. You know what I'm saying? So absolutely excited and yeah. >> How different is he when he's in there as opposed to when he's like coach or not? >> Well, he's the same guy every day. You know what I'm saying? The same leader he is on the field is the same leader he is off the field. So, you know what I'm saying? When we come out, he'll be giving us pointers and things like that. So, he he's always been pretty good with that. >> This is always a difficult time at camp. You build relationship with guys around here. Just talk about guys that possibly might not be here. Okay. See, that was a lot. So, what was the first uh emphasis of that question? >> Guys that are going to get cut and the difficulty of you guys being friends and now they won't be here. They won't be here tomorrow or next week. >> Yeah. I mean, it's a brotherhood at the end of the day. You know what I'm saying? That don't just mean on the field, but also off the field. You know what I'm saying? We all have a great relationship with each other. We all keep in touch with each other. And, you know, unfortunately, that's part of the business, but we do have relationships with each other, and we build upon that. >> How do you approach the game on Saturday when you're not playing? Are you trying to younger guys. You try to be on defensive. What does it look like for you when you're not dressed for a game like that? >> Well, it's all about bringing the energy and motivating guys and helping guys get better and just continuing to bring the juice and helping them in any way I can help as as a fellow teammate >> to go too far back, but what did you take away from? >> Yeah, I mean that's a physical team, you know what I'm saying? And you know, got a lot of respect for them and their head coach and they did an amazing job getting us better. And you know what I'm saying? and we went out there, we competed with them and all in all it was a good day. We got better and they got better as well. >> Tell me about um DTackle group. It seems like y'all have some pretty good depth there with with you and KG and Zack. Um what what are you seeing with that group as far as pass rushing and stopping the run and that kind of stuff? >> Yeah, I mean every day we're always trying to get each other better. You know what I'm saying? We're a tight-knit group that takes coaching well and you know what I'm saying? We're going to continue to get better uh collectively. What what do y'all do best? Because it it seems like you guys are are pretty physical, pretty aggressive. What What do you guys do best, do you think? >> I mean, collectively as a group, like I said, we're focused on getting better and we're focused on taking the next step every day and we're we're we're focused on the process. The result is a side effect. >> Kind of going off of that, how good can this be overall? Feels like that's where the strength of this team lies right now. >> The sky's is the limit. You know, that's why we continue to come out here every day and get better. We go inside the meeting rooms and we take the coaching, you know what I'm saying? Focus on what it is we need to do to get better and we apply that when when it's time to uh get onto the field and we just focus on the process. >> I know it's not your side of the ball, but what was it like Chris Bell out there knowing what he's been through? >> Yeah, man. Chris, you know, he's a competitor, good player. He was a good player in college. He's a good player, you know, on this team and we're excited to have him back and see him out there compete. like we see you go up against a Brew every day the first reps of all once we have him. What's something you've taken away from Brew this summer that helped you get better? >> Yeah, I mean Brew is obviously a great player, you know, not only for this or organization, but all in all in the NFL. He's good. He's a great player. And you know, we focus on getting each other better each and every day. And you know what I'm saying? Like if it's something I need to work on, he tells me. If it's something he needs to work on, I tell him. And collectively, we're getting better, which will then help us help the organization better. Does his strength ever sneak up on you to know he's so quick off the football, but he's also a pretty strong player. Does that ever surprise you with other guys for the first time how strong he is? >> Yeah, Bruce's pretty strong. You know what I'm saying? Athletic. Like I said, he's a really good player in this league and for this organization.

title: EDGE Josh Uche meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: First let's start with the how this training camp has has gone for you. You're getting a lot of reps and and what do you think you can do >> Yeah, uh coach Haf's regime it's been a tough one, man. I mean, just instilling a new culture tough, detailed, and disciplined. And now it's been fun bonding with the guys, getting to know the young guys, the staff. They everyone's been great. And it's like family. >> What do you think the potential is of you and Antoine feeding off of each other? >> Sky's the limit. We just got to push each other, you know? Um we definitely feed off of each other and we bring different things to the table that's going to help the team win. >> You've been around a lot of NFL head coaches. With the way Haf has handled discipline, other aspects of being the job, what's your general perception of what kind of coach he's going to be? >> He's a detailed coach. Um an intense coach. You know, I mean, just like the expectation he has for us the inspiration that he gives to us, pregame speeches, the energy we all feed off of that. And um I think he's just like like all of us, the sky's the limit. And I know I'm bought in fully on what he has going on here. >> You're one of the veterans on this team. What's it like to lead such a young cast of players? >> Yeah. Nah, it's been it's been great. You know, especially with the coach like coach Haf, coach Clark. I mean, it's just that old school style of football, especially with coach Clark, man. Um I feel like he coaches the game the way it's supposed to be played. And we're building tough, detailed, and disciplined guys here. >> Being one of those veterans, what did it mean to you to have the day off in the preseason game where a lot of guys are fighting for a job, but you're one of the ones that I guess is kind of secure and where you stand? >> Nothing's ever secure, you know? I think um during that preseason game, just trying to help the guys, the younger guys with their detail and their operation, you know, trying to give some of the wisdom I've seen over my career. And just doing the best I can to be the best vet that I could be for the guys. And um everything is earned. Rent is due every day as everyone here knows. And just got to keep earning it each and every day. >> Do you want to play in that preseason finale this coming week? >> Listen, it's up to the coaches. It's whatever they want, you know what I mean? But um just doing whatever is asked of me, you know? >> How would it feel to be the first time you suit up and and play at Arrowhead Stadium, which is your hometown? >> Yeah. Yeah, I know. I'm excited, man, to be home. Again, like we talked a little bit about high school, you know, it's just seeing you. It's familiar faces and just to be back home with familiar faces and friends and just get to rep the city that raised me. >> You've been in that situation with a lot of young a lot of young players are in where they're nervous. This is the last week. They know cuts are coming. What do you advise them in terms of how to take mentally handle that? >> Be where your feet are. You know, um control the controllable. You can't control the past. You can't control the future. Just be where your feet are, you know, and um you'll end up where you're supposed to be. >> At this stage of your career, is there anything that you can pick up from coaches as far as pass rush moves? You've had a lot of sacks. You've had a ton of pressures in your career. Is there anything you can pick up or have picked up from a new set of coaching eyes? >> Always, man. Like that's the thing. Um I remember Patrick Chung when I was in New England told me, "Keep learning. When you stop learning is when you're dead." You know what I mean? So, you just got to keep learning every day. And Coach Clark has brought some really good things to my game, especially the bull rush series and stuff like that in hands. Um so, those are just a couple things that he's kind of like taught me, things that I didn't know before. >> I don't know if if you would even share it with us, but I am curious if you enter seasons with a sack number goal. >> No. Um just affect the game, affect the quarterback, and get to the quarterback, and stop the run, you know? So. >> How does a Joshua Uche of today compare to the kid who was last year when you were playing with the college football team >> Yeah, a lot more season, man. Um I've had experiences with blizzards and all types of weather conditions and things like that. Um but yeah, a lot of a lot more maturity under my belt, a lot more patience under my belt, uh a lot more wisdom. Um and so, just grateful to be here, playing the game that I love, man. It's just a blessing. >> It's a classic experience of classic combination of rain. >> Yeah. Exactly. The bipolarity of the city, you know? We got to love it, though. >> You've started some. You've come off the bench some in your career. Starting again, if it ends up that way as it seems it would, is that meaningful to you at the stage of your career to be an NFL starter? >> It's always meaningful. Anytime you're able to suit up for an NFL organization is meaningful, you know. Um they're putting their trust in you to go out there and represent the organization and put the best film, you know, possible out there for the fans to see. Put out the best product. >> How tough is this this part of the season where you know the business aspect comes in, you know, guys that might be here today might not be here tomorrow because obviously they're going to move on from you. >> Yeah. Uh it's a business, like you said. Um now I remember my dad I was talking to my dad about it a little bit and there's a African proverb that goes, "Soldier come, soldier go." So, you just got to keep going, you know. And um things change, but you got to be where your feet are and control the controllables. >> I'm wondering what's your impression of the rookies. I'm not seeing a lot of them. I'm wondering if anyone else is standing out. >> Yeah, Max has a high motor, high effort. Um just the details Coach Clark is definitely on top of them and I'm liking the progress I'm seeing out of them, especially with Coach Clark kind of just, you know, stilling that discipline and and and that dolphin mentality into them. >> I have a very random question. I see that kickers now make 69, 70-yard field goals and I've been thinking about how it changes end-of-game situations in in like the last 2 years especially. What have you noticed since you entered the league? It seems to me like a touchback starts at the 35. Team could get the ball trailing by six with 20 seconds left, complete one pass and they're in field goal range. >> Yeah. >> Have you thought about this and have you seen it perhaps change defense mentality and strategy at the end of half and games? >> Definitely. I think amongst everything you said, the the more important part is the special teams part. Like you said, if you get a touchback you're starting at the 35, so you want to keep that ball in play. Stop them around the 20. Stop them at the 20, you've got more real estate to work with as a defense. Get them down, have to punt. So, I think special teams is the most important factor in that situation right there. >> Mhm.

title: ILB Jackson Woodard meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Made a great play. I think several, but definitely the one that stood out was a fumble recovery creating a turnover. What did it feel like just doing that at that stadium and then also having the whole sideline come over and and celebrate with you afterwards. A lot of starters there, too. >> Yeah, that was a lot of fun. Obviously, I want to first start with just thanking my Lord and Savior Jesus Christ for another day. He's blessed me with so much, but yeah, that play in particular, I think the whole defense was doing their job. Um and we took advantage of um what they had done, which is put the ball on the ground. I found my way to the ball, jumped on it, um which is a huge play. Like turnovers win ball games. Um we got to get more of them as defense. But that was a lot of fun. Like Hard Rock Stadium is a fun place to play. I thought the fans brought a lot of good energy. Um and so that was a big play. And then, like you said, all the defense coming over celebrating the play. Um that was fun, man. That's what it's about. >> You played plenty in the preseason game. I know Coach Hafley wanted to to kind of switch up speeds. The guys who played a lot didn't get too many reps, but you also got a lot of reps >> today, so can you talk about the >> Yeah. Um been putting in a lot of work. I mean, that's what training camp is. Like these are the dog days. Like we get limited reps in the season where you got full pads on. So, like we want to take advantage of those. You got athletes just constantly been talking about like this is like we want to see improvement. Like the daily daily daily um improvement is what we're worried about. Like process over results. And so, as many reps and opportunities as I can get on the field, one just building like trust with the teammates, but also um furthering my football IQ. Like I'm going to take those. Um and I've been grateful to get those reps. >> Beyond the general thing of building football IQ and trust, what else do you think you need to do to establish yourself as an NFL player long-term as opposed to guys on the bubble? >> Yeah, for sure. I mean, I think when I look at like my game, I want to fix so many things. Like I want to improve in so many things, whether it's footwork, eyes, hands, communication. Um I think I can get better in so many ways. Um And so, I think like um if you're asking for one thing, I think my coverage should get better, you know? That's something that is a little different in NFL. Like the quarterbacks are a lot better, a lot quicker. Um and so, I just got to quicken my um mind, legs, feet um when when you're getting into the uh the coverage reps. Um and I think that'll help me. But a lot of it's just doing what the coaches ask, you know? Like these coaches are really good coaches. They're in the NFL for a reason. They got you in the position um where you're going to make plays. And so, for me, that's all I got to do is just do what they ask um and then the plays will come, and hopefully my career, Lord willing, will um continue and flourish. >> You got a lot of guys that are battling for roster spots this final week >> Yeah. >> before roster cuts. Can you just kind of detail what what that's like going through this competition this final week before the preseason finale? >> Yeah, I mean, I look at it as like Listen, how many guys we got? 90 guys? Like we're a team. Like we come in every day and it's it's us coming out here competing as a team. The front office, they all deal with that. So, that's out of our control. So, we come in, bust our tails, um and compete as a team. And when that day comes, that day comes, but we're not really focused on that, like this is once-in-a-lifetime. My linebacker coach Joe Barry was just talking about it. Like we're in the one of 1%, you know? So, we're just blessed to be here um and then to just take advantage of of the opportunity that we have as a team, cultivating the brotherhood, the friendships, um and then let the front office and and and everyone else handle all that. >> Do you feel good about where you stand? >> For sure, man. Yeah. Um I just come to compete, man. The Lord's blessed me. Like I said, like I look at everything as a blessing, you know? Like being able to talk to y'all, what a blessing. Like being able to practice out here, what a blessing. Whenever you look at everything with just like, man, this is a blessing. Like you're going to go take advantage of that. You're going to go do it with everything you have. Um and so I'm just blessed to be here. I feel good. I love my teammates. Um and yeah, I'm just blessed, man. >> Is it going to be a blessing to talk to you? >> Thank you, man. Thank you. >> you think stress, anxiety, stomach in knots at any point over the next week when you get to Saturday, Sunday? >> You know, if it was last year, yeah. You know, just cuz I I think rookie year you come in and you there's a lot of unknowns. Um but I've talked to y'all about it just here and then um in the media before like once I figured out what mattered in life and like what my real purpose on this earth is to love on others, you know, to build others up, to to further the kingdom of God, like everything else just kind of fell in place. Like now I know that I'm here to to help others. I'm here to be a blessing. and so it kind of just you know, gave me a ultimate peace of like this is my job. This is what I'm here for to to do, but but it's not my purpose. Like this is this is my job, not my purpose. And so with that, like whatever happens, like I'm blessed. Like I keep saying and I hate to keep saying I'm blessed, but that's true. So no, I'll I'll be at peace and um like I said, I'm just excited to um compete and then we got a big opportunity coming this week, you know. Friday's going to be a big game. A lot of us are going to get the opportunity to go play ball. So uh I'm just excited, man.

title: TE Greg Dulcich meets with the media | Miami Dolphins

So, we're excited to, you know, have him moving around and, you know, progressing. So. >> Ricky, how how long does it take a quarterback and a tight end to get a relationship going because you and Malik this is obviously new. Uh how is it going and how long do you think it will take to get there? >> Yeah, I think it's going well. Um he's he's a he's a great leader on the offense and on the team. So, he's a dude that, uh you know, is very approachable for, you know, all the, uh you know, offensive skill guys. He gets with all of us, which is cool. Uh he makes sure, you know, we're all on the same page. He does a great job with the tight ends. So, it's uh it's going to be fun. >> I know it was brief for today, but it looked like the offense was hitting stuff on the drive getting the ball out. Is that what you saw out there? Was that kind of intentional for today? >> Yeah. Yeah, it was a good day. Uh yeah, tried to, you know, had the day off yesterday and just try to get moving around and, uh you know, play with intent. So, I thought uh we did a good job with that. >> Hate to go back too far, but what were your thoughts on the joint practice against the Giants? >> Yeah, thought we played physical. That's kind of what those uh those are really about is, you know, hitting somebody else. Um and and and the attitude that goes with that. So, I thought we did a good job with that. Um yeah. >> This time of the season obviously is very tough for many of us. Business aspect comes in. You know, cuts are coming up. How do you guys approach that, you know, building relationships with guys that they might not be here? >> Yeah, it's it's tough because, like you said, you you build relationships with everyone. Um and what's cool, we got a close-knit team. Um and, you know, we're all excited about each other's success and uh you know, we want everyone to be here. Um we want all of us to contribute to this thing and, um you know, you only have a certain number of spots. So, everyone uh it's it's a matter of, you know, putting your best foot forward, competing, and, uh you know, leaving it all out there. >> Okay, what's the potential of the trio of rookie receivers, do you think? >> I think they're awesome. Yeah, they've done a great job, you know, since OTAs, training camp. Um I think uh each of them got very bright future, so I'm excited. >> What's it been like being the old head in the tight end room? >> It's crazy, yeah. I know, yeah. 26 and the old head is pretty insane, but you know, I'm Cole is Cole's right there with me and uh No, it's cool cuz you kind of you know, only a short time ago I was you know, just like the rookies, you know, trying to figure things out and you know, the league is is a very different game than college football is. And they're taking things, you know, absolutely in stride. They're doing a great job. I think that when you think of my time in Chicago, I think of Anthony Miller rookie year. He had a phenomenal rookie season. You know, I think of I think of Tariq Cohen's ability to be unlocked. I remember us playing against the Giants at Metife and I think Tariq Cohen had 170 yards and he was a running back. We had a game plan, but we knew when we would get Landon Collins matched up on Tariq Cohen, we had a whole bag of different route concepts that could change and that could audible on the fly if we see him come down to the box and knowing he's going to kind of be the the matchup or the man-to-man defender on Tariq Cohen coming out of the back field. We could get to out and ups. We could get to angle Texas routes. We could get to Reed routes on the fly with Tariq Cohen as we're seeing those things as we're predicting in practice. It'll be twoon two between myself and the corner and Landon Collins and Tariq Cohen and we can kind of play those matchups in that game as far as creating those one-on- ones for myself and Tariq and ultimately we lost that game in overtime, but that's an example of how we were able to take advantage of that matchup and Tariq Cohen had a phenomenal game. >> Love it. Obviously, he's not Travis Kelce, but I'm a big fan of Isaiah Likely and the plays he's made over his career, not just catching the ball, but also being a tight end that can have a lot of catch and run opportunities as well. title: Kellen Moore recaps Day 16 | Saints Training Camp 2026
text: All right. I think you guys probably got the news as far as the moves. Raheem going to IR, signing Daniel Carlson, and then the the trade with Deion for Samir. So, um you know, a couple moves there as we eyes forward. And then, you know, today we had kind of a hybrid walk-through day with a little bit of fundamentals and individual full speed. Just get our guys legs going back after, you know, the trip with some really good joint practices, a game, all that good stuff. And so, um you know, guys will be ready to go. And then, we'll get back into it tomorrow with a full speed practice, which should be good. So, open up questions. >> Have you already made a decision about whether or not starters are expected to play this week? >> We're going to work through it. Haven't made total decision yet. So, um you know, today was kind of a day to kind of rejuvenate these guys a little bit after a really good week. And then, um and then we'll kind of see where we're at tomorrow. >> What went into the decision to bring in another kicker? >> Yeah, just, you know, Daniel's a really talented kicker. He's He's had a lot of success in this league. And, you know, feel like there's there's worthy opportunities there for for a competition. Get him involved here. We'll you anticipate trying to kick here in 2 days on Wednesday. And we'll go from there. >> Do you plan to carry three kickers into this preseason game? Or do you even want >> Yes. Yes, as of right now, three. >> Uh with the trade for a running back, does that mean Devine Ozigbo could go on IR? >> We have a few guys that are kind of dealing with some injury stuff and some maintenance. And so, you know, Devine obviously um he came up with the hamstring in the game. So, that'll be time lost to some degree as they collect more information. Um you know, Samir's obviously played play a lot of football in this league. And so, we feel fortunate to be able uh get him. >> What is You mentioned how much football Samir's played. What do you like about him and how he fits in this offense? What can he bring? >> Yeah, I think, you know, he's done a nice job in this league. Um you know, going back to college as well. And just watching his preseason film, I think this will be a smooth transition. This is really hard for a guy like him to hop in here, you know, midweek. And you know, with the you know, trying to give yourself as much of an opportunity for Friday. And so, I feel like the transition will be pretty smooth as far as, you know, what he was being asked to do, um, you know, the last few weeks. >> Kellen, uh What did you like about C.J. Donaldson the other night? And, uh, is he the kind of guy who you definitely need to see in this live action and in the >> I'm excited to see C.J. more and more. He's, um, had some good exposure so far through preseason for us. I think credit him. He's been always really well prepared. Um, he knows what he's doing. He brings value on special teams. Um, he's done a nice job for us. And so, um, he'll certainly have some opportunities on Friday. >> Are you all still at 90? >> I think we're technically, uh 91 just cuz of, uh, Charlie's technically viewed as an international player. So. >> Does that carry over to the regular season again? >> From a practice squad, you can have the international spot, but not, obviously, in the reg the regular roster. >> Kellen, you mentioned, uh, White's experience in the league. What do you like about Demonte? >> Yeah, I think good vertical 1/runner. Um, you know, I think from an from a zone standpoint, he'll transition really well here. What he was being asked to do in San Francisco will transition well here. And so, I feel like it'll give him an opportunity to compete on Friday. And, um, you know, it'll be good. >> Any of the other injuries from, like, Saturday's game week-to-week on any of them? Like, Brian Allen Styles or Mike Allen? >> Yeah, I mean, we're kind of we we got a healthy dose here. Um, Lorenzo will be time loss. Uh, we'll see how that progresses as we go. And so, um, there'll be a few others, you know, Maliek and Ty. Chandler will have some time loss. So, we'll gather some information on those guys. >> Is All right, is Maliek's like a ACL or anything or >> It's a knee. Gathering more information. >> Okay. Kellen, now, do you I mean, obviously, you guys have been looking into acquiring kickers at a couple different times at different stages this offseason. What was Was Daniel Carlson Carlson always available? Is there a reason why he didn't sign with any team until this time that that you're aware of? >> I I don't know him on a personal level as far as, you know, his preference. I know there's been dialogue throughout the throughout the off-season with him. Um you know, obviously we we've seen his career and the success he's had in uh you know, Las Vegas and he's he's been a really good kicker in this league and so uh feel like this will be a good opportunity for him. >> Was was your approach and philosophy that you wanted to try to identify a younger developmental kicker before you wanted to to turn to a veteran? >> You know, we felt good about where we're at uh with those two young guys. I think just we feel like at this time, you know, adding a third third guy is going to be valuable for us and we'll just let the next few days take its course. We'll have a uh really good day on Wednesday with kicking at practice and then uh transition into the Friday game. >> Kellen, you were a former college football star. Have you been paying attention to kind of everything that's been going on with rookies possibly leaving the NFL and going back to college football? And kind of what's your overall thoughts on that situation? >> Yeah. Uh I just think it's unfortunate there's no uh regulation anything right now. Uh obviously my brother coaches college football uh so I get to kind of follow closely from a fan perspective just watching uh everything that college football is going through and so uh um you know, I I think for it's a balancing act. Obviously, you want as many opportunities for all these guys at the same time there's kids that just work their tail off all off-season and all season long and uh you know, they have to make decisions on their roster now because of added players and so I think there's a challenging balancing act to this and hopefully hopefully there can be some leadership and some regulations developed here shortly. >> Just to clarify, when you say time lost for injuries like that is that more on the serious side? >> Did that come up with Harris at all? Whenever he left the roster or he was waived. Like was that a conversation that about him going back to >> I was I was asked about him. No. >> He actually just committed to LSU so like is there >> [laughter] >> I don't know. Yeah, I missed I missed that one so um yeah. >> Like from your experience with him just as a as a player >> Yeah, obviously we were in a unique situation with him. He was coming off of an injury and so he never made it to the field with us. We spent some time with them and obviously made a transaction that you know, we felt like we needed to make. >> Did you ever think you'd hear that guy that was on your team going to college? >> No. >> It's a unique unique college football world we live in right now. >> 48 hours later is there anything about Saturday you feel better about? >> I think from the on-field production, you know, when you take the emotions out of it, you know, there's obviously going to be individualized you know, plays that you feel good about maybe player performances that you feel good about collectively it's it's not at all close to what we want. Um you know, and so it's going to be a great lesson for us, you know, all those lessons the twos twos and threes had in that game the ones get to learn certainly today. We spent a lot of time on that. Um but I felt like it was a really good week overall, you know, unfortunately we did not end the week you know, the way we wanted to, you know, and that's that's there's no exceptions or excuses for that. Uh if you watch those films, um it's as good of work as you're going to get in August. You know, those three days I thought that was excellent against three really good teams, high-quality teams uh with different styles, different approaches, and so I think we got exposed to a lot of football, which was great. Now it puts us in a position to have a great week this week. We'll see what happens and make a decision here in the next day or two. >> Mike, before the Cardinals coach was saying that there was a presentation at owners meetings and the like the health science of joint practices versus preseason games and if you have joint practices or just in the reps, like did anything stand out to you about that or do you what do you remember from that at all? >> I'd just say it it continues to add context to what the joint practices are, which is really valuable opportunities for for starters to play very meaningful snaps and then it backed up as far as uh the value of that for those guys. You know, that if they get enough reps in those, you're getting the equivalent of what they would get if they had to go in a preseason game in somewhat of a controlled environment and so um again, I feel like we got some really good work. These joint practices are awesome awesome opportunities for us, I think. Um you know, for the players, from a scheme standpoint, you get to test your test yourself. Um you know, you get to do some things in those joint practices maybe you don't always do and um you know, I know there's a lot about an unfortunate, you know, some fights in in the Dallas one, which is obviously an unfortunate part. No one wants that. But collectively, um there was really good work. That's as good of work as we can possibly get in August. >> Have you had that talk with the league about the appeal? Is there any update on that? >> No update. >> What's Oscar dealt with in practice? >> Um Oscar, he's just working through a hamstring. >> Is there any concern at this point about the the number of injuries? Does it make it difficult to kind of like design a plan when there's that many players out there? >> That's part of the journey you're on in the NFL and inevitably you're going to have to juggle some some medical things and that's just part of this. You know, our guys have got to be be able to adjust and that's part of that's going to happen in season. You're going to have to adjust your scheme, adjust your rotations and so, you know, I feel like we have a great group. They they've been working their tails off and you know, we'll have plenty of opportunities this week to prepare. >> I counted I think it was 22 total players today that were either not present or that were kind of working off to the side. Is that more of a display of like caution [clears throat] in terms of the bumps and bruises or is there a bigger concern? >> There's a lot of variables probably within those 22 guys. I don't know the exact number. >> It's our last injury question. There's a lot of them. So. >> With the tape, I mean, how how do you assess the quarterback play from Saturday? >> Yeah, we just didn't get in any rhythm. They've done a really good job. Um think the world of both of those guys. They're they're big-time quarterbacks and so we'll let those guys keep competing, but they're in a good place. >> I think after the game Spencer said he felt like he operated a little more free in that game. He said he felt like a little too safe maybe in the opener. Did you see that? >> Yeah, I think I think everyone's going to kind of self-correct every single week and find different opportunities that they can get better. I think they're both playing some good football. You know, you go look at those two joint practices and for people who are able to view those, I felt like their performances were really steady and they did a really good job. >> Is Chris Rock close to returning to practice tomorrow? >> Uh, we'll see. Yeah, he's he's progressing well though.

I I say one series at most and get them out of there. Um I'm I'm kind of old school. I guess you I I just kind of believe in that that dress rehearsal idea, but they have gotten enough work in these joint practices that I probably feel okay about it. And the the level of injury right now does have me a bit concerned about where they're at. Um, you know, the Rams basically don't do anything in the preseason and they win all kinds of games. And I guess, you know, if that's the blueprint, it's fine. Like, if as long as it works, as long as you're ready to go for the season, you just got to make sure you've gotten enough work in to be ready for that stuff. It's just the world has changed, man. Like we were talking about this on uh I I do this this show with uh Ryan Paganetti. The um and the playlist is on our our YouTube page, the off YouTube page. You can find it there. That playlist will take you over there. And you know, we just talk about analytics and trends in the league and stuff like that. And you know, he made the point today that Tom Brady recently did an interview where he was talking about how in the third quarter of a preseason game, he threw a pass to Randy Moss. That's inconceivable in in today's NFL. like nobody's playing their starters into the third quarter and I just think people have changed their thinking on that and there's more than one way to do it. So if they wanted to shut them down that's fine. Like I'm always okay with any idea of how you approach basically just about anything but you got to have a plan and it has to work. Like that's the whole thing. I'm cool with trying anything. Look, McVey and them don't even go to the combine. Their teams win games. Fine with me. They find Puka. Fine with me. Like do whatever you want. Just have a process that works. But, you know, performative stuff, whatever. Like, I don't think you have to do that anymore. Just be right when you don't do the things that people conceive as as norms. You know, if you're going to be the Browns and you're going to go all in on the Moneyball aspect of things, it has to work. Or you're open for criticism. So, if they don't want to play these guys, that's cool with me. I wouldn't even criticize it. Even if they aren't, like, I don't think a series, oh no, they didn't touch the field. Like I don't think a series is even going to make a huge difference against Detroit. Like at this point, you basically got to have gotten enough working in these joint practices to feel good about where you're at. Stay sharp. My main thing is is just get healthy, man. Like this is scary right now. The number of injuries around this team. Get that under control. To me, that's way more important than anything else. Um keep everybody upright. Get to the season. Get rolling. Get going. As I'm talking through this, man, shut it down. Like I don't even need to see them. Like shut it down. I'm I'm scared of the injury bug right now. Um so yeah, that's going to do it for today's show. I appreciate you guys for watching. We'll talk to you next time.

title: Saints HC Kellen Moore on trip to California, updates injuries and looks ahead to preseason finale
text: It's >> [laughter] >> All right. You guys good? All right. I think you guys probably got the news as far as the moves. Uh Ray-Ray going to IR, signing Daniel uh Carlson, and then the the trade with Deion for uh Samir. So, um you know, a couple moves there as we uh eyes forward, and then um you know, today we had kind of a hybrid walk-through uh day with a little bit of fundamentals and individual at full speed. Um just got our guys legs kind of back after uh you know, the trip with uh some really good joint practices, a game, all that good stuff. And so, um you know, guys will be ready to go, and then we'll get back into it tomorrow with uh a full-speed practice, which should be good. So, open up questions. >> Have you already made a decision about uh whether or not starters are expected to play this week? >> We're going to work through it. Haven't made total decision yet, so um you know, today was kind of a day to kind of rejuvenate these guys a little bit after a really good week, and then uh and then we'll kind of see where we're at tomorrow. >> What went into the decision to bring in another kicker? >> Yeah, just you know, Daniel's a really talented kicker. He's um he's had a lot of success in this league, and um you know, feel like there's there's worthy opportunities there for for a competition, get him in involved here. We'll um you know, anticipate trying to kick here in uh 2 days on Wednesday, and um we'll go from there. >> Do you plan to carry three kickers into this preseason game, or do you even want >> Yes. Yes, as of right now, three. >> Uh with the trade for a running back, does that mean Devine Ozigbo could go on IR? >> We have a few guys that are kind of dealing with some injury stuff uh and some maintenance, and so, you know, Devine obviously um he came up with the hamstring in the game, so that'll be time lost to some degree as they collect more information, and um you know, Samir's obviously played played a lot of football in this league, and so we feel fortunate to be able uh get him. >> What is um you mentioned how much football Samir's played. What do you like about him and how he fits in this offense and brings to it? >> Yeah, I think you know, he he's done a nice job in this league. Um you know, going back to college as well and uh just watching his preseason film, I think this will be a smooth transition. This is really hard for a guy like him to hop in here, you know, midweek and you know, with the you know, trying to give yourself as much of an opportunity for Friday and so feel like the transition will be pretty smooth as far as, you know, what he was being asked to do um you know, the last few weeks. >> What did you like about C.J. Donaldson the other night and uh is he the kind of guy who you definitely need to see live action >> Yeah, I'm excited to see C.J. more and more. He's um had some good exposure so far through preseason for us. I think credit him, he's been always really well prepared. Um he knows what he's doing. He brings value on special teams. He's a good vertical one slash runner. Um you know, I think from an from a zone standpoint, he'll transition really well here. What he was being asked to do in San Francisco will transition well here and so feel like it'll give him an opportunity to compete on Friday and um you know, it'll be good. >> Any other injuries from Saturday's game? Week to week on any of them with Lorenzo Styles or what not? >> Yeah, I mean, we're kind of we we got a healthy dose here. Um Lorenzo will be time loss. Uh we'll see how that progresses as we go and so uh there'll be a few others, you know, Maliek and Ty. Chandler will have some time loss so we'll gather some information on those guys. >> All right, is Maliek's like a ACL thing or >> It's a knee. Gathering more information. >> Okay. Kellen, now I mean, obviously you guys have been looking into acquiring kickers a couple different times at different stages this offseason. Was Was Daniel Carlson Carlson always available? Is there a reason why he didn't sign with any team until this time that that you're aware of? >> I I don't know him on a personal level as far as, you know, his preference. I know there's been dialogue throughout the throughout the offseason with him. You know, obviously we've we've seen his career and the success he's had in uh you know, Las Vegas and he's he's been a really good kicker in in league and so uh I like this would be a good opportunity for him. >> Was was your approach and philosophy that you wanted to try to identify a younger developmental kicker before you wanted to to turn to a veteran or >> You know, we felt good about where we're at uh with those two young guys. I think just we feel like at this time, you know, adding a third third guy is going to be valuable for us, and we'll just let the next few days take its course. We'll have a uh really good day on Wednesday with kicking at practice, and then uh transition that to the Friday game. >> Kellen, you were a former college football star. Have you been paying attention to kind of everything that's been going on with rookies possibly leaving the NFL and going back to college football? What's what's your overall thoughts on that situation? >> Yeah. Uh um I just think it's unfortunate there's no regulation to anything right now. Uh obviously my brother coaches college football, uh so I get to kind of follow closely from a fan perspective just watching uh everything that college football is going through, and so, um you know, I I think for it's a balancing act. Obviously, you want as many opportunities for all these guys. At the same time, there's kids that just work their tail off all off season and all season long, and uh you know, they have to make decisions on their roster now because of added players, and so, I think there's a challenging balancing act to this, and hopefully hopefully there can be some leadership and some regulations developed here shortly. >> Just to clarify, when you say time lost for injuries, like that is that more on the serious side? >> Yeah. >> Did that come up with Harris at all? Whenever he left the roster or he was waived, like was that a conversation that that went on there? >> I was I was able to No. >> He actually just committed to LSU, so like is there >> I don't know. Yeah, I missed I missed that one, so um yeah. >> like from your experience with him just as a as a player >> Yeah, obviously we we were in a unique situation with him. He was coming off of an injury, and so, he never made it to the field with us. We spent some time with him, and um obviously made a transaction that, you know, we felt like we needed to make. >> Did you ever think you'd hear that that a guy that was on your team in college? >> No. >> It's a unique unique uh college football world we live in right now. >> 48 hours later, is there anything about Saturday you feel better about? >> I think from the on-field production, you know, when you take the emotions out of it, you know, there's obviously going to be individualized um you know, plays that you feel good about, maybe player performances that you feel good about. Collectively, it's it's not at all close to what we want. Um you know, and so it's going to be a great lesson for us, you know. Uh all those lessons the twos twos and threes had in that game, the ones get to learn uh certainly today. We spent a lot of time on that. Um but I felt like it was a really good week overall, you know. Unfortunately, we did not end the week, you know, the way we wanted to, you know, and that's that's there's no exceptions or excuses for that. Um but I felt like overall it was a good week. >> Kevin, I'm sure you guys are way factors like at at some point in a game. >> I really felt like the focus was those joint practices were going to be uh a great opportunity for us, um you know, as well as those, you know, first two preseason games. I felt like, you know, the Jacksonville one, I felt like we had some really good work and we had good work in this one. We just didn't play well enough. Uh and coached well enough really at all. And so, um it puts us in a position to evaluate our team and we'll see it we'll see what suits us best for Friday. And so, you know, tomorrow we'll have a really good practice and we'll kind of evaluate from there where our roster's at, where our health's at, and make a decision from that standpoint. >> What's your philosophy on I mean, you know, certain players like that in live tackling situations, full pads, like you you think it like is not necessary you know, necessarily if you can get the work in other ways? >> Yeah, I thought we got great work with all three joint practices. Uh if you watch those films, um it's as good of work as you're going to get in August. You know, those three days, I thought that was excellent uh against three really good teams, high-quality teams, um with different styles, different approaches. And so, I think we got exposed to a lot of football, which was great. Now, it puts us in a position to have a great week this week. We'll see what happens and make a decision here in the next day or two. >> Like before, the Cardinals coach was saying that there was a presentation at owners meetings and like the health science of joint practices versus preseason games and if you have joint practices, you're adjusting your reps. Like did anything stand out to you about that or do you what do you remember from that at all? >> I just say it continues to add context to what the joint practices are, which is really valuable opportunities for for starters to play very meaningful snaps and backed up as far as the value of that for those guys. You know, that if they get enough reps in those you're getting the equivalent of what they would get if they had to go in a preseason game in somewhat of a controlled environment and so um again, I feel like we got some really good work. These joint practices are awesome awesome opportunities for us, I think. Um you know, for the players from a scheme standpoint, it's for us, I think. You know, for the players from a scheme standpoint, you get to test your test yourself. Um you know, you get to do some things in those joint practices maybe you don't always do. And um you know, I know there's a lot about an unfortunate, you know, some fights in in the Dallas one, which is obviously unfortunate part. No one wants that. But collectively um there was really good work. That's as good of work as we can possibly get in August. >> Have you had that talk with the league about the appeal? Is there any update on that? >> No update. >> What's Oscar Dahl doing there? >> Um Oscar, he's just working through a hamstring. >> Is there any concern at this point about the the number of injuries? Does it make it difficult to kind of like design a plan when there's that many to face out there? >> That's part of the journey you're on in the NFL and inevitably you're going to juggle some some medical things and that's just part of this. Um you know, our guys got to be be able to adjust and that's part of that's going to happen in season. You're going to have to adjust your scheme, adjust uh your rotations and so you know, I feel like we have a great group. They they've been working their tails off and uh you know, we'll have we'll have plenty of opportunities this week to prepare. >> I counted I think it was 22 total players today that were either not present or that were kind of working off to the side. Is that more of a display of like caution in terms of the Buccaneers or is there a bigger concern? >> There's a lot of variables probably within those 22 guys. There's going to be some guys obviously that we know that are hurt right now that aren't able to participate and you know, they got a little bit of a road to go. Um and then there's some guys that are just in maintenance programs where you know, we're trying to get some some guys' bodies back and ready to go for uh you know, what Friday's going to be. >> With Brezhon, is there a hip injury that he >> suffered and will he have surgery or anything? >> Um yes. >> Not to delve beyond but we have these two preseason games under your belt. What's your confidence level with the linebacker room? >> They're doing a really nice job. Um you know, I thought you know, when you when Jordan or excuse me, not Jordan, Jalen uh Jalen and Isaiah and uh Jackson, you know, even Dion before we traded him, you know, those guys got a ton of reps and they get to lead the charge too which I think is awesome. You know, like Jalen's the green dot. He's getting the play call and he's communicating to the whole group and I thought there were some really good examples of him taking charge of that which was excellent. >> How much has that kind of helped to separate Jalen a a little bit cuz you know, he obviously in college when he wasn't a green dot guy or that system wasn't any of that. How have you seen him kind of grow into that? >> Yeah, anyone who hasn't been a part of it, there's a you know, an acclimation period. Most of the time those guys call it anyways. It's just whether you're getting it from, you know, a signal from the sideline or obviously in the earpiece and so um I think in general our linebacker room's done a really good job of just, you know, they're in the middle of it all. So they got to communicate to everyone. >> Has pretty much has almost everybody in the linebacker room gotten the opportunity to work with that? >> Probably close. Uh I don't know the exact number. >> Sorry for the last picture question. There was a lot of lot of them. What did you say Ty Chandler was doing with >> Ty Chandler has a knee. >> Is that a long-term >> Potential long-term time loss. We'll see. >> You said Neil's potential long-term? Um gathering more information on that one. Devin, um Yes. Yeah, we'll just talk through it. There's there's plenty of vari- variables we can talk through and discuss. Um again, I'm really I want to have a really good practice tomorrow. That was kind of the intent of today, set us up for a really good practice, and then after that we'll kind of have some uh good decision discussions on what the rest of week looks like. So. Yeah, we just didn't get in any rhythm. Uh those guys, you know, I know we can look at it from one preseason game, we can look at it collectively from an entire Uh I like the progress uh Zach and Spence have both made. They've done a really good job. Um think the world of both of those guys. They're they're big-time quarterbacks, and so we'll just have those guys keep competing, but they're in a good place. Yeah, I think I think everyone's going to kind of self-correct every single week and find different opportunities that they can get better. I think they're both playing some good football. You know, you got to look at those two joint practices, and for people who are able to view those, I felt like their performances were really steady, and they did a really good job. Uh we'll see. Yeah, he's he's progressing well, though.

title: Saints LB Kaden Elliss on starters playing in preseason, linebacker unit & Brandon Staley's scheme
text: Good, how are you guys today? >> Can you take us through the the busy weekend in LA and >> Yeah. Yeah, you know it's a awesome place out there. It was fun to to head out there for a little bit. We uh took off on a Monday, I believe. I had a joint practice Tuesday versus Cowboys. Um you know, walk-throughs and stuff on Wednesday, try to get the body right cuz then another joint practice Thursday with the Rams and and a day off and then game time. Um so it was a it was a busy week but it was very productive. >> How did the What did you feel that you all could take away from those joint practices and kind of the unique opportunity that it that it brought? >> Yeah, you know um very good teams that we went up against. Um you know, the Cowboys are uh pretty well known for their offense as of last year. They had you know, number one in a lot of metrics. Um so it was good to get to go up against them and then we got to go up against, you know, a lot of the I mean, Vegas is number one odds on the Super Bowl with LA. Um so I think it was a really good uh measuring sticks to you know, measure yourself by and what this team's made of. Um really proud of the work we put in and the way we competed. >> The measuring sticks said >> I think we're we're building the right way. >> Um What were your impressions of Chase Young before you arrived here and now being around him? You know, how has that changed or might a greater appreciation for >> Yeah, um you know, obviously such a high draft pick. Uh you know, from afar, um you always tend to you know, watch how that goes and you know, defensive rookie of the year. I seen the success he had over there with the uh Redskins Commanders. Um and then you know, I I didn't know him before that. Um I had I had known teammates that had played with him and they all said they loved him. Um then getting here, it's it's been pretty cool getting to see really what he did last year from a more in-depth lens, from a you know, behind the scenes lens. And And also getting to be his teammate, seeing how dominant he is, playing play out, the energy he brings every day, the leadership he displays. He's a special person, a special player, and it's been pretty fun playing with him so far. I'm excited to do it for real on Sundays. >> How is he as a trash talker compared to maybe some of the other >> [laughter] >> You know, he he he he does just fine in that category. We'll we'll leave it at that. >> You mentioned the measuring stick with the joint practices. And there's obviously like change of thought on are the joint practices more valuable? Do you need to play in a preseason game? Do you feel like as starters you want to play in this final preseason game against the Cowboys, or do you feel like the work that you were able to see in the joint practices is enough? >> Yep. Look, I think as long as your team approaches it the right way, and and you know, the mission is clear, the culture is clear, and the plan is clear, I really think you can make arguments all directions. I When I first got in the NFL and I was with Sean Payton on very successful teams, it was the old school ramp up, you know, drive a quarter, a half, and then the fourth game they sat, right? The starters. I And we were successful. I've been in where we played a little bit of the first game, and we came out rolling that year. And in Atlanta, I was in uh last 2 years where, you know, we didn't play in any. And again, one of the years we we started off hot. So I don't And then now I'm here with this uh coaching staff, and you know, they're they're talking about the plan, what they're going to do. Like, I think as long as you have the right guys, I think that's what's more important, the culture, uh the buy-in to the the coaches and what what they're preaching. Um cuz I I mean, you look around the league and you've seen Tomlin, Harbaugh, all these guys that have had more success than almost anybody in the NFL, and you know, they're going for it, and they're out there. And then you see people like McVay and the Rams who are also as successful as anybody out there, and they're not playing any of them. So to me, it's really about the buy-in and the culture, uh what your coaches are selling you, and um do you have the right culture for the players to pick it up and then run with it. >> Going back to your point, what's your thoughts about Jaylen Ford's progression in the South Carolina >> Yeah, he's Oh, it's it's been really cool to see, you know, um I didn't know Jacob before coming here, but he's someone that stood out right away. He's a um extremely athletic and intelligent linebacker. He plays the right way, and him going out there and just making these plays is been really special to watch, and uh he's only going to continue to ascend. >> Similar question. >> Go ahead, now. >> [clears throat] >> Similar question, but just on Isaiah. Uh you know, he had a really specific role last year, and now it seems that, you know, he's kind of fitting in a couple different places. What's kind of stood out to you about that? >> Yeah, he's another guy that you mean you see why he was playing in in that role last year, cuz he's so explosive. He can cover, he can blitz. Uh he's he's a really great athlete, and so seeing, you know, I wasn't here last year, but seeing the linebacker he is right now, it's it's really cool to see him going out there making plays as well, and um continuing to show that, you know, he can play every down. >> Despite the recent transaction, what is your uh confidence level with the linebacking group? >> Uh very high. This is a a extremely good group. I think it's a awesome mix of um some veterans and and then some some young guys that are out there and that are hungry, and um this linebacker group I think can uh be a driving force to this team. what you're talking about before with the maybe there isn't a correlation between how you play in the first season. You've been in situations where you have started fast, it's been like an emphasis this off season of like, all right, we have to start fast. Your guys' perspective, um is that like, what have you found is kind of the key to success there in in starting fast? How do you guys accomplish that as a group? >> I think a lot of times people really want to obsess over the result of starting fast. I think much more important are you know, again, your culture, like what you bring. So, like, if I were to verbalize it in my terms, I'd say is there execution? Like, did everybody do their job? Did everybody know their job on the you know, to start the game, were we do we know our job, do we do our job? Was there effort? Were guys running to the ball, running to make the tackle, running to get that extra block on offense? And then was there energy? Like did you celebrate when you made a play? Were you excited for your teammates? Was the juice there immediately? And I think if you get those categories correct, oftentimes you're going to have plays that you are very excited with. It's going to be three and out or a touchdown to start. But sometimes like the other team gets paid, too. And sometimes you may have those three things right, but someone on the team makes a great play, right? And if that's the case, it's okay. Like it still doesn't mean you didn't start fast, in my opinion. Like to start fast means to approach the game the right way and to have your culture at the forefront at the beginning of the game. And that's going to carry you through all four quarters and overtime if you get there. And that will, more times than not, be the recipe for a three and out to start the game, for a takeaway, for points on the first drive. That's my opinion. >> I'm just wondering to what you've seen of like like you know, Chase has talked a lot about wanting to be like more of a leader and it seems like he's he's been more vocal in that regard, but what is it about your guys' culture that like accepts what someone wants to do that and like not pigeon them into a oh, this is what you did before, like you can't do Um you know, leadership is something that's just like to me it's earned. And it's earned every day and I think you see one of the reasons why guys gravitate to him more and more. I wasn't here last year, but I played against him twice and I saw the way he disrupted games. I saw the way he brought energy to those games. And then watching the film and again, getting the behind the scenes look on what last year was, what this offseason is, like he's a guy that's out there making plays. He's a guy that's out there doing the right thing. He's a guy that's out there playing hard. Guys gravitate towards that. Um so, I mean, what I mean pigeonhole, I I don't think anyone's going to try to say no, you can't be a leader. But if you want to be a leader, you have to do things right. And if you don't, it's not pigeonholing you, it's that you haven't earned that right to do things right. And if you don't, it's not pigeonholing you, it's that you haven't earned that right. He's going out there, he's taking the steps to earn that right and he's doing a great job. >> And this question doesn't that make sense but like um with uh Staley um and kind of the vision he has for you guys and what he wants you to do to get out there and make plays and like how have you found him as a like a communicator with that just kind of like uh explain to y'all like the why behind >> the the concepts and ideas. >> Um you know, you can take that from like philosophically like the why to play this way, you know, his major aspects for us as a defense, for us as a team. He does that. He also does it the why to why we play this technique, why we play this coverage this way. He's he's extremely detailed and I think that really allows us to be, you know, free and play out there not because he's overrunning us with details but because he's giving us the detail, the why, the scheme, the schematic, the culture. This is why we do what we do cuz we want to win cuz we want these outcomes on the field and when he you the one when that's clear to you as a player, it allows you to play fast cuz you understand what we're trying to give them, you understand what we expect of ourselves, you understand the standard that's set every day and it allows you to go out there and excel within that standard. >> Speaking of uh young guys, I know Danny Sorensen's been a guy that everyone's been kind of paying attention to. What What have you thought about his play throughout the offseason? >> Um it's it's been cool to watch him play. Um I remember last year when I was uh watching the film from the other place, um I was like did did Pete get an collar right cuz it's 28 and 20 so sometimes far away film you couldn't tell the difference. but man, I I I think he's a similar athlete and that's an extremely high compliment. Um like the way that he goes and he he plays this game, he's he's got good length and size and strength. Um he's also fast though and he plays with the, you know, good amount of bend, a good strike. Like he plays the game the right way. He's smart, he's intelligent and um he's another guy that's out there making plays, another reason I I our linebacker core can uh help drive >> You don't see too many guys in that role nowadays or that collar, you know. >> It's rare, but you know he's he's out there doing it. Makes it look good. >> That's just like just not a like a cool line backer play. >> It's got to be. He just, you know, he he wants fullbacks, I guess. Fullbacks in the hole. He's doing good though, man. >> do you immediately gather an assumption about the way that play a player plays if they have that on? >> For sure. But but that's what you know, that's the thing about Danny is, you know, normally if you see a guy out there in coverage with that thing on, you're just throwing it there. But he's a But he But he's a great athlete in space and so he may be trying to deceive them, get some interceptions. You know what I mean? All right, y'all. Thank you, guys. >> God bless.

title: Saints RB Kendre Miller on battling injuries throughout career and expanded opportunities

You were you were here all offseason, right? >> Yeah. Yeah. >> What was that process like? >> Honestly, you know, I wasn't um cuz you know the offseason you get to do whatever, take trips or whatever. I wasn't too too bummed out on it at all. I mean, um, the the biggest thing was me just getting healthy. Uh, because like I said, it's I think every year like it's, you know, it's your contract year, which is this year is my contract year.
