title: What's Really Going on with the Seahawks' Secondary?
text: I believe really discussed this since uh the signing news broke, but also today we learned that uh former Cowboys cornerback Trevon Diggs did try out for the Seahawks. Rob, is there anything notable about this or what should we know about this news? >> Well, I have to be honest. When I saw that they'd had a Trevon Diggs in for a workout, I thought, "Well, I've not been worrying about this, but if they're giving him a workout, I can't I maybe I need to worry about it cuz uh I don't think he's very reliable at all. Um I I I don't have any issue with the Tariq Woolen thing. Uh I I think it's one of those things where people will wring their hands about stuff like this sometimes. Uh it seems to me as if there was a I think we talked about it last week. There's there was a bit of a a battle to sign him in the end. And uh the way that J- uh John Harbaugh was speaking with the Giants, he was really keen to bring him in. The Seahawks obviously had him in for a visit and a workout. Uh we heard uh John Schneider reference that they thought there might be a chance he could play in the preseason. It doesn't seem that's going to be the case. It does seem now as if they've got maybe a bit more information having agreed to this deal that he's going to go on the the commissioner's exempt list. And therefore, we wait to see what happens both legally and and with the NFL. I I think probably the worst-case scenario here is he he isn't able to play this year. And then, what do you do? Do you sign him with the idea that if he doesn't go to jail, you could have him next year because the the club control will will last for a couple of years as a restricted player. Uh and therefore, you could have him next year and therefore, still an opportunity there. But then, do you really want to keep a player who's not going to play this year, who's who's maybe got a bit of baggage there legally? I I don't know. When when is this going to be resolved legally as well? That's that's stuff we don't really know at this point. So, I don't have a problem with it. Like I don't have a an issue with the Seahawks rolling the dice here. I think they've got a lot of money in the bank. I don't think the Seahawks are an irresponsible franchise. I think there are other franchises who were doing this that it would look like a bit of a stunt, but I don't think you can uh label the Seahawks just doing that. So, I'm quite happy for them to go through the process. I I personally hope I don't have to watch Trevante Diggs play for the Seahawks next year. Um but I if they are having to try people out, then I I did have a look. I did Google NFL trade candidates about an hour and a half ago to see if there were any cornerbacks being mentioned in any articles, and the ones that were weren't worth having. So, um could be an interesting positional situation there. >> Well, it does seem like the Seahawks did their due diligence, too, with the connections that other form or other players and coaches have with Arnold before this this news out about his timeline. But, Brian, what does this tell you, and what what should we know about what his his role Trevante Arnold's role could look like with the Seahawks? >> Well, you know, I will admit something to both of you. I I'm a multitasker. Even when I'm on my own show, I'm I'm reading things and paying attention to texts and other stuff coming in. And so, when we were all talking, I saw an article from Mike Florio about this. And he wrote an article where he was like, "The Seahawks miscalculated as to whether Trevante Arnold would be available to to practice, and they may maybe looking for an exit ramp." And in that article, he actually wrote uh that they gain nothing from having Arnold under contract while criminal charges are are not resolved. And honestly, that's part of why I got into doing this is the fact that you have people nationally that just spew absolute nonsense. Like that are not doing actual analysis and not thinking through it and are just putting stuff out there because kind of what Rob said there, if you sign Trevone Diggs and you're a Seahawk front office, even if he doesn't play a snap for you this year, you have him as an exclusive rights free agent next year, which means he would be a minimum salary essentially player for you without any other team being able to sign him. And the year after that, he would be a restricted free agent, which would also mean that you'd be able to get him back for a very reasonable amount. so it is factually incorrect to say there is no reason for the Seahawks to sign Trevone Diggs even if the legal situation isn't resolved, even if he doesn't play a snap for the team this year. So that's one just like let's just have a reality check for people that actually care and and actually want to follow the Seahawks about what's going on. Then there's the other part of this, which is well, that's fine, but if you have a situation where you want to support your secondary a little bit more and improve your secondary and now you've got a question about whether Trevone Diggs can be part of that picture, you have to start looking for alternatives and I think what the Seahawks have done in tipping their hand here is until they brought in Trevone Diggs, you could spin this publicly very clearly of we we actually like our cornerback room. Like we like our depth. In fact, Mike McDonald was very clear that they this is a not about our cornerback depth. We like our cornerback. This is about us being in everything and trying to get, you know, great players that we really feel good about in the in the room. Well, if you're talking about signing any cornerback on August 18th, that's a veteran free agent, and you don't have injuries. Like there's not injury situations other than Nikki Minneboo there's not really injury situations in the Seahawks secondary. That kind of flies in the face of we feel good about our secondary depth. So, that's the thing that I think we're now monitoring is I don't think Trevon Arnold was just a signing because they wanted to get a good player that they liked. I think they do have questions about their secondary. I think Nehemiah Pritchett is part of that conversation. I think that um Noah Igbinoghene is part of that conversation. And one way or another, it looks like we will probably find out whether or not the Seahawks are comfortable rolling the dice with those guys. Or if they sign Trevon Diggs, it's a pretty clear sign they've already made some decisions about the guys already on the roster uh and how they feel about them. So, it's going to be an interesting next couple of weeks before cutdown. >> It will be and and I don't believe we have an update on Julian Love. Is that correct on his injury front? >> Correct. Yes, so that is the the injury that is there and he has not practiced since they've gone into pads. He is is not he it's the weirdest thing. I I should talked about this in the my post practice report today. This is now the fourth time I have seen him in pads all the way dressed going through warm-ups and then not doing anything in practice. It's like a very I don't know what I don't know what the purpose of that is. Uh I mean, I'm not Sam Ramsden. I'm not the Seahawks. They obviously have a really good smart group making these plans. But as someone who's really eager to watch this guy practice, I am like it's a bummer. I will never get to see Julian Neal practice before the season, even if he does come back, because other than the joint practice, which I will not be for there for, there will not be any more press access for practices. So, we'll just have to hope and and wait, and uh we'll see what happens there. I I always kind of thought Julian Neal was a developmental player this year. I did not think he was going to be a guy that jumped in and would play immediately. But, you know, who knows how this will play out.

title: Makai Lemon & More On Returning to Training Camp
text: You know, I felt great. You know, definitely blessed. You know, every time I'm able to step on the field, you know, I just never take it for granted. You say you learned from it. What I'm curious, what have you learned in terms of, I guess, preventing it again? And what did this process teach you about taking care of yourself and being a professional? You said, >> I think, just make sure um, I'm being more professional, you know, off the field, you know, in all aspects. >> You remember how it happened, >> huh? You remember how it happened? >> Oh, yeah. Yeah, just um bursting the field, you know, just a little tweak, just making sure, you know, I got my body warm. >> Now, now that you're back, I mean, what's kind of like the biggest adjustment that you're facing, you know, putting into getting ready for the season? And whenever you uh listen to the bad things, they say it can get to you, but whenever you listen to the good things, you can't let that get to you as well. You got to stay even. So, um you know, that's just a life of being a professional and a DB. >> What's it like going down? Can >> you describe the pick six that you had, you know, going against AJ on? >> Uh sure. I just, you know, played the play within the play. Uh they called a great call. I kept my leverage and I just seen the ball come and I got to make the best of my opportunities and the ball came, I caught it and shoot a nice interception. >> What's it like to bring the juice to the defense when you do that? >> Uh, it's pretty cool just because I'm the new guy, you know. Uh, I still feel like I got a lot more to prove to these guys, even the fans and everybody here. People only know me where I come from and what they've heard from where I came from. You know, people don't really know me as a person. So the more and more I make plays, the more and more I talk to you guys, talk to people around here, they'll be able to understand me and get to know me and know the type of player I am. So, uh, that's one thing right there. >> This was your first this was the first practice since Devonte's been back. What, you know, what does he add to the offense when you guys are going in these competitive moments? >> Uh, he adds a lot. I mean, that's our guy. I mean, whenever he's out there on the field, you you love to have him out there cuz, you know, you got a chance of winning. And being able to have him out there, you know, the other receivers can build off of him as well. So, you know, it's a full circle, you know, thing. And I feel like having him back out there, it's amazing because, you know, he's our guy and we need to go against him to get better as well and he got to go against us to continue to get him better. >> Tomorrow night will be your first opportunity in front of thousands of Eagles fans link to public practice. What are you expecting and how much are you looking forward to that? Uh, honestly, I'm just excited, uh, you know, to play football. I feel like every day I wake up, it's a new opportunity for me to continue to get better. And like I said, you know, me being new here, you know, it's another opportunity to show people, you know, how I play ball and to just express who I am. I mean, the more and more people get to see me and, you know, hear from me, understand me, I feel like they'll get to like me. So, I'm just excited to, you know, go out there and have a joint, not a joint, but a regular practice, you know, in front of a lot of fans and, you know, especially to be in the link. So, it's going to be pretty cool. >> You guys have sides of I know there haven't been that many sides of Kai yet. What do you see in him? >> Uh, shoot. When he got here since OTAAS, you know, he's been fitting into the culture well. You know, he's a young pro. He come in, he works. Uh, he does everything he needs to do so he can come back out and be available on the field. And you know, all the receivers, they they do a great job as well, you know, making sure he doing the right thing. So, uh, I'm excited to have him coming back to practice and stuff like that. And it's pretty cool to see him out there spinning because, you know, that's something that everybody wants to see, you know, him healthy and having fun again. >> Do you notice that because in the rec recent years, college guys get paid now. Is there a level of professionalism because it's sort of like part of it's like almost like a job in college now? Have you noticed that in the last couple years? >> Uh, I mean, a little bit. I mean, I just know I I wish I would have got paid in college. So, uh, other than that, uh, you know, I just felt like from what I've experienced with Mai, I mean, he's come in and, you know, he just been working. I mean, some guys, they get money at an early age and especially in college and, you know, different distractions here and there, but, you know, the ones that overcome all that, those are the ones that make it to the next level. And that's the reason why he got drafted in the first round and drafted the position he did. You know, he's, like I said, he's a young professional. He's handled all that well and you know as a young athlete who has had NIL I mean shoot he's done a good job and you wouldn't have noticed any difference to him. He's still the same person. He's still a chill guy and you know he's still ready to work. >> Rick, what's your perspective on the play that led to Jook's interception in New England? >> Uh shoot it was pretty dope. I mean I was just playing coverage and shoot honestly I didn't know the ball was just in the air. I just shoot swipe for the ball and then it was in the air and I heard people were yelling and he had the ball. So it was pretty cool and for you know to make a you know a takeaway and especially in that capacity of the moment you know just because it's like the intensity of the drill. So for for us to get a takeaway is pretty awesome. >> This far into camp, what's it been like for you to work opposite of Quinan and how much have you two been um you know working together to to to get better together in certain things that you do well? Uh, it's pretty cool just because like I said, man, it's like people only knew me for what I came from. So, when every day I come here, it's an opportunity, you know, just to work, to get better, you know, to get adjusted and, you know, to fit real well with the DBs, you know, especially with Q, you know, playing opposite of him. I know I'm going to have great opportunities and I know he's going to have great opportunities as well. So, you know, for me, I just got to continue to keep working and as I continue to learn from him, uh, he's going to feed for me as well. >> How did the guys in the locker room welcome you so that you could just place your full potential right away? >> Uh, honestly, just as I got here since OTAAS, you know, the guys been, you know, being uh, real, you know, respectful, real cool. And I feel like as we go through camp, you know, especially last week and uh you know, we it was just pretty cool to make plays cuz I feel like when I make plays, those guys, you know, that's what they want to expect from me. So, as I continue to make plays and, you know, off the field, continue to talk to guys throughout the locker room, throughout the facility, you know, I'll grow closer. You know what I'm saying? I one thing I always tell to myself is like, you know, you just got to be yourself for real. cuz I I still kind of do get nervous a little bit when I go out there just because like if I'm if like I'm a rookie again. I was in a whole different city 4 years ago and I got to come to a new city. I got to move all my stuff. I got to, you know, get well getting know my teammates, get acclimated to a city. So, uh, honestly, this has been pretty cool and I feel like every day I continue to get better, continue to fit well, fit in. >> A few times just wanting to show who you really are as a player and as a person. Do you feel like there were some misconceptions about you before you got here? Oh, most definitely. But I mean, people when people don't understand things and they they don't know the the unknown, you know, that people just, you know, just run with thoughts. And, you know, I can't, you know, be likable to everybody. But I know that people who really do know me, I know there's a reason why they like me. That's cuz I'm being myself. And, you know, I'm still a great guy. So, other than that, I just got to continue being myself and it'll show for itself. I mean, I'm here for a reason. God put me here for a reason. He surrounded me here with a lot of great people. So other than that, as long as I'm here being on my feet at I feel like uh my personality will outshine a lot of things. >> All right, that's our last one. >> Appreciate it. Appreciate it. Heaven.

title: Sean Mannion on Offensive Progression During Training Camp
text: How's it going, guys? Sean, >> so uh first game, uh first game in the booth. How did it go? And what are some of the differences you noticed when being on the sideline? >> Yeah, I uh was glad I you was able to experience it. Um I thought the communication really both game one and game two um being on the field or in the booth was was smooth. Um great communication with the coaches. Um there's some differences, but you know, I felt really comfortable with both of them and um you know, still sorting through all that as a staff, but it was a good opportunity in the in the preseason get to get to use both uh both options. >> What are you going to do on on Friday? Have you made a decision? >> No, still sorting through that. >> Uh as far as backup quarterback and you know, in the preseason it's difficult because sometimes you're playing second team, third team. How how does that affect the evaluation when the stats may look better for somebody than somebody else? >> Yeah, with any with any any position, quarterback or otherwise, it's it's about the entire body of work. You know, obviously the preseason games um are really, you know, useful tool to evaluate. Obviously, a game setting, different situations kind of coming up unscripted, but I mean, these guys have been hard at work um starting back in April. Um we've got tons and tons of reps on the practice field as well. Um, you know, both quarterbacks, really all of our quarterbacks have done, um, you know, a really nice job in the practice setting, in the game setting. Um, so it's it's really about the entire body of the work. Certainly the preseason's part of that, but um, there is a ton of banked reps going all the way back to the spring as well. >> Sean, there's got to be a point where you want to name that number two or decide on it so they can get as much reps as possible as as the primary backer. Do you feel like you're you guys are at that point now? >> No, we we still got time. you know, we still got a whole, you know, a great week's work uh here ahead of the Cincinnati game and then, you know, you get some extra practices before week one as well. So, um you know, we're going to use we're going to use every chance we get to work with with all of our guys um quarterback or otherwise and um and then kind of make a full evaluation from from every bit of practice that we have. >> This thing was new for Tanner. What did you see from him in on Saturday and what was kind of in the playbook there to maybe get a look at what he can do? Yeah, you know, he did a nice job operating. I thought he got got the ball out of his hand fast. Um, found completions. Um, you know, obviously was it was nice. We were really able to lean on the run game early on in the game. Um, and then, you know, you had a a couple long drives with some with some third down conversions. You know, he hit Stone on a throughout late. Um, so there was good stuff really from from all the all the different units in the game. Um, you know, we we leaned on the run game early and then later on, you know, got a little bit more um pass attempts in there, but um he operated well, got the ball out of his hands quickly and and as did Andy. You know, we had let us on a scoring drive and um there was a lot of good stuff from from all the guys in the game. >> With a player like Andy, with a player like Andy who has all this experience in the league, how do you weigh that versus what you can evaluate from what you've seen this summer? >> Yeah, obviously that's something that Andy brings to the table. You know, he's he's a veteran in this league. He's got well over a hundred starts. unique. Um, but we get a chance to be around him, Tanner, Cole, Jaylen every day. Um, and so, you know, that that's part of what he brings to the room. Um, but but everyone's bringing something to the table. You know, um, Tanner, Cole, Jaylen, obviously um, they all bring their own experiences. It is something unique to Andy with with having so much experience, but, um, ultimately it's an evaluation on the field um, both in the practice and the games. Um, that's the driving force. How did he perform in the in the during practices? >> I thought he did a good job. You know, I thought the first day um you know, we had a lot of big plays and just a couple um you know, a couple turnovers we need to clean up. Obviously, that's always a focus for us, but um you could really see the run game come to life. You could see the play passes off of it. Um you know, we hit a nice pylon route to to Elijah. Um but you could see the explosives in the pass game as well. You know, a couple turnovers. Um you know, those are obviously things we always want to address. Um, we talk about the ball relentlessly, but he did a really nice job. Um, for the guys who didn't play in the game, they got a ton of great work in those two practices against the Patriots. Um, I was really happy with how Jaylen played uh throughout >> Joe. We've uh we've seen Mai Lemon look close to returning to a full participant. Uh, do you expect that this week? And what's the ramp up plan for him after missing so much time? >> Yeah, you know, he's been working working his tail off to get back out here. you know, I think we're hopeful he'll he'll be out on the practice field um in some capacity here today. Um and you know, he's been really really engaged mentally and I think that's the challenge. Any player that you're injured, you know, you lose those physical reps, but um he's done a really nice job. He's been with AMO, you know, Grizz constantly. Um you know, he's been locked in in all the walkthrough settings. You know, even when he can't get the rep, he's he's kind of shadowing his position on the field and and staying super engaged. And uh you know, he's been working his way back. I know he's looked good and and uh hopefully we'll see him out here in a minute. >> What stood out to you about Patriots? >> Yeah, it was execution and play style. I thought, you know, obviously the starting unit wasn't in there, but that, you know, that second unit, that third unit, they they really did a nice job. We controlled the line of scrimmage. I thought early in the game, um that kind of that first series, um you know, I thought the play style was on display. And those are the two things I I told him. I want to execute really three, execution, fundamentals, and play style. Um, we were a little sloppy in terms of our fundamentals and execution at times in the preseason game. Uh, number one, I thought it was much improved in game two. Um, particularly with that with the offensive line group up front. >> Mai, how much does he have to do? >> Yeah, mentally he's been super engaged. Um, so I I I don't worry about that one bit with Mai. I know the work he's been putting in. you know, injuries, unfortunately, they happen in in football. Um, but he's been a total pro about his approach to rehab, his approach to the mental side of the game, and like I said, you know, the unfortunate nature of football is sometimes you might miss some time, but he's done everything in his power despite not having those physical reps to be ready for us uh to make an impact. >> In terms of the preset protection calls, does that follow on channel primarily? >> It's it's on both the offensive line unit initially and then the quarterback has a hand in that as It's a little bit dependent on the play on the protection scheme in terms of um how much is on the quarterback's plate, but both uh quarterback and offensive line have a hand in that. >> So there's not there's not a person who makes the final call. >> Well, again, it would be dependent on the protection scheme. Um we have multiple different protection schemes. Um some of them it would be the quarterback um would would have the final say. Some of them it's communication within the offensive line unit. Sure. >> Um but they've both done a nice job. both units. I mean, there's so much communication on the offensive line that I think goes unseen. Um, our centers have done a great job. Jaylen's done a great job, you know, with some of our pass protection schemes. Um, where he does need to make adjustments. He's done a nice job of that as well. >> What's the second offensive line group showing you since started? >> Physicality. Um, you know, just the effort strain every day. I mean, those guys, you know, you watch that kind of those early snaps in the preseason game. it really it really stood out on the tape, which is what we want to be out as an offense. Um, and then the commitment to the fundamentals. You know, Coupe Coup's done a great job with those guys. Um, you know, obviously the starting unit, but you know, there's a lot of young talented players um kind of in that second, third unit. They've gotten better every day. It's a testament to their hard work, to the work that Coup's done with his position group. Um, and they continue to make strides. We're really pleased with them. >> What stands out about the way Chris Cooper handles some of those developmental offensive linemen? Yeah, it's it's detail. Um he's a great teacher. Um you know, it's it's total focus on the fundamentals. You know, I think he's he's done an outstanding job for us. Um you you can see him every day after practice with those young guys working on um you know, all the finer points of offensive line play and and he brings a unique perspective been having been a player himself. I think he's able to lend a lot of context um to, hey, this is where, you know, this adjustment to your fundamentals is super useful. Um, like I said, he's done a great job with with the whole room. Um, you know, in talking about those those young guys, right, that are just coming up. Um, it's really stood out in the preseason game with the work he's put in with those guys. >> Sean, where do you think uh through the entire process, like you were talking about before, Eli Sters has where is he in in that process? How much has he improved? >> He's getting better each day. You know, it's he's a he's a young player we're really excited about. Um, you know, tight end that kind of we've spoken about in some of these press conferences, right? There's a lot of different elements of the game that get thrown at you, especially for a rookie tight end. You know, um you know, some of the differences schematically that that NFL offenses will ask of you than a than a college offense. Um but he's taken to it really well. Again, some of the things may may go unseen. You know, they might not show up on the stat sheet. Um but he's working super hard. Um he's he's he's an exciting young talent. Um, and so he he's getting better each day and and and at that position in particular, there's so many different things that we're working on. He he's doing a nice job and he'll keep getting better. >> Maybe maybe a bigger picture >> in terms of your in terms of your scheme and having built-in answers to blitz and simulated pressures. How do you balance that with being explosive, you know, being able to throw that downfield? What is your philosophy? >> Yeah. Um, I think the first thing is is being sound with your protection scheme. Um and then having answers kind of uh pressure relief so to speak where hey if they are bringing guys that we can't account for in the protection scheme. One have we train the quarterback properly and then to schematically are there answers within the play. Um it's a little bit different you know week to week opponent to opponent um in terms of how you handle um different teams or different you know schematic adjustments. Um, but I think it starts with the, you know, making sure that we're really sound on our end with our protection rules, our training of the quarterback, um, to throw hot if need be or or make an adjustment if need be. Um, so I think it's it's a it's a big area of focus for us as an offense just to always make sure we're we're prepared and ready because when you do protect, when you do operate well, there are opportunities for big plays when teams want to bring pressure. >> John, some of the branches of of what we expect this offense to look like feature the fullback quite a bit. Is we haven't seen that yet. Is that something that you might have up your sleeve? >> Uh, you know what? I guess we'll have to wait and see. I want to want to I don't want to reveal too much. Uh, but, uh, you know, certainly, um, position, versatility, alignment, flexibility, those are things we place a premium on. Um, you know, so it's, uh, I guess I get, again, I apologize for not answering the question, but I don't want to reveal too much. Um, but those are things that, um, are very valuable to us as an offense and and that we challenge our guys to do across all our position groups. remember to camp in >> if I can test your memory to uh camp in 2017. What was it like first learning this scheme and did you know then this is the type of scheme you wanted to kind of I guess lean into? Yeah, you know, it was um you know, the like you said that 2017 um you know, offseason really that you know when they hired you know Shawn McVey and Matt Lafleur and all those guys. I know it's been well documented but um you know Zack Taylor, Greg Olsson, bunch of great coaches. I just felt like I was learning so so much and it was um you know such an exciting way to match you know match the run and pass um to you know they had such a way about teaching the game where we could feel ourselves challenging a defense but it felt simple to us. Um those are things that really stood out to me going through that experience um that really resonate resonated with me as a player and um certainly resonate with me as a coach. Um but yeah, that was a a very um exciting point in my football life. Um just the exposure to um that type of teaching, that type of scheme. I know, you know, Matt obviously a mentor of mine, getting to play for Shawn. Um you know, I learned so much from those people. It it's certainly a big part of, you know, molding me into the type of coach I am now. >> You mentioned a role for Carson Steel. >> He's done a great job. Yeah. I mean, he he, you know, he got limited snaps in the in the first week. Obviously, it was unfortunate. You know, uh JJ goes down on the opening kickoff, so he he carried a heavy workload late in that game and he handled it really nicely. Um you know, again, there's so many guys across our roster that um put the work in every day. Um Carson was a great example of getting an opportunity for expanded reps in the preseason and and really did a nice job with it. You know, did a great job with the ball in with the ball in his hand, run and pass. Um, so yeah, there could certainly be a role for him and um, you know, I was excited to see him go out there and really thrive in the reps he got.

title: Football at Four: Detailing Eagles Depth Chart Changes in Camp
text: Jeff Moher from the Inside the Birds podcast and of course phillyvoice.com all football season long. We get ready for the birds and of course uh they play Saturday night against the Patriots and kind of a uh tough performance to even break down because obviously no starters are in that game. We did hear from Shawn Manion earlier today and it it seems Jeff the main storyline moving forward after two games is the backup quarterback spot. And I guess we'll start with that. Uh, is this something here? Can they trade one of these guys? How do you kind of look at what we've seen through two games with Andy Dalton and Tanner McKe? >> Mike, you know, from me coming on and talking to you since the off season, early in the offseason, I I never understood how they plan to make it work with four quarterbacks. Once they drafted Cole Payton and had four, to me, it just didn't make sense. You don't want to, you know, for many reasons. We talked about snaps in practice, about having, you know, a plan to to be able to optimize your 53man roster and keeping four when you're only going to play one and maybe two only if your one gets hurt. It's just a really difficult proposition. So, uh, I'm I, you know, I don't claim to have the answer. I claim to be confused. I know that Howie Roseman, we've talked about this on Inside the Bird, Adam has brought it up, Howie Roseman's always liked Andy Dalton. Uh, I don't know how much he's liking him right now. Uh McKe had a slow start in general. Uh I I felt watching him Saturday night that he looked more comfortable. Still not perfect. I mean, we've seen like this guy looked like an absolute stud to the point where like, hey, this guy could be like a starter in the NFL. And maybe he still could. Um not everything was perfect, but I mean, he was certainly in a much better rhythm. Um and operating the new offense the way it should be operated on Saturday. and and obviously and you know I won't make too much of it but today he was the first quarterback up at at camp practice in for the >> Let me ask you what what I mean obviously we're talking about the backup quarterback and you're hoping it doesn't come to any factor but what are the Eagles looking for from their backup quarterback the veteran presence in Andy Dalton or maybe a guy who if they if for whatever reason Jaylen Herz got hurt the better player. >> Yeah I mean the Eagles have always valued a the position but they've always valued a veteran backup. I mean, you know, it was Kenny Picket for a a little while. Before that, it was somebody whose names Nick Fos was there, you know. I mean, they've always had a veteran backup, a Joe Flacco, you know, but then they've also been a big proponent of drafting young quarterbacks as many, you know, as often as possible to develop them, you know. We've seen that with Thorson. We've seen that with Herz. We've seen that with Cole Payton. Now, we saw it last year with uh Kyle McCord. So, it's great philosophy. I just it's just rare that you you see it and then you have four guys on the 53. So, what are they looking for? Honestly, they don't have a template, right? Cuz we've discussed how often they've had a quarterback like Jaylen Herds who can run and give you all sorts of rushing production. They have a quarterback like Tanner McKe who's not not ever going to run and give you rushing production. They they just like the position and like to have as much talent at it as possible. And yes, they they do prefer to have someone who if your starter goes down has been through some wars there. Uh and Dalton certainly has. Flaco has. You know, Picket had at least been a starter for the Steelers in a very tough division for a while. Um so it sounded it's it felt like they were trying to get the best of both worlds there with McKe and Dalton, but then they drafted Cole Payton and then it all just to me didn't make sense in terms of a long-term plan. I'm sure they have one. I'm just saying like I'm from the outside looking in it doesn't make a whole lot of sense. >> Well, at this point, uh Jeff, do you think that Howie Roseman is seeing if either one of the quarterbacks have any value on the trade market? >> I'm sure I'm sure he is. And then I'm sure people are calling him asking about it. The question you have to ask yourself is what is the market now for Dalton who is what 38? um >> has not put great film this preseason on. U you know, he was okay last year when he had to play with the Panthers. I mean, I don't know. I mean, I do think that there probably is. It's no, I wouldn't say no market. Every team always likes to have a good veteran backup. And we'll have to see if somebody wants to take Andy Dalton off the Eagles hands or kind of call, you know, dare them to keep four QBs and see what kind of roster, you know, maneuvering the Eagles will do. >> Uh Jeff, at running back, you're looking at the backup quarterback. What about the running back situation? Carson Steel obviously had a night on Saturday. You've got Shipley back there. Is is uh the backup running back even a conversation or something that the Eagles are even considering right now? Here's the conversation, you know, and it's funny because I we, you know, the beat writers, we all kind of discuss things among just amongst ourselves. There are some, you know, Jimmy Kempky, my colleague at Philly Voice, he really thinks that that Carson Steel is playing himself onto the 53. And I think it's a fair argument, if you believe that, that the Eagles like to keep running backs and they've kept four quite a bit. But the argument is also that when they do that, that guy tends to collect dust, right? Whether it's AJ Dylan, whether it's Rashad Penny, it's been other guys in the past who just basically sit there and don't play. Trey Surman for a while, right? They they just don't play. And Saquon's your workhorse. BSby, we're all talking about maybe seeing expanded role. And Shipley's had a really good camp. And if you're going to get somebody on the field to give you a little juice in the uh in the passing game that's not Saquon, um Shipley looks like he's pretty good there. So my argument would be there's no reason to keep Carson Steel unless you've got some kind of fullback idea in mind. Uh interestingly, today at practice they threw Dallas in a uh fullback role on a snap. That was interesting. Um but but uh even if they keep him, what what's he gonna do? I mean, how much time what why would you expend when you when you break it down this way, right? You're looking at maybe having to keep We just talked about four quarterbacks, right? At least three. Um if you're looking at maybe having to keep these two kids that they um brought on to the team from um Africa, right? Joshua Wuru and uh OR Bernard, knowing that they're not going to play, but you're going to have to occupy two spots on your 53. How do you also keep a fourth running back knowing you need to keep a lot of offensive linemen and defensive linemen? You're gonna have to keep a couple different safeties and corners. I the math at some point just doesn't add up if you're just keeping all these guys. >> Yeah, and that's something that's going to come up as we have further conversations based on two games. You look at wide receiver, you got good news today that Lemon was finally able to practice. So, that's something there. Obviously, you have, you know, Quz Watkins has 53 snaps, Tory 45, you've got CVY here, you've got Cooper here. Uh, when you look at the wide receivers, has this have have these two games done anything to clear that position up? >> Uh, you know, not not really. Now, the interesting thing today is Lemon's practicing for the first time in a while, right? Weeks, >> full practice. He he looked like a guy that the coaches were trying to make up three weeks of time in one session. I mean, the amount of motion, pre- snap motion, and him running, he must have ran more 10 times more yards horizontally than vertically today. I mean, he motion left across the line of scrimmage. Motion right across the line. Oh, left, then right, then right, then left. I mean, they were he must his conditioning is probably going to be pretty good after uh after today because he was good to see by the way. That's supposed to be a big part of this offense Sean Manion's bringing that we we've seen it at times in practice, but not as heavy as today where you have that pre- snap motion, that bootleg play action off of it, which gets you some nice easy uh theoretically easy um pitch and catch situations. You saw a little bit of that Saturday against the Patriots. So, has it changed? No, because I think you know your one and two are are cemented. They are they're Dvonte Smith and Dantavian Wixs. Um your slot receiver is Mai Lemon. He lined up a lot there today because you know he still has two weeks. That's the benefit of the late start. I mean he'll be ready as long as he doesn't suffer another energy injury. He'll be ready. The question is just how much will he be ready for? How much 11 personnel will they play? Will they play more 12? Uh but the pecking order will be those three guys, Wixs, Lemon, uh and and Smith as the number one.
