title: Rhamondre Stevenson, Kevin Byard III, Romeo Doubs & More Address the Media | Press Conference
text: Uh, we're in the red zone. Uh, you know, that's been a you know, big emphasis for us this whole off season. So, just getting reps there. Uh, you know, that'll help us, you know, throughout the season. I love them. I love them. >> Armondre, what did you make of the turf today? It just looks like it was a little slippery out there. >> Everybody was slipping, right? Uh, it's just something uh, we got to get used to. Uh, you know, if that's the field conditions, we have to get used to it and know how to plant uh, plant on our outside foot and, you know, stay on our feet. >> Possibility of Oh, no. Starts not playing uh, in the preseason finale. Uh, is that an adjustment for you guys if that's the case for you? And how do you [clears throat] how do you feel as you kind of getting closer and closer to the the first game? >> Uh, ultimately, uh, yeah, I'm ready for the first game. Uh, you know, I feel well prepared. Um, you know, in the past we probably played one preseason game or something like that, but you know, we're still all on the sideline getting our mental reps. biggest thing is just going to be out there getting tackled. Uh, but you know, we're pros. I think we're used to getting tackled and things like that. So, just staying into the games, all three preseason games. Um, and yeah, just getting the reps mentally more than anything. >> Sir, Armondre, with the field today, is it usually that slick or was today kind of unusual? >> Uh, I don't know. We haven't practiced there in a minute. I can't really remember. But, I know we were all slipping. We need to find our footing down there. >> You know, is that pass catcher I asked you about that you all wrote about? That catch you had um, Robert and everything. That's tight look tight window and you're catching it. You've seen quite a few of those in camp as well. Um, as a pass catcher, when did you feel like that part of the game maybe for you took another step forward? >> Uh, honestly, my I I've always been confident and and comfortable catching the ball and doing those routes out the backfield. I think it was just uh, getting those things on film. Uh, and just letting everybody around me, all the offensive players, all the offensive staff, uh, you know, getting that confidence I had in myself in me. So, I think they just seen me uh, working at it, you know, running running some routes, getting open, and I think we're sticking with it a little bit. >> Ronald, we saw you guys do a blitz pick up drill today. I think it's fair to say you're one of the better blitz pick up backs in the league, but is there anything that even you are still trying to hone and work on at this point in your career? >> Yeah, of course. You know, that that pass pro it honestly it changes up game by game, year by year. It's something you got to get used to. Uh you got to know who you're going against. So, I feel like that's 80% of the battle and, you know, just be wanting to do it. Uh if you're willing to do it, probably like 10% fundamentals and, you know, technique to it. >> Ronald, how is your body feeling? Seems like you've been a real strong camp for you so far. >> Yeah, I feel I feel great. Uh probably one of my you know, healthier training camps I would say. Body feels fresh. I've been proactive in the training room, things like that, just trying to stay ahead of everything. >> That that catch you had in the corner, is that old hat for you at this point? Uh >> You said it what? >> The catch you had in the corner, is that is that just a regular everyday occurrence for you now? >> I'm trying to make it like that. Trying to make it like that. Trying to make my teammates comfortable with me. Uh you know, just knowing I'm going to go up and get the ball and, you know, just show Just putting it on film, man. Just putting it on film. But yeah, I'm comfortable doing it. >> Ronald, in the red zone, what did coach say specifically could have been better there last year? Like the things at the top of the list. >> I mean, we got to score. We didn't score. We didn't score down there as much as we should have. I think I'll say that's the That's the main point. >> So, I guess why why was that? >> Weren't getting in the end zone. I don't know. we're going backwards. Uh we got to stay positive in the red zone, I'll say. Uh no negative plays. >> You guys have been through you know, good part of camp here, new acquisitions and everything. How do you feel about the offense as you guys get ready for start of the season? >> Yeah, I feel good. Uh you know, still a lot of things to, you know, hone down on and fix up and fix. Uh but I feel real confident. Uh I'm getting to know my, you know, my teammates again and, you know, real real comfortable with them. >> How do you feel running behind Elijah Jared up front? Obviously, Jared's in a new spot, Elijah's new, and then also Reggie at fullback. >> Yeah, it's been great. Uh you know, they're they're making holes for us to run through. Uh little chemistry, uh you know, getting on the same play page, same tracks, and things like that. But, I think it's going good. I think we'll go we'll be where we need to be by time season starts. >> How used are you um running behind a true fullback like Reggie? How much have you done that in your career and >> Uh yeah, Josh was up here. We had uh my boy Yakub Johnson uh uh my rookie year. So, I'm pretty comfortable running behind a fullback, but uh it is an adjustment. We haven't done it in, you know, a little bit. So, just getting comfortable uh just like the old line, man, it's just getting on the same tracks as uh our fullback and just thinking the same thing. >> Mhm. >> All right, I appreciate it, man. >> How's it going? >> How are you? >> I'm good. >> Just um was asking I think Marcus about John Saunders. He seems to find the ball. And you talked a lot about the importance of turnovers and finding the ball. What have you seen from John and like how do you guys compete? Put it up on the board. Who's got the most turnovers in camp? Like, what does that look like? >> No, John definitely has the most turnovers this camp. He's been balling out of control. He has a very like quiet confidence to him. He doesn't talk a lot. Um I've been trying to work on the celebrations. He does a little basketball thing, which is pretty cool. But, he doesn't say anything. He doesn't have any emotion when he catches interceptions. Uh but, even in the preseason games, he's been balling out. Uh so, it's been really good to see him cuz obviously, you know a guy like him who was I think he was on the practice squad last year here and you know, fighting for a roster spot, taking advantage of every opportunity that he's getting. Um no, it's it's been really good to see. I always say taking the ball away is something that you really you can coach. Some guys have it. Um but, it's something that Let me take that back. It's something that you really can't coach. You know what I mean? Like, certain guys have it. You can you know, get a key here and there by film study and stuff like that. But, the the amount that he's been able to get, um that's something that you really can't coach. He's he's a ball hawk. >> And what is it about his skill set that you didn't see him until he got out there? Having Gonzo back in practice, how uplifting is that? >> No, it's good. Our locker's next to each other and I, you know, just kind of briefly seen him in the locker room. I asked him, "How's it going?" And, you know, he was like, "I'm going today." I was like, "Okay. Yeah, that's pretty good." Um, no, I mean, it's always special to have one of the better corners in this league uh to have him out here with us. And obviously, as we >> [snorts] >> start to ramp up getting to the season, for him to be able to go out there and then start practicing fully uh it was pretty cool. So, excited about him and being able to be healthy and be out there and playing with us. >> Being his locker mate, do you see any frustration from him over the state of his contract negotiations? >> No, I don't I don't see it. Um, I think he's honestly handling it as as as best as I can imagine anybody in his situation is handling it. Um, he's still, you know, obviously having regular conversations in the locker room. Obviously, he's spent a lot of time in the training room uh trying to get back healthy. But, no, honestly, I've been I've been seeing him be his normal self. We all know Gonzo's not the biggest talker. So, you know, as we have a conversation, we're talking, but he's not like in the locker room pouting or not being himself, you know what I mean? So, I think he's handling it very well. >> When it comes to John, what is it about his skill set that puts him not only in position to get all these turnovers, but actually to finish them? Is it an intangible thing? Is it like a traits thing? >> Uh I mean, I I I just think that he's he's very like it's I would say like, you know, you have certain guys that they just kind of panic when the ball gets in the air or when it's certain situation a good communicator, but I think he he doesn't panic when the ball's in the air, you know what I mean? I think he just he does a good job when the ball's in the air. He zeros in on the ball. He catches every interception. Um, he's caught, you know, interceptions in the post. He's caught them, you know, in zone coverage and getting pass breakups in man. So, no, I mean, he's he's very I mean, I would almost say he's very unassuming, you know what I mean? Because, you know, when you see John, he's tall, whatever may be, but he he has great hands. He has a, you know, good ball skills. So, no, I I've been impressed with him because um like I said, he's very quiet, you know what I mean? So, you won't see a guy like, oh, I didn't know too much about him before I got here, but I'm like, man, he's got like five, six interceptions, caught one today, so no, I'm proud of him for sure. >> And with this being his being around the league for so long and and dealt with your contract situations, it how much if at all does that come up with Christian even you guys are next to each other in the locker room? >> No, I mean, I I think when I first got here, like in the spring, we would just kind of have a conversations. Um obviously didn't really know or don't really know how things go, you know, I'm just using myself for example. Um my contract situation had got handled like right before like our conditioning test. So, he's in a whole new territory of like obviously going into the season and obviously, you know, when you got contracts probably of of this magnitude, you know, they kind of take a little bit of time. Um so, it just kind of like there's not really too much advice you can give a guy, you know what I mean? You could just If he wants to talk about it, you know, I'm there for him to have conversations, but no, it was kind of one of those deals where um you know, him and his representation and the team, they're handling their way, but like I said before, I think he's been handling it just as good as anybody could, you know what I mean? Like this is a life-changing situation for him, you know what I mean? I get it. You know, it's ball and all this other stuff, but it's life-changing, so um I can only imagine there's a lot probably some emotions and things like that, but I think he's being a pro, you know, he's being a pro about it. He's he's still being team first. Um there's a lot of different situations going on around the league and everybody has the right to deal with their situations the way they want to, and I don't think it's like a oh, he's wrong for doing it this way or he's right for doing it this way, it's really just individually depending on the player and the team and their representation, so um and I've seen it all the different situations. I just think for him um it just speaks to who he is and his character, just the simple fact that he wants to be out there in practice and be with the team regardless if it goes down or not. I think that's pretty It's just in my opinion, I think that's pretty cool. It's pretty neat. >> Kevin, obviously you had more turnovers this summer in training camp. Is that something that can just click during the regular season for you? >> No, I mean I definitely want to get more turnovers. I think you know, I want to get a turnover every day, honestly. But I will say I've had training camps where I've gotten a lot of turnovers and then getting to the season I had one interception. Then like last year in Chicago, I may have had I think I had two interceptions and they were they were both doing the joint practices and then I led the league in picks. So I feel like it's one of those deals for me, I'm just always focused on the process. It's not necessarily more about the result, especially now coming into like a new scheme a little bit. This defense is very particular depending on situations, third down, different stuff like that. So me honestly trying to see what I can get away with sometimes and then, you know, as you get to the game situation is a little bit different. The quarterback's clock is a little bit more sped up. A lot of plays are sacks, they won't happen in so it's a little bit different, but no, I mean to your point I definitely want to get interceptions. I want to get turnovers, but at the end of the day I'll rather get them in games than get all my interceptions in practice. So but no, I mean definitely something I want to do, but at the end of the day I'm still confident in my abilities and knowing this defense I'll be able to pick my spots and get my turnovers during the season. >> Kevin, obviously you [clears throat] weren't with the team last year. So as someone coming in from the outside, what's been your impression of the way this organization has tried to pick itself up and move on from losing the Super Bowl? >> I mean I don't I don't know if they were I haven't sensed like the whole pick themselves up situation. I don't think anybody's um at least since I've been here feeling sad or that they lost. Obviously it's disappointing, but um I've always been under the belief that at the end of the day like no matter what success you had the previous year like you got to start all over, you know what I mean? Like you got to build the foundation back up. You don't really create or keep any momentum from the previous year. It's a whole new locker room. Um it's new guys on the team. We got to build our own culture, our own chemistry. And so, we're still in the foundation uh building process, you know what I mean? Like um I think that's been the special part about it that we're just more focused on this team today. And I understand that there's always going to be that comparison from last year and like, "Oh, you won this year, so the expectation is automatically here that you got to win a Super Bowl guaranteed." It's like the expectations need to be tapered, just in my opinion. It's not just because of what's been going on during training camp, I just kind of understand that it's very challenging to be able to get back there. And so, I think if anybody is leaning on the fact that we was there last year, that means we should get there. No, that's not how it works. Like, we got to continue to put in the work and not worry about what happened last year. Just focus on now, focus on the day. And uh I think that's what we've been more focused on versus you know, this team from last year and how they played and and the type of group that they had. And we're not trying to recreate that magic or nothing like that. This is a whole new situation with new guys. And we're going to have to win a different way than the probably they won last year. So, I think that's what we've been more focused on. >> Josh question. >> Mike could said that starters may not play Thursday. Are you okay with that as starter if you just get what you get out of joint practices? >> Yeah, I'm okay with whatever the head coach wants to do. I mean, I've had uh training camps where I played in every preseason game. I've had some where I played in two, played in one. I've had some where I played with none with Mike. So, it's you know, every year's different, you know what I mean? Like, if coach choose to play us for a whole half, then I'm with it, you know what I mean? Like, you kind of have to prepare in that way. as a veteran, you know, sometimes you want to kind of go in there and get a little contact, you know what I mean? But I'd rather save my body, you know what I mean? Like, I feel like it's really just I mean, I'm a player, you know what I mean? At the end of the day. If it's green grass and it's white lines out there, let's go out there and ball, you know what I mean? Like, I don't care if it's three players or if it's 30 players. I'm going to try to play my hardest. But at the end of the day, that's just what pros are, you know what I mean? You get no preseason, so what? Go there, you're still expected to make every tackle, make every play. That's kind of the game that we signed up for and we're going to be judged accordingly. So, no, like I said, however the coach feels about, you know, us playing every game, that's kind of where I'm at with it as well. >> Thank you all. >> Yeah, of course. Yeah. >> What did you like about practice today? >> I thought practice was pretty clean. Um, you know, just continuously getting better day in and day out. Uh, I've said it before and I can I'll continue to say it, this is a day-to-day league, so you know, I think it's just our job to keep striving for the best and just, you know, chasing the process and the progress every day, so. >> If you guys start don't play in the game Thursday, Mike kind of alluded that you may not, uh, joint practices, what did you take from them? How good were they for you guys as a group and how do you feel about the offense? >> Uh, I feel really good about this offense. Um, I thought the joint practices obviously is what you need in this league. Uh, you know, I know going against our defense is one thing, but when we get another opportunity to go up go up against another, you know, another team, um, that's just uh, another opportunity for us to show our uh, what we can do, so. >> Romeo, in that in that sense, in that sense in the preseason games, when you haven't really had any action with Drake in live preseason action, do you feel like you need those kind of reps or is the the joint practices and what you guys are doing out there enough? >> Great great question. Um, I think just any opportunity that you give a Drake, it's important that we maximize just the detail and just obviously being on the same page with him and um, I mean, yeah, I'll let the rest speak for itself, so. >> Romeo, hold on. A week 10 days ago, you really became very apparent during practices, made a ton of plays and it just continued during the joint practices. Did you feel that same kind of rise to prominence as we did where it kind of the light it on or was it just opportunity in the ball coming your way? What explains it? >> Yeah, I think it's just an opportunity opportunity thing. You know, I think my job obviously is to be the best I can be in this offense. And just continuously chasing the process and the detail of this offense day in and day out. And um you know, whatever happens on the field, I just let it happen. So. >> Is it um when you have that stretch of three practices, do you drive home at night or come in in the morning and go have a good It's going to be good again today. [clears throat] It's going to be good. >> Uh no, man. I just, you know, obviously I take note of the practice, uh see the things that I can get better at as a pro. And um obviously I forget about the day, and I'll just move on to the next one. So. >> Romeo, I had read, I believe you played running back and quarterback in high school, if that's correct. Um >> Yes. >> Which was your primary position of the three, including receiver, and how did you end up honing in on receiver eventually? >> Um so in high school, I was in a wing T offense, so there's not a lot of opportunity to get catches or whatnot. So my when I started playing receiver, it just I started going to camps. I started doing 7-on-7 tournaments. And from that point on forward, I was given enough opportunity to showcase what I can do. And I mean, the rest just kind of speaks for itself, honestly. >> When you see Darren Morton take a punt during the game, does that make you want to try and go for Drake's job a little bit there then? With that quarterback experience? >> No, I mean, I I The more you can do in this league is one thing, but I mean, that's that's that's let's just leave that there. >> Do you feel that those reps at those other positions help you even even way back to high school days just be like a more well-rounded player in terms of of how you can maybe envision a route from from like multiple facets of the offense. >> Yeah, I mean like I said before, I mean the more you can do in this league, the better. And if I get any opportunity to show what I could do outside of playing receiver, I will take that opportunity. So >> Backing off that a little bit, tell me about your experiences as a punt returner. How much of a point of pride is that for you and how much of a part is that part of your game? >> Um I mean special teams is obviously important and uh punt returning was something I did in high school. I did it in college and um I was given an opportunity to do it at this level. again, that's just you know, I was just an athlete on the field, but just playing at the Excuse me. Playing on this level, there's a lot more detail to it. So I mean as long as I keep chasing that it's going to be all good. >> Two more? >> Can you think of a situation where you'd be able to catch I I saw the video of catching six punts a couple of years ago in camp with the Packers. Can you envision a scenario where Marquez Jones might be able to do something like that? >> I mean Marquez is explosive, man. Um so I would say that he can do that. Um you know, and I learn from Marquez day in and day out just being behind him. Just seeing his technique. Um you know, knowing that he plays a huge role in this uh in this on this team and um yeah. >> kind of work day-to-day and obviously want to get better. What's most important for you to accomplish over the next two and a half weeks before the opener? >> Um it's really simple. Just chasing the progress uh as much as I can and ultimately just being a team player because that's what it takes to win in this league. This is not a individualized league and um like I said, I've learned I've learned that early on in my career and I continue to just continue to master that as much as I can, so. >> Thank you, man. >> Thank you. >> What would you say you guys got accomplished today after your break? >> Uh man, uh a lot of competition. You know, we've been against uh other teams when it comes down to joint practice, but getting back to the basics was the main thing today. Uh we were happy to be back uh going against our offense and everything and seeing new looks and stuff, so. >> How nice to have Gonzo back out there, too? >> Oh, great, man. Um you know, the most important thing is health and everything. So happy that he's feeling better and everything and uh happy to have him back out there on the field. >> Was footwork an issue tonight for you guys? It looked like there was some slipping and sliding out there on the lower field. >> Yeah, I mean, when it comes down to it, um however the grass is, it's you know, however we got to play. Uh we've been on slippery slipperier uh surfaces before when it comes down to seven-stud cleats, but we got to make sure that we take care take care of those situations. >> Sorry, man. >> You good. >> Um Marcus, when did you know Christian or how did you find out Christian was going to practice today? >> Oh, I just went out to the practice field and then he was there. So, I found out just like you guys. >> What did you think of his song? >> Oh, I was happy that he was back part of the part of DB room and everything. He's been in meetings and everything, so we've seen each other when it comes down to being in the building, but um anytime, you know, we got a player out there that's been away, we're happy to have him back part of our squad. >> Marcus, with the two preseason games that you haven't played in this last one, if you don't get the opportunity if Vrabel decides not to play the starters in those games, do you feel like those two joint practices are two against three, actually, were enough for you to be ready for week one? >> I feel like when it comes down to it, every snap that we get, regardless if it's against joint practices or, you know, practices that we have with each other, we just take advantage of those opportunities that we get. Um when it comes down to the situation of playing in those games, um you know, if coach decides to do it, then we're ready for it. Uh but at the end of the day, they know what's best and um we're always ready to compete wherever we are. >> Richard, um turnovers at in the media tent, see a lot of picks. Yeah. John Saunders like shoots up to the top of the list and I'm wondering I guess two things. One, do you guys chart them in your room and like is there a competition? And what about Saunders? >> For sure. Yeah, I mean the most important thing like I said, we want to be the number one scoring defense and in order to do that we got to turn the ball over. So, John man has been having a great training camp when it comes down to it. A guy that whenever we talk about stuff in the in the film room, like he applies it to the field and you can definitely see the confidence out there and whenever we have guys making turnovers and everything, we're excited as a whole >> Do you put them up on the board like and and or do you just talk about it in the locker room like who's got the most? >> Oh yeah, so our thing with practice is that we want to get at least two turnovers. If we don't then we do push-ups. So, we always talk about situation of a turnovers. >> Marcus, would you take us through the last play there? I know there was like one second there at the line but you're right on AJ as Drake throws that ball. >> Yeah. Um first off, I mean they had the score. So, it was last play situation. We were in a great coverage. When it comes down to it, it would have been a bang-bang play so I feel like it was a good play by the offense and a good play by the defense. >> How did you notice Christian's absence during those joint practices, Marcus? >> Um I would say when it comes down to it, we always think about next man up when it comes down to it. Like I said, we always want guys to be healthy at the end of the day. Um if they're not then we don't want them out there to get hurt worse when it comes down to it but um yeah, I mean we know how he is as a player but we understand that we also have other guys as part of the team too that's ready to take advantage of those opportunities. >> The little you got to just see him either in one-on-ones or when you were out for team, what how did he look to you? >> Uh when it comes down to me, I honestly like I don't see those things until we go back in and watch film. Um I'm kind of on the field at the same time he is so I'm kind of worried about what I have to do. But um I know whenever he's out there, you know, if he feels like that he can do it then he'll be out there. And if he doesn't, like I said, we want to take care and make sure everyone feels good. >> Do you think it's a different like a different level of confidence just knowing that he's in the huddle with >> Um I would say yeah, when it comes down to him as a player like I know anybody's out there, I'm not going to think of it as like only him. Um whenever we have those guys that's out there that's been a having a whole bunch of snaps like we have confidence along the board when it comes down to it. But yeah, I have a whole bunch of confidence of him being on the field as well. >> We saw Kindle Vildor make a few plays against the Eagles. Seems like he's been doing it through the spring and the summer. What have your impressions been of him? And are you surprised when he makes those plays or what is it about him that allows that to translate to the >> No, not surprised at all. He's a guy, man, when it comes down to competitor, he's at the top of the list. Uh he's played a lot of football as well. And we've seen him make plays at practice. And when it comes down to the game, we know that it's going to translate. His confidence is at an all-time high. So, we know whenever we have him out there, he's going to take advantage of opportunities. And as you guys can tell on the sideline, we're going on crazy whenever we see those plays cuz we love it and we understand how much time that we've put into situations like that to take advantage of them. >> Thank you, guys. >> Thank you, guys, so much. >> Uh what did you feel you got accomplished today out of that practice? >> Um I feel like I feel like last week we kind of had a up-and-down day in the red zone. Um which I in a way, you know, we kind of had again in a way, but I feel like we executed some things that we we needed to execute today. Um obviously a red zone is a critical part of the game and um and then two-minute at the end of the game, too, is is huge. And so, just working on critical situations is you know, the most important thing you can kind of work on at practice. So, that was huge for us today. >> When it comes to the red zone, you know, the coaches have emphasized that dating back to OTAs. What about last year do you think like, okay, we could have been better short yardage, you know, route spacing? Like what were the things specifically within the red zone that could have >> Yeah, man, I think it starts with I mean, you got to you to run the football a little better in the red zone. I mean, everybody you know, the top teams that um are some of the best red zone teams, you know, are able to run the football down there cuz it's condensed. It's hard to throw the football down there. Um you know, it's easier to it's a little easier to cover uh for guys. I mean, there's less field, there's less grass. So, running football always alleviates some of that some of that pressure. Um and then just being detailed um a little bit more detailed at least for us as skill guys um on where to be, you know, you know, timing of things but timing happens really really fast. And so, you know, I think another year in this offense understanding things, you know, we were all kind of learning together as we went last year and putting in the red zone in. And so, another year in the offense understanding it, Drake understanding it um can definitely help the timing. >> Have you ever started a season without playing any reps in a preseason game? >> I have. >> So, you you feel confident >> If you don't play Thursday, you'll still be ready for week one, I guess. >> Yeah, I do. >> Yeah, all right. I guess. what's the process like of getting ready for week one when you don't get those preseason reps? >> Um I mean, personally, I can speak for my experience. I mean, I've played, you know, this is going to be my 11th year. I've I've banked a lot of reps. Um so, uh you know, that toot my own horn, but I I've played a lot of football and kind of know what it entails and you know, the process of getting to that to that point. Um I mean, I've done this before. Um I mean, obviously COVID year we didn't have any uh you know, any preseason games. Um so, you know, it's just it's part of the process. I mean, whatever Vrabes whatever Vrabes wants to do, uh you know, we'll attack it and be ready to go. So, um you know, that's you know, we'll be ready to go no matter what. >> Hunter, you guys have more size at receiver and tight end this year. Do you feel like that's going to help you in the red zone at all? >> Size helps for sure down there. Uh like I said, less space. Um so, you know, obviously size size can help and uh but I think timing and just understanding things and banking reps especially down there, um you know, understanding where maybe Drake wants us to be or, you know, where he think, you know, we tell him like kind of hey, what we're thinking on something. Just being able to talk through things, but size can definitely help. >> Coach, how would you describe Romeo's versatility and what he brings to this offense? >> Yeah, Rome's, uh, you know, he's he's been doing a lot of great things for us through throughout this camp and um, moving him at different positions. Um, just I think I've been impressed with how smart he is. I mean, we're moving him all over the, you know, offense and, you know, that can be a lot, um, especially in this kind of offense. But, we have to do it at tight end, so I I trust me, I know kind of the the burden it can put on a guy of, you know, you have to kind of know a lot, um, and kind of know where you fit in the different schemes and he's been, you know, just doing a lot of great things. Um, obviously, he's quick. He's got, you know, he's he's got some size to him, too, honestly, uh, for for a guy. And then, just the quicks and um, just honestly high-pointing the ball throughout camp has been pretty impressive. >> Is there anything new that you plan to go over with Drake Maye this year? >> New? Uh, I don't think there's anything new. No. Uh, I mean, I know him pretty well, so uh, I feel like he's I think that's the thing about Drake, man, um, that I I really respect and enjoy being around is I think he's very consistent. Um, not just obviously on the football field, he's very consistent, but he's consistent in the locker room as a guy, as a person, um, all the time, he's very, very consistent in just who he is as a leader, as a player, and just he wants to he wants to get better every single day. I think that's what I really respect about him is he just like continues to want to improve. >> Coach Freeze said, uh, after the game, he doesn't think he has a very deep team. He shared this morning that he went and visited with Elliott just to kind of make sure there was no shade there. Is that anything he's followed up with the team? >> Uh, no, not not with the team, but I mean, I can speak personally, I I we got a lot of good football players in there. Um I mean, I I I believe I I go against a lot of different guys on a day-to-day basis and we we got a lot of really really good football players. Um so, you know, it's a joy to compete against our defense on a day-to-day basis. They've made us a lot of better a lot better. Um and just honestly, some a lot of the young guys I've seen a lot of growth from them um from day one to where we're at now. And so, uh it's it's cool to kind of see that growth, but also see all the kind of different guys we have on defense. So, it's It definitely makes us better. >> Considering, you know, you obviously spend more time around Brahe than some of the young guys, especially the rookies, right? If he doesn't follow up, do you feel compelled at all as a veteran to be like, "Hey, I'm sure you heard this." And and speak to them or how how does it show up if at all? No, I mean, I I I'm going to let Brahe kind of handle all that uh to be honest um and let him handle kind of all that with the young guys, but if anything, they should motivate you, man. Uh to kind of raise your level. I mean, that was that's the thing at this level, man. It's a production-based business and you got to continue to earn that respect and earn that thing on a year-to-year basis, on a day-to-day basis, on a week-to-week basis. So, um you have to bring it every single day and I think Brahe is just trying to call everybody up. I mean, I I take that personally. I mean, we should all take it personally that, you know, we're all trying to be our best. >> You seen Tanner Allen spend a lot of time at fullback during the preseason, obviously in practices as well. You've also seen Josh at times use you in the backfield. How do things kind of change for you process-wise or what have you when you're attached to the formation versus when you're lining up in the back? >> Yeah, I think that's the thing with our position, man. We have to be very versatile in this offense. I mean, you got to be able to know all the positions, honestly. Um every single, you know, receiver position, backfield position, um obviously inline stuff. So, it it it's a definitely a mental toll, um but you kind of just you have to be ready to go um at every position. And like honestly, Josh loves kind of the more you can do. He can move you around and you know, more you can understand and um um I think that's the benefit of having, you know, smart guys in the room that can, you know, obviously move around and be able to do different things. And Tanner's been one of those guys. >> Hunter, how have you seen Eli come along throughout training camp? How have you seen him kind of adapt to the NFL workload so far? >> Yeah, I mean, he's doing doing a lot of good things, man. Um a lot of good things. Um and just continuing to grow on things that he does well. I mean, I think he he gains confidence, obviously. I mean, we all gain confidence when you do something right. Um and then I think, you know, when he maybe messes something up or um does something maybe not to the level that he wants, he's he never really makes the same mistake twice. Um he learns a lot. He asks a lot of questions. He's really eager. He's a lot of fun to like be around in the room, too. I mean, he's just a good good dude. Um so, it's kind of fun to kind of grow with him, uh see his growth like throughout training camp, and that's only going to continue to go as as we get into the season and on a week-to-week basis. >> Final question. >> Well, Thursday's final preseason game, after that, what's that like for you? What the focus and the attention to detail? How much does that ramp up as you get closer and closer to opening night? >> Yeah, I mean, it it's uh you know, there's there's almost like there's like practice speed, um and then there's kind of like a preseason speed, and then like when we get to the regular season, that speed kind of goes up a notch. Um and then it kind of continues to ramp up as you go through the season. Um but yeah, it's uh opening night and opening day is always uh exciting. Um you know, you you wait, it feels like forever to kind of the build-up to it. And uh you know, you kind of have to focus in on the little details, all the things that you kind of been working on throughout training camp, and um try to apply them out, you know, uh on the biggest stage and be ready to go. All right, guys. >> What did you feel that you got accomplished out there today at practice? I I liked the energy we had coming out today. Um that was a really good preseason game we had against the Eagles. The guys fought hard. And then to see the guys who played come out and play as hard as they did today, I love the grit we're building. I love the identity we're building. And as a whole, I'm loving how our team's feeling. >> Like you talked about possibility of the starters not playing Thursday in Cleveland. Uh the joint practices, how useful was it for you as a defense, for yourself individually against the Colts and the Eagles? >> They're extremely useful. It's a It's a good way to measure how you're doing. Um they have guys that are getting paid to. They have guys that are um Pro Bowlers, you know, going to be Hall of Famers, all those type of guys. So, you know, to be able to go up against people like that um on both teams and to play how we played and improve each day, it was an amazing thing to experience and it only helps us. >> If you don't get the opportunity to play in this final preseason, do you still feel like those joint practices were enough for you to be ready for week one? >> Yeah, I think our coaches have a great plan for us. I think the organization has a great plan for us. As players, you know, we're always ready to play. It doesn't matter what day, what um what day of the week, what time of the month. It doesn't matter where we're at, home, away. Um we're going to be ready to play and that's how the coaches train us and that's how we see ourselves where whenever we line up the ball, we're going to be ready. >> Talked about energy. How much of a boost do you guys get when you see Christian back out there? >> Uh it's so much fun. He's a He's a big personality and we love it. We love having his energy. He honestly brings life to the field. He brings life to the locker room, to those he's around. Um so, it's awesome to have him out there and it makes my job a lot easier as a linebacker. >> When and how did you know Gonzo was >> Oh, um when I saw him out there. Yeah, that's not something I really pay attention I try to day of practice, focus on my job, focus on what I try to do. And then, you know, whoever's out there, will play together, we'll play hard. >> Chris, what does it say about Gonzo that he was showing up while waiting for the contract and now again coming off the injury? >> Yeah, um he's a he's a ball player first and foremost. Um he loves football, he loves being around the team, he loves uh lining up and playing against the best, um being one of the best corners, if not the best corner in the league. Um he just is a player, like at the end of the day, it doesn't matter. Um what he has going on. He's in the lineup and play and he locks people down, so. >> Chris, it seemed like playing fast was a big emphasis for you last season. This year, how are you trying to continue to evolve as a player? >> A lot of pre-snap. For me, it's uh trying to narrow down the plays the offense can run out of certain formations, narrow down who what guys they have in the game, what type of stuff they like to do. Um it's all stuff that I can process a lot faster being in the second year of the defense and um honestly, it's coming a lot easier to play. Um and then the coaches have done a really good job narrowing down my focus and making sure that I know where my eyes go, know where my alignment should be and play ball. >> How much of an impact has been Paul Williams role in that and how he's been working with the room now that's his first full season at the position? >> Yeah, loving loving. He does [clears throat] a great job with us. Um he keeps us in line, he has a good time with us and you know, whenever we're in our meeting room, he lets us know how it is and him being a ex-linebacker, he played at Boston College. Um he's recently in the role, so he knows exactly how a linebacker should play and that's something that you can't replace with coaches, you know, who might have a lot of ball knowledge, but we're never on the field. >> I know there's always a long laundry list of things that you want to improve upon. How do you feel about where the the run defense is at this at this point in time? >> Yeah, we're doing really good job. Um you know, with a lot of the um new faces, new guys and getting our identity and how we like to fit the run, how we like to um move our guys, how we like to play ball. Um I think we've been doing a great job. I think every week has gotten better and especially I mean it leads with our D-line. When our D-line dominate, we dominate as a defense and you know, it's it's our job as the linebackers just to make sure they're free, make sure they can do their job and I think they're doing a great job. >> Coach Vrabel mentioned the improvement in the run defense last week with the Eagles from day one to day two. What do you guys think you improved on on day two to shore that up? >> Honestly, it's more of a mentality thing than anything. Like you watch the film and it's just like, "Okay, so like are you going to be aggressive here? Are you going to try to guess? You're going to try to slow play it?" No, like at the end of the day you got to put your face mask on somebody and then you play off of that and then they start getting "Oh, is he coming?" You know? So, for us as defense it's about being fast, aggressive. We edge, we wall, we swarm and that's how we're going to play. >> And also um some of the guys talked about Mike challenging you guys between the first and the second practice like in my complaint. So, you're not not feeling comfortable. How much if at all did that impact you guys? >> Um Mike's a great motivational speaker. Vrabel's always gets us in the right mindset for practice and um I think him being an ex-player really helps him in that aspect um because he knows what it's like. He knows what it's like to go uh training camp joint practice and, you know, to have a day where you're like, "Dang, I wish I could have that back." You can't have it back. So, what do you got to do? You got to look at the next day and what are you going to do to improve? Um and he's done a great job in keeping our eyes focused on what we have ahead. >> Christian, Vrabel has talked to us sometimes about managing guys workload throughout the course of the summer and [clears throat] sometimes we haven't seen you out there. What's kept you out on the days that you haven't been full go the last couple weeks? >> Um you know, I'm a I'm a keep that between me and Vrabel. Um you know, it's not anything serious. Like it's just for me like I have a little bang here, little bang there and um just trying to trying to be smart with my body. Um you know, as I'm getting older, as I'm dealing with things off the field. Um but for me, like where whenever they want me to play, whenever they want me to line up, I'll line up and play, whether it's preseason game, whether it's not preseason game, and um yeah. >> Christian, what have you seen from Landman and Quill Jackson start to make some plays on the preseason? What have you just seen from both the rookies? >> They're amazing. Um they're wise beyond their years. They um know how to play linebacker at a good level. they're correcting the what you call the rookie mistakes, you know, and they're moving forward every single week, moving forward every single practice. So, I'm really proud of them. I'm proud of how they work. I'm proud of how they approach our meetings. I'm proud of how they watch film, how they come early. It's all things I love to see. Um and they're going to do great things in >> W- was the footing tough today at >> Uh just a little bit, just a little bit. Got to keep your feet under you, you know. Um yeah, it wasn't too bad, though. >> Did you want to go in at halftime and change the studs or whatever? >> [laughter] >> That would have been ideal. >> Appreciate you guys.

title: Mike Vrabel: "We Try to Focus on the Things That Get the Team Ready." | Patriots Press Conference
text: How are you? Hi, Karen. I'm great, thank you. >> Do you anticipate having Christian Gonzalez back in practice later tomorrow? >> Uh yeah, I think we're hopeful that that he'll be able to do some stuff. He was working um you know, before the game and trying to work through the return to play, so we'll see how he feels this morning. >> Mike, do you guys have to bring in a new punter with Braden Mann? >> Yeah, I think we will. So, we'll probably sign somebody here shortly. >> How serious is Braden? >> Serious enough that we'll probably have to sign a new punter. >> What was it like? Did it happen in the game? >> It happened in the game, yes. Yeah, I mean, I wouldn't make him go out and kick while he was injured, if that's what you're asking. But yeah, no, it it it was something that occurred during the game, which is why the quarterback had to punt. >> Mike, you've talked in the beginning of having a sense of urgency with this team. When it comes to what you were talking about the other day about depth and things like that, how do you squeeze the the talent that you have with the sense of urgency to get to where you need to be? >> Well, I mean, depth, you know, I mean, depth has to be built, you know, I mean, that's something that has to be built through um experience and, you know, making sure that the guys are in place to be uh the the first backup and those those are critical. Those are almost uh starters. You know, we know how many people are going to have to play for you throughout the season and and there can't be a a drop-off. And so, you know, that that's why we we're we're building it and that's what you have preseason for. That's what you have training camp for. That's what you have practices and joint practices is to be able to, you know, identify those players that you think um are in a position to to provide that and um that that's what we're trying to do. >> Were there clearly some tough moments in the second half? >> I think in the second half, I think there certainly were. You know, I think uh you know, some guys that the the coaches pointed out. I think Kendall obviously, uh you know, some very competitive snaps. Um you know, some guys down, you know, Clowney over, I thought played well and tried to finish and try to to use his length in pass protection. Um I think that um you know, I thought Lenny T played played well and and and factored and showed up. Um I think offensively, even just down the line, I thought Chiz did a great job of, you know, when the ball found him, making the plays, but also, you know, his ability to go and block force and and finish and, you know, Kyle Dixon hadn't been out there for a while. And so, you know, a guy that's relatively new to the receiver position, that was really cool to see him show up in some big moments. We're throwing the ball to Kyle Dixon. You know, he's a a baseball player not too long ago on fourth down and he's making a play and then he was trying to block, you know, finding the right guys to block in a run game. So, you know, those are all really really interesting things. >> Mike, specific to Christian, what will the protocol be before practice today to determine if he's ready to play or not? >> Uh we'll meet here with Jim and and myself and and see where things are at and see how he feels and see how he feels warming up. >> Have you worked through whether you whether you want the starters to play a little bit on Thursday night? >> I'm sorry, if >> Have you worked through whether you want the starters to play or >> Uh we have 2 days. You know, it's a short week, so we have 2 days and again, I have to see where we're at here coming out of the red zone today and and where we're at tomorrow, but no, I haven't made a determining factor or decision. >> Mike, I'm curious about you are embracing sports science and kind of load management cuz I think people might look at you as a former linebacker from Northeast Ohio and not think of a guy wanting to give a Morgan or Reggie a day off. Did that come from like conversations with doctors or maybe when you were a player, you thought, "Hey, if we dialed it back a little, guys might be prepared, or how did you come to that? >> No, I thought 10 straight two-a-days was a good way to prepare the football team. I I just think as the data becomes more available and and I think you have to be careful to go overboard. I mean, you want to track certain numbers and high-speed numbers and yardage and all the other stuff and and also have a pretty good gauge of I think the player and what they look like and how conditioned they are and you know, we try to set the schedule up accordingly. Some of that um kind of takes care of itself just by the way that we try to put the schedule together and just try to map it out. And then when there's a longer stretch, you may have to you know, dial back on on a you know, particular player. But I think probably just when you become a head coach, you try to focus on that things that get the team ready and what they need and what each guy needs and then you know, some more of the the GPS stuff became, you know, really popular and prevalent and you know, anything that can that can help us uh keep the players out there, uh I'm all for. >> How much is on the undrafted starters, so >> Uh I have both of them. >> Oh, okay. Um >> Stop being so nice, Sof. >> I can't. >> I know. >> Um with the linebacker position with Christian and Robert having not played in the two games, how do you evaluate the guys who have um played >> Yeah, I mean, I think K.J. has been physical, which is it is good. You know, I think he's using that as a strength. He was physical in the in the Philadelphia joint practices. Uh the young guys continue to kind of, you know, factor and then there's a lot of things that they need to learn and there's a lot of different defenses and situations and a lot of plays. There's There's of firsts uh for for Nam and and Khalil. And then certainly Riley and you know Wilson in that group too. And then Chad, you know, was you know, came in last year mid-season and and helped us and helped us in the kicking game. So, um you know, we'll continue to to see where those guys are and you know, I wouldn't anticipate seeing Khalil out there this week. You know, he's working through something and I'd say we got a pretty good list of guys. Marcus Bryant would be in that category. Uh wouldn't plan on seeing Craig Woodson out there today. X won't be out there. Xavier won't be Um Lan and Jam probably won't be out there today either. >> How much does the unusual kind of start date that you guys have play into the the decisions you're making about this final preseason? >> Um I mean, I think whether we played Sunday or Wednesday, I don't think that really would factor into it. I think it factors into just you know, are we getting the work that we need and then however, you just back it out from the normal the the start date on Wednesday you know, for example, I think the Friday before becomes a Tuesday and you know, we just kind of live in Sunday to Sunday world. So, when you play on a Wednesday, you just kind of adjust everything back from there. >> Like uh maybe the starters are not playing the Thursday How can uh how do you use this as a season preseason game uh to prepare your coaching staff to get ready for the regular season or do you think they need that kind of accommodation? >> That our coaches do? >> Coaches. >> Yeah, I haven't The coaches have been involved in both of the preseason games um I think the communication's been good. The headset's been good, but I don't think who As long as we have 11 guys out there, the coaches are going to be working through um their communication and how we need to fix things and then whether I'm telling Josh, "Hey, we got four downs." or you know, what the line is that we're going to kick or hey, this is the 2-minute situation. So, it was good that we had a lot of those situations come up uh Saturday. >> What do you anticipate your guys going to do? >> Jauan Williams said that he had a chance to call a play in the second half yesterday. Just what prompted you to give him that opportunity? >> Well, I just appreciate the the program that we have with the Bill Bill Walsh internship program. I think Clint McMillan does a a fantastic job of identifying a a great group of qualified coaches that then we we meet with and and and and and invite. they commit a lot to our program and to our players. And so, you know, I had Abdulla call a you know, third down pressure. I told him it better be a pressure and it worked. And we got off the field. Jauan called a defense. Uh Brad Davis called a run. It We didn't gain many yards. He said the back made a bad cut. and then Jauan uh called a pass. So, I again, I just uh feel like I was appreciated what they did and uh thought it thought I'd give them an opportunity to to pick a play that they wanted to call throughout the game. >> The preseason sort of has been a hot topic of its value and I think in the last you had Terrell call >> Terrell was the head coach. He acted as the head coach for the 3 days prior to the game because um thought that was an earned opportunity for him. Uh something that I that I want to continue to do once we we get established here. I I didn't want to cut you off, but I can go back and explain what I did. And he handled the team meetings for the 2 days prior to the to the game. He uh he he met with the officials. He worked with the challenges. He talked to the coaches. He handled the media the post game and thought that that was you know we talk about trying to grow coaches I try to think of ways to do it. And I thought that that was a good one. >> What does that mean to you guys? >> question would basically be the preseason has been such a hot topic. People have said that it should be eliminated. You just told us about the joint practices instead. Do you view this aspect of giving like the coaches that type of elevated opportunity as a potential like under seen value in keeping the preseason or is >> I think that's part of it. I think that that's certainly part of it. And these weren't like plays just off the top of their head. They were actually on the game plan that they looked at and whether Zach called it or or Josh called it they they were on the call sheet. So I I just think trying to be creative and find ways to develop everybody that we have when we identify you know the people that we have here that can continue to grow and do a good job. I think it's uh it's always a good thing. So whenever the the game is the situation you know preseason you know regular season we just have to make sure that we have a plan and that you know we're trying to do everything that we can to to get the most out of those games and and certainly win them and I think that that was clearly obvious and evident from the way that our guys played certainly in the second half on Saturday. I thought guys they really responded. >> Do you anticipate the team being active in either the trade market or waiver wire to fill in some areas of depth? >> I mean just like we do always every year. You know I mean that that won't change. We we did that last year. We we tried to you know again when you're claiming 31st and you're claiming fourth there's a big difference. >> Like when you mentioned the other night that you feel like you're a very deep team right now. Is there a message trying to be sent there by you in that situation? >> No, I got to ask this this morning. That we're we're all on the same page. Like the there's no front office, there's no back office, there's the Patriots. There's there's me, there's Elliot, there's Ryan, there's Stretch. I told you those are the people that you know, we rely on to to make uh decisions. So, there there is uh no message and I it just was Mike asked me, I think, about the starters playing I mean we whatever, you know, we we lost a couple guys that are aren't going to be with us. So, you you can only play that for so long. You can only do that for so long and we we're going to need to prepare the football team and be smart and make sure that they're we're as ready to go as we possibly can. and the depth was about building the depth. It was about taking the guys that we have and building them and then identifying if there's other people that we can add to the roster. You know, we'll continually try to do that. >> Mike, I know he's >> Do you get more value out of a joint practice versus preseason games and where the injury risk falls between the >> I you know, I mean, I don't I know the data will tell you one thing, uh but there were some really good opportunities and moments uh during Saturday night's game that we wouldn't be able to replicate uh with the Eagles. fourth-and-one situations, just the live tackling, players you know, the ability to um to adjust quickly, our ability to run the football, to finish runs, to to push the piles, there's a there's a lot of benefits uh to that game that I saw on Saturday. >> Mike, I know he's going to return to play and that's the focus for Christian right now. I'm just curious, given the time he's missed, about how many padded practices he's participated in, do you have any concern at this stage about his potential readiness for week one? >> I'm going to focus on today. I'm not ready to talk about week one. I hope you know, we have to do everything we can to get guys ready. Each Each guy has to be ready individually and then I'll have to find a way to make sure that the the football team is ready and that we're conditioned and you know, ready to go. >> Next two or three final questions. >> For Gill, what was it seemed like in the past two preseason games his recovery ability has really stood out, the ability to maybe stay on blocks even if it hasn't been perfect. Have you seen it the same way and what are some things he can do to make sure he wins earlier in the rep to avoid having to recover? >> Yeah, I mean I don't think you have to be, you know, you would you don't want to rely on being able to recover too much. You know, I think just you know, being square, throwing your hands, you know, playing with a good base, you know, not get overextended is things that can help you. >> Okay, Mark, you're going to get a chance to have Hunter try out there? >> Uh maybe. Maybe his plus 50 has to improve and then we need some more hang time and not kick it right down the middle and think, you know, at least they bounced and then it went forward, so that was positive. >> Sorry, did you know he could do that? Did he raise his hand at the time like other times? >> No, I just know that what who can punt. I wasn't going to go to to to Mets or one of the offensive linemen. I just I know that every quarterback's probably been a punter and they were the shortstop on the baseball team and they were the shooting guard on the on the basketball team. It's kind of what happens, you know what I mean? And it wasn't going to be Drake and it it Burn was the obvious choice that anyone of you would have would have went to. >> Thanks.

title: One Step Closer: 'The Build' Episode 3 – Inside 49ers Training Camp
text: 90 guys going for 53 spots in a matter of weeks. >> Now it ramps up this week. Another joint practice with the Chargers and then preseason [music] game number two at Sofi Stadium. >> LA Takeover. >> Well, the Niners, we travel in packs. >> That's right. >> There going to be more red jerseys than you see blue jerseys. >> We get to take the flag. >> Yeah, you dang right. Take as many as you can. [music] It's special for me because I just remember when I was that age playing football, just enjoying it. >> You spend your whole life trying to prove if you belong and then one day you're one of the all-time greats. >> This guy's still playing at a high level. He's an amazing leader. So excited for his presence, not only in the locker room, but out on the field. >> Kyle is going to have this team formidable and competing at a high level. >> Hey, this is just a sneak peek, bro. title: Robert Saleh on Cam Ward, Carnell Tate & Roster Cuts | Press Conference
text: Uh Cam said last night he doesn't think the offense is that far off right now timing and things like that. Uh, so there's a lot of different things that are happening. I I can tell you more often than not, the quarterback knows where the uh defenders are with the offensive players backs turn to the defense, if I'm making sense to you. And throughout the league, you'll see it. Quarterbacks will put the ball in places that they're trying to get the the the the ball carrier to to be able to stay away from defenders.
